| `ConditionalExpression` | added | 9 | ConditionalExpression[expr, cond]: expr when cond is True, Undefined when cond is False, nested conditions combine with And (ConditionalExpression[ConditionalExpression[x, a], b] = ConditionalExpression[x, a && b]), otherwise unevaluated (returned by Integrate, Sum, Solve and the Fourier coefficient functions for parameter conditions; arithmetic on ConditionalExpression objects is not propagated).  Single implementation shared by batches 4 and 6. |
| `D` | fixed | 48 | batch 4: D[f, x, y, ...], D[f, {x, n}], D[f, {{x1, x2, ...}}] (gradient) and {{...}, n} (arrays of higher derivatives), threads over lists and equations (implicit differentiation D[x^2 + y[x]^2 == 1, x]), NonConstants -> {y}, derivatives with respect to f[x]; chain rule results are Wolfram Derivative forms (D[f[g[x]], x] -> f'[g[x]] g'[x]; previously D[f[g[x]], g[x]] g'[x]); symbolic orders stay unevaluated; D[f] with no variable returns f |
| `DSolve` | fixed | 26 | batch 4: every solution returned by DSolve (ODEs and ODE systems in one variable, initial conditions, y[x] or y forms) is now substituted back into the equations and checked (symbolically, else numerically at sample points); PDEs raise. Free constants may be numbered differently from Wolfram (the solution family is the same) |
| `DSolveValue` | added | 4 | DSolveValue[eqns, y[x], x] gives the solution value, DSolveValue[eqns, y, x] a pure function, DSolveValue[eqns, expr, x] the value of expr; several solutions give a list; checked like DSolve |
| `Derivative` | added | 4 | Derivative[n1, n2, ...][f] for pure functions and built-in mathematical functions gives a pure function (Derivative[1][Sin] -> Cos[#1] &, Derivative[2][#^3 &] -> 6 #1 &); Derivative[n...][f][x...] evaluates for known f (Sin'[x] -> Cos[x], previously unevaluated) and stays symbolic for undefined f (f'[x], Derivative[1, 0][f][x, y]); Derivative[0][f] -> f |
| `DiracDelta` | added | 8 | Wolfram DiracDelta[x1, ...]: 0 when any argument is a nonzero real number, unevaluated otherwise (DiracDelta[0] stays); complex numeric arguments raise; integrates and transforms through SymPy (Integrate[f[x] DiracDelta[x - a], {x, -Infinity, Infinity}] -> f[a]); D[HeavisideTheta[x], x] -> DiracDelta[x] |
| `Dt` | added | 9 | total derivatives: Dt[f, x] treats every other symbol as a function of x (Dt[x^2 y, x] -> 2 x y + x^2 Dt[y, x]), Dt[f, {x, n}], Dt[f] is the total differential (Dt[x y] -> y Dt[x] + x Dt[y]); Constants -> {a, ...}; Dt[y, x] for an independent symbol y stays unevaluated; numeric constants (Pi, E, ...) have derivative 0 |
| `FourierCoefficient` | added | 7 | FourierCoefficient[f, t, n] = 1/(2π) ∫_{-π}^{π} f e^(-int) dt (Wolfram default FourierParameters {1, 1}; other parameters raise); integer or symbolic n (symbolic n is integer: a separate n == 0 value appears as Piecewise[{{c0, n == 0}}, g[n]]); the general term is checked against direct integrals at n = ±1, ±2, 3, 5 |
| `FourierCosCoefficient` | added | 3 | FourierCosCoefficient[f, t, n] = 2/π ∫_0^π f cos(nt) dt, with 1/π ∫_0^π f dt for n = 0 (Wolfram); symbolic n checked against direct integrals |
| `FourierCosSeries` | added | 3 | FourierCosSeries[f, t, k] = Σ_{n=0}^{k} FourierCosCoefficient[f, t, n] Cos[n t] (even extension of f on [0, π]) |
| `FourierSeries` | added | 3 | FourierSeries[f, t, k] = Σ_{n=-k}^{k} FourierCoefficient[f, t, n] E^(I n t) (Wolfram default parameters; others raise) |
| `FourierSinCoefficient` | added | 3 | FourierSinCoefficient[f, t, n] = 2/π ∫_0^π f sin(nt) dt (Wolfram); symbolic n checked against direct integrals |
| `FourierSinSeries` | added | 3 | FourierSinSeries[f, t, k] = Σ_{n=1}^{k} FourierSinCoefficient[f, t, n] Sin[n t] (odd extension of f on [0, π]) |
| `FourierTrigSeries` | added | 3 | FourierTrigSeries[f, t, k] = a0 + Σ_{n=1}^{k} (a_n Cos[n t] + b_n Sin[n t]) with a0 = 1/(2π)∫f, a_n = 1/π ∫_{-π}^{π} f cos(nt), b_n = 1/π ∫_{-π}^{π} f sin(nt) (Wolfram default parameters) |
| `HeavisideTheta` | added | 8 | Wolfram HeavisideTheta[x1, ...]: 1 when every argument is positive, 0 when any is negative, unevaluated at 0 (unlike UnitStep[0] = 1 and SymPy's Heaviside(0) = 1/2); D gives DiracDelta |
| `ImplicitD` | added | 5 | ImplicitD[f == g, y, x] = dy/dx for y defined implicitly (ImplicitD[x^2 + y^2 == 1, y, x] -> -x/y), ImplicitD[eqn, y, {x, n}] higher derivatives (expressed in x and y), ImplicitD[{eqns}, {y1, y2}, x] for systems |
| `Integrate` | fixed | 60 | batch 4: indefinite integrals (verified by differentiating back), definite, improper and multiple integrals (the last specification is innermost); options Assumptions, GenerateConditions (Automatic/True give ConditionalExpression[value, cond] when the result needs a parameter condition, e.g. Integrate[x^a, {x, 0, 1}] -> ConditionalExpression[1/(1 + a), Re[a] > -1]; False gives the generic value) and PrincipalValue -> True (Cauchy principal value, Integrate[1/x, {x, -1, 2}, PrincipalValue -> True] -> Log[2]); SymPy convergence conditions are rewritten in Wolfram form (Abs[Arg[a]] < Pi/2 -> Re[a] > 0); integrals that diverge to +-Infinity give that limit, indeterminate (oscillating/cancelling) ones raise; HeavisideTheta and DiracDelta integrands are supported; integrals SymPy cannot do stay unevaluated |
| `InverseSeries` | added | 3 | InverseSeries[s] / InverseSeries[s, y] for a power series s = a1 x + a2 x^2 + ... + O[x]^n about 0 with a1 != 0: the series of the inverse function to the same order (InverseSeries[Series[Sin[x], {x, 0, 5}]] -> x + x^3/6 + 3 x^5/40 + O[x]^6); the result is checked by composing back |
| `Limit` | fixed | 19 | batch 4: Limit[f, x -> a] (two-sided: Indeterminate when the one-sided limits differ), Direction -> "FromAbove" / "FromBelow" / -1 / 1 / "TwoSided", Assumptions, limits at +-Infinity, lists of functions, and multivariate limits Limit[f, {x, y} -> {a, b}] (continuity after cancellation, Indeterminate when two paths disagree, otherwise a clear error); oscillating limits raise (use MaxLimit/MinLimit); legacy rejected every option |
| `MaxLimit` | added | 4 | upper limit (limsup) MaxLimit[f, x -> a] with Direction and Assumptions: the larger one-sided limit, or A + \|B\| for f = A + B Sin[g] / A + B Cos[g] with g -> +-Infinity (MaxLimit[Sin[1/x], x -> 0] -> 1); other oscillating functions raise |
| `MinLimit` | added | 3 | lower limit (liminf) MinLimit[f, x -> a]; see MaxLimit (MinLimit[Sign[x], x -> 0] -> -1) |
| `Normal` | fixed | 157 | batch 4 adds: Normal[series] drops every O term structurally (also the inner ones of multivariate series) and evaluates the remaining polynomial; associations and other heads as before (batch 1) |
| `O` | added | 3 | order term O[x]^n / O[x - x0]^n / O[1/x]^n of Series results (stays symbolic); Normal removes it; SeriesCoefficient, InverseSeries and ComposeSeries read it |
| `Product` | fixed | 8 | batch 4: as Sum (finite, symbolic and infinite products via SymPy; parametric products give the generic value, ConditionalExpression with GenerateConditions -> True) |
| `RSolve` | fixed | 10 | batch 4: RSolve[eqns, a[n], n] -> {{a[n] -> ...}} and RSolve[eqns, a, n] -> {{a -> Function[{n}, ...]}}; linear recurrences with constant or polynomial coefficients and initial conditions (SymPy rsolve); every solution is substituted back into the recurrence and the initial conditions; free constants are C[1], C[2], ...; systems raise |
| `RSolveValue` | added | 4 | RSolveValue[eqns, a[n], n] gives the solution value, RSolveValue[eqns, a, n] a pure function, RSolveValue[eqns, expr, n] the value of expr (e.g. a[10]); checked like RSolve |
| `Series` | fixed | 28 | batch 4: Series[f, {x, x0, n}] with Laurent and Puiseux terms, expansions at +-Infinity in powers of 1/x (O[1/x]^(n+1)), the O term always present (Series[1/x, {x, 0, 2}] -> 1/x + O[x]^3; previously dropped), expansions about x0 grouped in powers of (x - x0) (O[x - x0]^k); several variables Series[f, {x, x0, nx}, {y, y0, ny}] expand in x with coefficients that are series in y; threads over lists; functions SymPy cannot expand raise |
| `SeriesCoefficient` | added | 9 | SeriesCoefficient[f, {x, x0, n}] (negative n for Laurent series, x0 may be Infinity: coefficient of (1/x)^n), several variables {x, x0, nx}, {y, y0, ny}, and SeriesCoefficient[series, n]; a symbolic n gives Piecewise[{{general term, n >= 0}}, 0] when SymPy finds a formal power series (checked against 10 Taylor coefficients); a coefficient beyond a given series' order is Indeterminate |
| `Sum` | fixed | 24 | batch 4: as before ({i, n}, {i, a, b}, {i, a, b, di}, {i, {values}}, several iterators, first outermost; divergent sums to +-Infinity give that limit, other non-convergent sums stay unevaluated), plus parametric series that SymPy sums under a convergence condition: Wolfram's generic value by default (Sum[x^k, {k, 0, Infinity}] -> 1/(1 - x); previously a recursion error) and ConditionalExpression[value, cond] with GenerateConditions -> True |
| `SumConvergence` | added | 7 | SumConvergence[f, n]: True/False for the convergence of Sum[f, {n, k, Infinity}] (SymPy's ratio, root, integral, comparison, alternating-series tests); the p-series family 1/n^p and n^p r^n with a parameter gives the Wolfram condition (Re[p] > 1, Abs[r] < 1); undecided cases stay unevaluated |

### calculus extras (W06)

| Function | Status | Cases | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Antihermitian` | added | 3 | Antihermitian[{s1, s2}]: sign change under conjugate transposition; inert symmetry specification used by TensorSymmetry, ArraySymbol, MatrixSymbol, Matrices and Arrays (Symmetric/Antisymmetric/ZeroSymmetric[All]: every slot); malformed slot lists raise |
| `Antisymmetric` | added | 12 | Antisymmetric[{s1, ..., sn}]: sign change under odd permutations; inert symmetry specification used by TensorSymmetry, ArraySymbol, MatrixSymbol, Matrices and Arrays (Symmetric/Antisymmetric/ZeroSymmetric[All]: every slot); malformed slot lists raise |
| `ArrayExpand` | added | 4 | ArrayExpand[expr]: expands symbolic-array expressions built from MatrixSymbol/VectorSymbol/ArraySymbol (rank <= 2) and Symbolic*Array with Plus, Times, Dot, Transpose, Inverse, MatrixPower, Tr, Det: distributes Dot over Plus, Transpose[a.b] -> Transpose[b].Transpose[a], Transpose[a + b] -> ..., Inverse[a.b] -> Inverse[b].Inverse[a] (SymPy matrix expressions); explicit arrays are expanded elementwise; anything else raises |
| `ArraySimplify` | added | 7 | ArraySimplify[expr]: simplifies symbolic-array expressions (Transpose[Transpose[a]] -> a, a.Inverse[a] -> identity, a.SymbolicIdentityArray[{n}] -> a, a.SymbolicZerosArray -> zeros, Transpose[a] -> a for MatrixSymbol[.., Symmetric[{1, 2}]] and -a for Antisymmetric) via SymPy matrix expressions; explicit arrays are simplified elementwise |
| `ArraySymbol` | added | 4 | ArraySymbol["A", dims] / [.., dom] / [.., dom, sym]: a symbolic array (inert); rank-1 and rank-2 ArraySymbols take part in ArrayExpand / ArraySimplify like VectorSymbol / MatrixSymbol |
| `Arrays` | added | 3 | Arrays[{d1, ..., dk}] / Arrays[dims, dom] / Arrays[dims, dom, sym]: the domain of arrays of the given dimensions; inert; malformed specifications raise |
| `Asymptotic` | added | 12 | Asymptotic[f, x -> x0]: the leading term of the asymptotic expansion (verified: f/term -> 1); Asymptotic[f, {x, x0, n}]: the expansion to order n; SeriesTermGoal -> k: the first k terms (Taylor, Laurent or Puiseux at finite x0; at Infinity down to x^-n, with exponential/power prefactors and Stirling-type expansions of Gamma, Factorial, Binomial, HarmonicNumber via LogGamma); unexpandable input raises |
| `AsymptoticDSolveValue` | added | 4 | AsymptoticDSolveValue[{ode, ics}, y[x], {x, x0, n} \| x -> x0]: the power-series solution of a (linear or nonlinear) ODE at an ordinary point x0 (Taylor coefficients by repeated differentiation of the solved equation; missing initial values become C[1], C[2], ...); AsymptoticDSolveValue[{ode, ics}, y[x], x, {e, 0, n}]: regular perturbation expansion in a parameter (each order solved with DSolve, residual checked); singular points, singular perturbations and systems raise |
| `AsymptoticEqual` | added | 3 | AsymptoticEqual[f, g, x -> x0]: True when f = Theta(g): \|f/g\| bounded above and away from 0 as x -> x0 (decided by the limit of \|f/g\|; oscillating ratios with finite bounds are decided where the bounds suffice), False otherwise; unevaluated when the limit cannot be decided or depends on parameters |
| `AsymptoticEquivalent` | added | 3 | AsymptoticEquivalent[f, g, x -> x0]: True when f ~ g: f/g -> 1 as x -> x0 (decided by the limit of \|f/g\|; oscillating ratios with finite bounds are decided where the bounds suffice), False otherwise; unevaluated when the limit cannot be decided or depends on parameters |
| `AsymptoticExpectation` | added | 3 | AsymptoticExpectation[expr, x \[Distributed] dist, a -> a0 \| {a, a0, n}]: the asymptotic expansion in a parameter of the exact Expectation (computed by Expectation, then expanded); raises when the expectation has no closed form |
| `AsymptoticGreater` | added | 3 | AsymptoticGreater[f, g, x -> x0]: True when f = omega(g): \|f/g\| -> Infinity as x -> x0 (decided by the limit of \|f/g\|; oscillating ratios with finite bounds are decided where the bounds suffice), False otherwise; unevaluated when the limit cannot be decided or depends on parameters |
| `AsymptoticGreaterEqual` | added | 3 | AsymptoticGreaterEqual[f, g, x -> x0]: True when f = Omega(g): \|f/g\| bounded away from 0 as x -> x0 (decided by the limit of \|f/g\|; oscillating ratios with finite bounds are decided where the bounds suffice), False otherwise; unevaluated when the limit cannot be decided or depends on parameters |
| `AsymptoticIntegrate` | added | 3 | AsymptoticIntegrate[f, x, x -> x0 \| {x, x0, n}]: asymptotic expansion of an antiderivative (SymPy's antiderivative checked by differentiation, else term-wise integration of the expansion of f, constant 0); AsymptoticIntegrate[f, {t, a, b}, {p, p0, n}]: expansion of a parametric integral (exact integral checked numerically, else term-wise integration of the expansion in p (finite p0, each term finite; the result is checked against numerical quadrature near p0)); divergent term-wise integrals raise |
| `AsymptoticLess` | added | 3 | AsymptoticLess[f, g, x -> x0]: True when f = o(g): f/g -> 0 as x -> x0 (decided by the limit of \|f/g\|; oscillating ratios with finite bounds are decided where the bounds suffice), False otherwise; unevaluated when the limit cannot be decided or depends on parameters |
| `AsymptoticLessEqual` | added | 3 | AsymptoticLessEqual[f, g, x -> x0]: True when f = O(g): \|f/g\| bounded as x -> x0 (decided by the limit of \|f/g\|; oscillating ratios with finite bounds are decided where the bounds suffice), False otherwise; unevaluated when the limit cannot be decided or depends on parameters |
| `AsymptoticProbability` | added | 3 | AsymptoticProbability[pred, x \[Distributed] dist, a -> a0 \| {a, a0, n}]: the asymptotic expansion in a parameter of the exact probability (Probability, or 1 - CDF / CDF for one-sided bounds of continuous distributions); e.g. the Gaussian tail Erfc[a/Sqrt[2]]/2 ~ E^(-a^2/2)/(a Sqrt[2 Pi]); no closed form -> error |
| `AsymptoticProduct` | added | 3 | AsymptoticProduct[f, {k, a, n}, n -> Infinity \| {n, Infinity, m}], AsymptoticProduct[f, {k, a, Infinity}, {p, p0, m}] and the indefinite AsymptoticProduct[f, k, {k, Infinity, m}] (= Product over 1..k-1): from SymPy's closed form (Gamma / rising factorials, checked numerically) expanded with Stirling's series (Product[k, {k, 2, n}] ~ Sqrt[2 Pi] n^(n + 1/2) E^-n); no closed form -> error |
| `AsymptoticRSolveValue` | added | 3 | AsymptoticRSolveValue[{eqn, ics}, y[n], n -> Infinity \| {n, Infinity, m}]: asymptotics of the solution of a recurrence: first-order linear homogeneous recurrences are solved as C[1] times a closed-form product (Gamma functions, verified); others via RSolveValue (verified by substitution); each free constant's part is expanded separately (Stirling / exponential scales; Fibonacci -> GoldenRatio^n/Sqrt[5]); parameter (perturbation) forms and recurrences without a verified closed form raise |
| `AsymptoticSolve` | added | 4 | AsymptoticSolve[eqn, {y, y0}, {x, x0, n}]: the branch of y(x) through (x0, y0) as a Taylor series (implicit function theorem, requires D[eqn, y] != 0 there; Newton iteration on truncated series, residual checked); AsymptoticSolve[eqn, y \| {y}, {x, x0, n} \| x -> x0]: every branch, from SymPy's closed-form roots expanded in Puiseux series; systems raise |
| `AsymptoticSum` | added | 5 | AsymptoticSum[f, {k, a, n}, n -> Infinity \| {n, Infinity, m}]: asymptotics of a partial sum, AsymptoticSum[f, {k, a, Infinity}, {p, p0, m}]: expansion of a parametric infinite sum, AsymptoticSum[f, k, {k, Infinity, m}]: the indefinite sum (the tail convention F(Infinity) = 0 for convergent sums, else Sum over 0..k-1); computed from SymPy's closed form (checked numerically against direct summation) with Euler-Maclaurin expansions of Hurwitz zeta / generalized harmonic numbers; no closed form -> error |
| `C` | added | 4 | C[i] is the i-th constant of integration generated by DSolve, RSolve, AsymptoticDSolveValue and GreenFunction-related solvers (inert; C[i] + C[i] = 2 C[i]) |
| `CaputoD` | added | 8 | CaputoD[f, {x, alpha}]: the Caputo differintegral I^(m-alpha) D^m f (m = Ceiling[alpha]) with lower terminal 0; powers in closed form (constants and x^k with k < alpha give 0; symbolic alpha gives a Piecewise for polynomial terms); other f with numeric alpha via the defining integral, checked against quadrature; threads over lists |
| `Casoratian` | added | 4 | Casoratian[{y1, ..., yk}, n] = Det[{y_j[n + i]}] (i = 0..k-1), simplified; Casoratian[..., n, True] gives the matrix; the equation form Casoratian[eqn, y, n] raises (its normalisation constant is not determined by the equation) |
| `ContourIntegrate` | added | 13 | ContourIntegrate[f, z ∈ cont]: complex contour integral; closed contours (Circle, Disk, Rectangle, Triangle, Polygon boundaries, counterclockwise) of meromorphic f by the residue theorem (poles found exactly); open contours (Line, HalfLine, InfiniteLine, arcs, ParametricRegion[{x[t], y[t]}, ...]) by an antiderivative or direct parametrised integration; every result is checked against numerical quadrature (parameters sampled); poles on the contour and symbolic pole locations raise |
| `CoordinateTransform` | added | 5 | CoordinateTransform["chart1" -> "chart2", pt]: the coordinates of pt in chart2 (charts Cartesian, Polar (n-dimensional hyperspherical), Spherical, Cylindrical; {"chart", n} gives the dimension); threads over a list of points |
| `DEigensystem` | added | 3 | DEigensystem[{L[u[x]], bcs}, u[x], {x, a, b}, n]: {eigenvalues, eigenfunctions} (unnormalised, e.g. Sin[k x]) for the same class of problems as DEigenvalues |
| `DEigenvalues` | added | 3 | DEigenvalues[{L[u[x]], bcs}, u[x], {x, a, b}, n]: the n smallest-magnitude eigenvalues of L u == lambda u for constant-coefficient second-order operators on an interval with Dirichlet (DirichletCondition or u[a] == 0) or Neumann (u'[a] == 0, NeumannValue[0, ...], the default) ends, in closed form; other regions, variable coefficients and Robin/periodic conditions raise |
| `DFixedPoints` | added | 3 | DFixedPoints[eqns, x[t] \| {x1, ...}, t]: the equilibria of an autonomous ODE system, as points of the first-order state (x, x', ..., x^(k-1)) for higher-order equations; sorted; raises for continua |

| `FindSequenceFunction` | added | 5 | FindSequenceFunction[{a1, a2, ...}, n] (or {{n1, a1}, ...}): rational functions of n, hypergeometric terms (rational successive ratios: products, factorials, powers), constant-coefficient linear recurrences (solved exactly; Fibonacci/LucasL recognised) and sums of hypergeometric differences, each fitted exactly with at least two confirming terms; FindSequenceFunction[list] gives a pure function; stays unevaluated when nothing is found |
| `FractionalD` | added | 10 | FractionalD[f, {x, alpha}]: the Riemann-Liouville differintegral with lower terminal 0; sums of powers c x^p (p > -1) in closed form for any (also symbolic) alpha, Gamma(p+1)/Gamma(p+1-alpha) x^(p-alpha); integer alpha gives D or repeated integrals; other f with numeric alpha via the defining integral (D^m I^(m-alpha) f), checked against quadrature; threads over lists |

| `FromPolarCoordinates` | added | 4 | FromPolarCoordinates[{r, t}] = {r Cos[t], r Sin[t]}; {r, t1, ..., t(n-1)} -> {r Cos[t1], r Sin[t1] Cos[t2], ..., r Sin[t1] ... Sin[t(n-1)]}; threads over a list of points |

| `GreenFunction` | added | 4 | GreenFunction[{L[u[x]], bcs}, u[x] \| u, {x, a, b}, y]: the Green's function of a linear ODE of any order with homogeneous two-point or initial conditions (homogeneous solutions by DSolve; continuity of the first n-2 derivatives and the jump 1/c_n(y) of the (n-1)th), as HeavisideTheta pieces; u gives Function[{x, y}, ...]; PDEs and problems without a unique Green's function raise |

| `HodgeDual` | promoted | 4 | HodgeDual[t]: the Hodge dual of an explicit array whose slots all have dimension n: (1/k!) LeviCivita_{i1..ik j1..j(n-k)} t_{i1..ik} (t is antisymmetrized in effect); HodgeDual[{a, b, c}] = {{0, c, -b}, {-c, 0, a}, {b, -a, 0}}; HodgeDual[x, n] for a scalar is x LeviCivitaTensor[n]; HodgeDual[t, n, slots] dualizes the given slots (the others become the last slots of the result); previously quarantined |

| `IntegrateChangeVariables` | added | 9 | IntegrateChangeVariables[Inactive[Integrate][f, x \| {x, a, b}], u, u == phi[x] \| x == psi[u]]: integration by substitution, f(psi(u)) psi'(u), returned as Inactive[Integrate][...]; for definite integrals the inverse branch mapping [ua, ub] onto [a, b] is chosen and the result is checked by quadrature; multiple integrals, regions and named coordinate charts raise |
| `InterpolatingPolynomial` | added | 8 | InterpolatingPolynomial[{f1, f2, ...}, x] (nodes 1, 2, ...), [{{x1, f1}, ...}, x] and Hermite data {{x1, f1, df1, ...}, ...} or {{x1, {f1, df1, ...}}, ...}: the lowest-degree interpolating polynomial in Newton/Horner form by (confluent) divided differences; symbolic nodes and values allowed; multidimensional data and the Modulus option raise |
| `InterpolationOrder` | added | 6 | option of Interpolation, ListInterpolation and FunctionInterpolation: the polynomial order of the interpolation (default 3) |
| `InterpolationPoints` | added | 3 | option of FunctionInterpolation: the number of sample points (default 31, refined until the interpolant agrees with the function at the midpoints) |

| `LyapunovSolve` | added | 5 | LyapunovSolve[a, c]: a.x + x.a^H == c; [a, b, c]: a.x + x.b == c; [{a, d}, c]: a.x.d^H + d.x.a^H == c; [{a, d}, {b, e}, c]: a.x.e + d.x.b == c; exact (Kronecker linear system) or numerical for inexact input; raises when the solution is not unique |
| `Matrices` | added | 5 | Matrices[{m, n}] / Matrices[{m, n}, dom] / Matrices[{m, n}, dom, sym]: the domain of m x n matrices (sym a Symmetric/Antisymmetric/Hermitian/... specification); inert; malformed specifications raise |
| `MatrixSymbol` | added | 13 | MatrixSymbol["A", {m, n}] / [.., dom] / [.., dom, sym]: a symbolic m x n matrix (inert); ArrayExpand / ArraySimplify treat it as a SymPy MatrixSymbol (symmetry Symmetric[{1, 2}] makes Transpose[A] = A) |
| `NCaputoD` | added | 4 | NCaputoD[f, {x, alpha}, x0]: numerical Caputo differintegral at x0 > 0 (tanh-sinh quadrature of the defining integral of f^(m)) |
| `NContourIntegrate` | added | 3 | NContourIntegrate[f, z ∈ cont]: numerical contour integral along the contours supported by ContourIntegrate (Line, HalfLine, InfiniteLine, Circle, arcs, Disk/Rectangle/Triangle/Polygon boundaries counterclockwise, ParametricRegion) |
| `NFractionalD` | added | 6 | NFractionalD[f, {x, alpha}, x0]: numerical Riemann-Liouville differintegral at x0 > 0 (Caputo integral of f^(m) by tanh-sinh quadrature plus the initial-value terms, or numerical differentiation of the fractional integral when f^(k)(0) is singular) |
| `NLineIntegrate` | added | 3 | NLineIntegrate[f \| {p, q, ...}, {x, ...} ∈ curve]: numerical scalar or vector line integral over the curves supported by LineIntegrate (adaptive Gauss-Legendre/tanh-sinh quadrature) |

| `RFixedPoints` | added | 3 | RFixedPoints[eqns, a[n] \| {a1, ...}, n]: the fixed points of an autonomous recurrence system (all shifts equal), as points of the state (a[n], ..., a[n + k - 1]); sorted; raises for continua |
| `RStabilityConditions` | added | 3 | RStabilityConditions[eqns, a, n] (optionally with points): {{point, condition}, ...} for asymptotic stability of the fixed points from the linearisation (all eigenvalues inside the unit circle; a single real parameter gives an interval such as -1 < a < 1, otherwise Abs[l] < 1 conditions) |
| `ResidueSum` | added | 19 | ResidueSum[f, z]: the sum of the residues at all finite poles (rational f: -Res at infinity; entire f: 0; other functions with infinitely many poles raise); ResidueSum[{f, cons}, z]: the residues at the poles satisfying cons (bounded constraints Abs[z - c] < r, or any constraint for rational f), with poles found exactly (polynomial roots, periodic families enumerated, Gamma poles); non-meromorphic functions, poles on the constraint boundary and symbolic pole locations raise |
| `RiccatiSolve` | added | 3 | RiccatiSolve[{a, b}, {q, r}] (or {q, r, p}): the stabilising solution of the continuous algebraic Riccati equation; exact via the stable invariant subspace of the Hamiltonian matrix (verified by substitution) for exact input, SciPy's solve_continuous_are for inexact input; unevaluated when no exact solution is found |
| `SeriesTermGoal` | added | 12 | option of Asymptotic and the Asymptotic* functions: the number of (non-zero) terms of the asymptotic approximation to return for x -> x0 specifications (the expansion order is raised until that many terms appear, then the most dominant are kept; default Automatic: the leading term) |
| `SurfaceIntegrate` | added | 12 | SurfaceIntegrate[f, {x, y, z} ∈ surface] (scalar, f dS) and SurfaceIntegrate[{p, q, r}, ...] (flux F.n dS) over Sphere, Ball (its boundary), Cuboid and Cube (outward normals), Triangle (scalar only) and two-parameter ParametricRegion (normal r_u x r_v); in the plane, boundaries of Disk/Circle/Rectangle/Triangle/Polygon (outward normal) and parametric curves; results checked by numerical quadrature |
| `SymbolicDeltaProductArray` | added | 3 | SymbolicDeltaProductArray[dims, {{s1, t1}, ...}]: the array whose entries are the product of KroneckerDelta[i_s, i_t] over the given slot pairs (pairs disjoint, slots in range); Normal gives the dense array |
| `SymbolicIdentityArray` | added | 5 | SymbolicIdentityArray[{n1, ..., nk}]: the identity array of dimensions {n1, ..., nk, n1, ..., nk} (entries KroneckerDelta[i1, j1] ... KroneckerDelta[ik, jk]); SymbolicIdentityArray[{n}] is the n x n identity matrix; Normal gives the dense array; A.SymbolicIdentityArray[{n}] simplifies to A |
| `SymbolicOnesArray` | added | 3 | SymbolicOnesArray[{d1, ...}]: a symbolic all-ones array (inert); Normal gives the dense array for integer dimensions |
| `SymbolicZerosArray` | added | 4 | SymbolicZerosArray[{d1, ...}]: a symbolic all-zero array (inert); Normal gives the dense array for integer dimensions; ArrayExpand/ArraySimplify use A.0 = 0, A + 0 = A |
| `Symmetric` | added | 17 | Symmetric[{s1, ..., sn}]: symmetry under any permutation of the slots; inert symmetry specification used by TensorSymmetry, ArraySymbol, MatrixSymbol, Matrices and Arrays (Symmetric/Antisymmetric/ZeroSymmetric[All]: every slot); malformed slot lists raise |
| `TargetStructure` | added | 7 | option of symbolic-array functions (Normal of SymbolicIdentityArray etc.): "Dense" (default) gives a dense list; other structures raise |
| `TensorExpand` | added | 3 | TensorExpand[expr]: distributes TensorProduct, TensorWedge and Dot over Plus and pulls numeric factors out of them (multilinearity), recursively; symbolic factors are treated as tensors (numeric coefficients only are scalars), so the result is valid for any ranks |
| `TensorReduce` | added | 4 | TensorReduce[expr]: canonical form of tensor polynomials: TensorExpand, then TensorWedge factors of known rank (VectorSymbol, MatrixSymbol, ArraySymbol) are sorted with the Koszul sign (-1)^(p q), a repeated odd-rank factor gives 0, and like terms are collected; explicit arrays evaluate directly |
| `TensorSymmetry` | added | 7 | TensorSymmetry[tensor]: the symmetry of an explicit array: Symmetric[{..}] / Antisymmetric[{..}] when the symmetry group is the full symmetric group on a set of slots (the others fixed), ZeroSymmetric[{1, ..., r}] for a zero array, {} for none, else a generating set {{Cycles[..], phase}, ...} (phases +-1 or roots of unity); also reads the symmetry of MatrixSymbol/ArraySymbol and SymbolicIdentityArray; TensorSymmetry[t, slots] restricts to the given slots |
| `TensorWedge` | added | 11 | TensorWedge[t1, t2, ...]: the exterior product of explicit antisymmetric arrays of equal dimension, normalized as (p + q)!/(p! q!) Alt(t1 (x) t2) (TensorWedge[{a1, a2}, {b1, b2}] = {{0, a1 b2 - a2 b1}, {a2 b1 - a1 b2, 0}}); scalars multiply; symbolic arguments stay unevaluated |
| `ToPolarCoordinates` | added | 5 | ToPolarCoordinates[{x, y}] = {Sqrt[x^2 + y^2], ArcTan[x, y]}; {x1, ..., xn} -> hyperspherical {r, ArcCos[x1/Sqrt[x1^2 + ... + xn^2]], ..., ArcTan[x(n-1), xn]}; threads over a list of points |
| `ToSphericalCoordinates` | added | 3 | ToSphericalCoordinates[{x, y, z}] = {Sqrt[x^2 + y^2 + z^2], ArcTan[z, Sqrt[x^2 + y^2]], ArcTan[x, y]} (radius, polar angle from the z axis, azimuth); threads over a list of points |
| `TransformedField` | added | 4 | TransformedField["chart1" -> "chart2", f, {x1, ...} -> {y1, ...}]: a scalar field f (expression) or a vector field (list of components in the orthonormal frame of chart1) re-expressed in chart2 coordinates {y1, ...} (charts Cartesian, Polar, Spherical, Cylindrical); simplification assumes the standard chart ranges (r > 0, polar angles in (0, Pi)); rank >= 2 tensor fields raise |
| `TruncateSum` | added | 5 | TruncateSum[expr, m]: every Sum and Inactive[Sum] in expr is replaced by the sum of its first m terms (explicit, activated); symbolic m gives Inactive[Sum][f, {i, a, a + m - 1}]; ActivateResult -> False keeps the truncated sums inactive |
| `VectorSymbol` | added | 12 | VectorSymbol["v"] / VectorSymbol["v", n] / VectorSymbol["v", {n}] / VectorSymbol["v", n, dom]: a symbolic vector of length n (inert; used by ArrayExpand, ArraySimplify, TensorDimensions-style functions in this module); bad arguments raise |
| `Vectors` | added | 5 | Vectors[n] / Vectors[n, dom]: the domain of length-n vectors (dom Complexes by default, Reals, ...); inert domain used with Element and VectorSymbol; malformed specifications raise |
| `ZeroSymmetric` | added | 4 | ZeroSymmetric[{s1, ..., sn}]: the symmetry of a zero array; inert symmetry specification used by TensorSymmetry, ArraySymbol, MatrixSymbol, Matrices and Arrays (Symmetric/Antisymmetric/ZeroSymmetric[All]: every slot); malformed slot lists raise |

| Function | Status | Cases | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ArithmeticSequence` | fixed | 3 | first n terms a, a + d, ...; exact for exact input (legacy converted to floats and rounded to 10 digits) |
| `Binomial` | fixed | 15 | legacy truncated arguments with int() (Binomial[5/2, 1] = 2) and failed on symbols; now exact/symbolic with Wolfram's conventions for negative integers (Binomial[-1, -1] = 1) |
| `CartesianProduct` | verified | 3 | pairs {a, b} for a in the first list and b in the second (= Tuples[{l1, l2}]); now variadic |
| `Compositions` | fixed | 3 | legacy returned k-subsets of {1..n-1}; now Compositions[n, k] lists all ordered k-tuples of non-negative integers summing to n (Combinatorica convention), lexicographic |
| `Derangements` | verified | 4 | number of derangements !n (MikoshiLang; same as Subfactorial) |
| `DoubleFactorial` | fixed | 4 | negative odd integers supported ((-5)!! = 1/3); legacy truncated reals |
| `Factorial` | fixed | 6 | non-integers use Gamma[n + 1] (Factorial[1/2] = Sqrt[Pi]/2); negative integers give ComplexInfinity; symbols stay unevaluated; legacy truncated with int() |
| `Factorial2` | promoted | 3 | Wolfram name for the double factorial |
| `FibonacciSequence` | verified | 3 | first n Fibonacci numbers F0, F1, ... (MikoshiLang) |
| `GeometricSequence` | fixed | 3 | first n terms a, a r, ...; exact for exact input (legacy converted to floats and rounded) |
| `HookLengthFormula` | fixed | 5 | legacy subtracted the row index from each hook (wrong counts / ZeroDivisionError); now the number of standard Young tableaux of the shape |
| `IntegerPartitions` | fixed | 7 | legacy returned the number of partitions; Wolfram IntegerPartitions lists them in reverse lexicographic order; supports [n], [n, k], [n, {k}], [n, {kmin, kmax}], [n, kspec, {s1, ...} or All] and [n, kspec, sspec, m] (first m partitions, batch 6) |
| `Multinomial` | fixed | 4 | legacy Multinomial[n, {k...}] was not Wolfram's form; now Multinomial[n1, n2, ...] = (n1 + n2 + ...)!/(n1! n2! ...), exact for any exact arguments |
| `PartitionCount` | verified | 3 | MikoshiLang alias of PartitionsP |
| `PartitionsList` | fixed | 3 | legacy reused one mutable dict (every entry was the last partition); now the partitions of n in Wolfram IntegerPartitions order |
| `PartitionsP` | promoted | 3 | number of unrestricted partitions |
| `PartitionsQ` | promoted | 3 | number of partitions into distinct parts |
| `Permutations` | fixed | 4 | legacy Permutations[n, k] returned the count n!/(n-k)!; Wolfram lists permutations of a list (duplicates removed); Permutations[list, n] and [list, {n}] supported; integer arguments raise |
| `PowerSet` | verified | 3 | MikoshiLang alias of Subsets[list] |
| `Subfactorial` | promoted | 3 | !n |
| `Subsets` | fixed | 12 | Subsets[list], [list, n], [list, {n}], [list, {min, max}], [list, {min, max, step}] in Wolfram order (by size, then position); batch 6 adds Subsets[list, nspec, s] (first s), [list, nspec, {s}] (the s-th, computed by unranking) and [list, nspec, {m, n(, step)}], and any head (Subsets[f[a, b]]) |
| `Tuples` | promoted | 9 | Tuples[list, n] and Tuples[{l1, l2, ...}]; batch 6 adds Tuples[list, {n1, n2, ...}] (all n1 x n2 x ... arrays) and any head (Tuples[f[a, b], 2] = {f[a, a], f[a, b], f[b, a], f[b, b]}) |
| `YoungTableaux` | promoted | 22 | YoungTableaux[shape]: all standard Young tableaux of the partition shape (rows strictly increase left to right and down columns), sorted by row word, as Combinatorica Tableaux[shape]; their number equals HookLengthFormula[shape]. YoungTableaux[n]: all standard tableaux with n cells (over all partitions in reverse-lexicographic order), whose number is the number of involutions of n. Refuses more than 100000 tableaux. Legacy built one tableau and returned its size |

Check: exact (padding validation detects most wrong keys); Encrypt round trips in tests. |
| `DecryptFile` | added | 6 | DecryptFile[key, "file.mx"] decrypts an EncryptFile result into file and DecryptFile[key, source, target] into target; OverwriteTarget (default False); returns the absolute output path. Check: exact; EncryptFile round trips in tests. |

Check: exact; PHC string round trips in tests. |

Check: exact (validated wrapper). |
| `Encrypt` | added | 41 | Encrypt[key, expr] with a SymmetricKey (random IV per call for CBC/CFB/OFB/CTR), a "password" (AES256 key derived with scrypt), an RSA PublicKey (PKCS1 or OAEP) or an RSA PrivateKey (PKCS1 type 1, decrypted with the public key); strings as UTF-8, ByteArrays literally, other expressions via Compress; Method -> <\|"Padding", "InitializationVector", "BlockMode"\|>; operator form Encrypt[key]; gives EncryptedObject[<\|"Data", "InitializationVector", "OriginalForm"\|>]. Elliptic-curve keys give a clear error. Check: reference (FIPS-197, SP 800-38A, Blowfish and RC4 vectors) and Decrypt round trips in tests. |

Check: exact; DecryptFile round trips in tests. |

Check: exact; sign/verify and encrypt/decrypt round trips in tests. |
| `GenerateDerivedKey` | added | 19 | GenerateDerivedKey[password] / [password, salt] derives a key with scrypt (RFC 7914; defaults KeySize 64, N 2^15, r 8, p 1, random 16-byte salt) giving DerivedKey[<\|"Function", "DerivedKey", "Salt", "FunctionParameters"\|>]; Method -> <\|"Function" -> "scrypt", "KeySize", "N", "r", "p"\|>. Argon2 functions raise a clear error. Check: reference (RFC 7914 scrypt vector) and VerifyDerivedKey in tests. |
| `GenerateDigitalSignature` | added | 29 | GenerateDigitalSignature[expr, privatekey] signs expr (strings as UTF-8, ByteArrays literally, other expressions as their FullForm text): RSA PKCS#1 v1.5, ECDSA with RFC 6979 deterministic nonces (or "NonDeterministic"; low-s on secp256k1) or BIP-340 "Schnorr", ed25519 (RFC 8032); Method -> <\|"HashingMethod" (default SHA256; None for a precomputed ByteArray/hex digest), "SignatureType", "Padding" (PKCS1; X931 gives a clear error)\|>; operator form GenerateDigitalSignature[key]. Check: reference (RFC 6979, RFC 8032, BIP-340 vectors) and VerifyDigitalSignature in tests. |
| `GenerateFileSignature` | added | 4 | GenerateFileSignature[file, privatekey] gives the DigitalSignature of the bytes of file (same methods and Method option as GenerateDigitalSignature); operator form GenerateFileSignature[key]. Check: reference; verified by VerifyFileSignature and an OpenSSL signature in tests. |
| `GenerateSymmetricKey` | added | 45 | GenerateSymmetricKey[] (random AES256/CBC key), ["password"] (deterministic scrypt derivation), [ByteArray] (the given key bytes), [DerivedKey[...]]; Method -> cipher \| <\|"Cipher", "BlockMode", "KeySize", "InitializationVector"\|>; ciphers AES128/192/256, Blowfish, RC4 (DES, CAST5, IDEA give a clear error); gives SymmetricKey[<\|"Cipher", "BlockMode", "Key", "InitializationVector"\|>]. Check: exact; Encrypt/Decrypt round trips and published cipher vectors in tests. |
| `PrivateKey` | added | 19 | PrivateKey[<\|...\|>] is a private key (RSA: PublicModulus/PublicExponent/PrivateExponent; EllipticCurve: CurveName and PrivateMultiplier \| PrivateHexString \| PrivateByteArray; EdwardsCurve ed25519: PrivateByteArray \| PrivateHexString); partial specifications are completed (public point, public key, RSA exponent); properties: stored fields plus PrivateByteArray, PublicByteArray, Private/PublicHexString, Private/PublicKeySize, "Properties". Check: exact (curve membership and private/public consistency are validated); RFC 6979 and RFC 8032 keys in tests. |
| `PublicKey` | added | 11 | PublicKey[<\|...\|>] is a public key (RSA: PublicModulus, PublicExponent; EllipticCurve: CurveName and PublicCurvePoint \| PublicByteArray \| PublicHexString (compressed or not); EdwardsCurve: PublicByteArray \| PublicHexString); validated (points must lie on the curve) and normalised; properties as for PrivateKey. Check: exact (points are validated on the curve); reference keys in tests. |
| `SecurityCertificate` | added | 5 | SecurityCertificate[<\|...\|>] represents an X.509 certificate imported from PEM (properties Version, SerialNumber, SignatureAlgorithm, Issuer, ValidityStartDate, ValidityEndDate, Subject, PublicKey, Extensions, DigitalSignature, SignedData, Certificate, Properties); SecurityCertificate["PEM text"] or SecurityCertificate[ByteArray (DER)] parses one; VerifyDigitalSignature[{cert["SignedData"], cert["DigitalSignature"]}, issuerKey] checks its signature. Check: reference (OpenSSL certificates; their signatures verify) in tests. |
| `SymmetricKey` | added | 17 | SymmetricKey[<\|"Cipher", "BlockMode", "Key", "InitializationVector"\|>] represents a symmetric key (properties by name and "Properties"); validated, otherwise inert. Check: exact (validated wrapper). |
| `VerifyDerivedKey` | added | 6 | VerifyDerivedKey[key, password] gives True when password derives the DerivedKey key (same function, salt and parameters; constant-time comparison), False otherwise. Check: delegated (hashlib.scrypt); RFC 7914 reference in tests. |
| `VerifyDigitalSignature` | added | 16 | VerifyDigitalSignature[{expr, sig}, key] gives True when sig is a valid signature of expr for the public key (a PrivateKey or a SecurityCertificate also supplies it), False otherwise; a list of pairs gives a list; operator form VerifyDigitalSignature[key]. Check: reference (OpenSSL signatures and certificates) in tests. |
| `VerifyFileSignature` | added | 5 | VerifyFileSignature[{file, sig}, key] verifies a GenerateFileSignature signature against the current bytes of file; a list of pairs gives a list; operator form VerifyFileSignature[key]. Check: reference (an OpenSSL ECDSA file signature) in tests. |

### evaluation control, definitions, contexts (W01)

| Function | Status | Cases | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$Context` | added | 23 | current context (default "Global`"); set by Begin, BeginPackage, End, EndPackage; assignable (validated); Block localises it |
| `$ContextAliases` | added | 23 | association "alias`" -> "context`" used when parsing qualified names; $ContextAliases["a`"] = "ctx`" and =. update it; Needs[ctx -> alias] adds one |
| `$ContextPath` | added | 23 | contexts searched (before $Context) when a name is parsed; default {"System`", "Global`"}; modified by BeginPackage, EndPackage, Needs, DeclarePackage |
| `$Epilog` | added | 3 | expression evaluated when the REPL session ends |
| `$HistoryLength` | added | 3 | number of In/Out lines kept by the main loop (default Infinity) |
| `$IterationLimit` | added | 6 | maximum length of an evaluation chain (default 4096): each rewrite of an expression by a definition or rule counts once; exceeding it raises $IterationLimit::itlim |
| `$Line` | added | 3 | number of the current main-loop input line; assignable |
| `$ModuleNumber` | added | 4 | the number the next Module or Unique symbol gets (x$nnn); assignable |
| `$NewSymbol` | added | 3 | if set, $NewSymbol[name, context] is evaluated before a new symbol is created by the parser |
| `$Packages` | added | 22 | contexts of loaded packages (BeginPackage adds; Needs consults it) |
| `$Post` | added | 3 | function applied to each main-loop result before it is stored in Out |
| `$Pre` | added | 3 | function applied to each main-loop input before evaluation (unevaluated if it holds) |
| `$PrePrint` | added | 3 | function applied to each main-loop result before it is printed (not stored) |
| `$PreRead` | added | 3 | function applied to each main-loop input string before it is parsed |
| `$RecursionLimit` | added | 6 | maximum evaluation depth (default 1024, Infinity or an integer >= 20); exceeding it raises $RecursionLimit::reclim. MikoshiLang counts nested evaluator calls |

| `AllowedHeads` | added | 3 | option name: heads of subexpressions into which a function may descend |
| `Application` | added | 3 | Application[f, g] is a formal application with no built-in meaning (stays unevaluated) |

| `Get` | added | 16 | Get["file"] (<<file) reads a file of Wolfram Language input and evaluates each expression in turn, returning the last result (a relative file name is also searched for in PACKAGE_PATH and $MIKOSHILANG_PATH); Get["ctx`"] loads ctx.wl, ctx.m, ctx/init.m or ctx/Kernel/init.m from the working directory, PACKAGE_PATH or $MIKOSHILANG_PATH. | `In` | added | 5 | In[n] re-evaluates input line n of the main loop; In[] the last line, In[-k] earlier lines; unevaluated when there is no such line |
| `InString` | added | 3 | InString[n] is the text of input line n of the main loop; InString[] the last, InString[-k] earlier |
| `Inactivate` | added | 11 | Inactivate[expr] replaces every head f (except List, Rule, Blank and other structural heads) by Inactive[f] before evaluation; Inactivate[expr, patt] only heads matching patt (a symbol, Alternatives, Except[...]); Heads -> False leaves compound heads alone |
| `Inactive` | added | 31 | Inactive[f][args] is an inert form of f[args] (the arguments are evaluated, f is not applied); Inactive[atom] gives atom for atoms other than symbols |
| `IncludedContexts` | added | 3 | FullDefinition option: only symbols in these contexts are followed |
| `Indexed` | added | 8 | Indexed[list, i] gives list[[i]], Indexed[list, {i, j, ...}] indexes recursively; for a symbolic expr, Indexed[x, i] stays as the component x_i (Indexed[x, {i}] is the same as Indexed[x, i]) |
| `Information` | added | 19 | Information[symbol] (also ?f, ??f) gives InformationData[<\|ObjectType, Usage, Documentation, OwnValues, UpValues, DownValues, SubValues, DefaultValues, NValues, FormatValues, Options, Attributes, FullName\|>]; Information[s, "prop"] gives one property; Information["patt*"] a list; LongForm -> False keeps only the summary. Usage messages (f::usage) are not available |
| `InformationData` | added | 3 | InformationData[assoc, False]["prop"] gives a property of an Information result |
| `Inherited` | added | 4 | inert option value: inherited from an enclosing setting |
| `InverseFunction` | added | 8 | InverseFunction[f]: ArcSin for Sin etc. (named inverses), the solved inverse of a pure function with a unique inverse (InverseFunction[2 # + 3 &] = (#1 - 3)/2 &), InverseFunction[InverseFunction[f]] = f; InverseFunction[f, n, tot] for the n-th of tot arguments; otherwise stays symbolic (InverseFunction[f][x]) |
| `InverseFunctions` | added | 3 | option name of Solve and Reduce: whether InverseFunction objects may be used |
| `Label` | added | 5 | Label[tag] marks a point in a compound expression for Goto[tag]; evaluates to Null |
| `LocalSymbol` | added | 6 | LocalSymbol["name"] gives the value stored persistently (a file under ~/.mikoshilang/LocalSymbols, or $MIKOSHILANG_LOCALSYMBOL_BASE) by LocalSymbol["name"] = val or := val; unevaluated when never assigned; LocalSymbol["name", "dir"] uses another base; =. deletes it |
| `Locked` | added | 5 | attribute: the attributes of the symbol can no longer be changed (Protect/Unprotect, SetAttributes, ClearAttributes, Attributes[f] = ... raise) |
| `Manual` | added | 6 | inert option value: selected manually |
| `Method` | added | 173 | option name Method -> "name" / {"name", opts} / Automatic for algorithm choices |
| `NHoldAll` | added | 3 | attribute: N does not affect any argument of f |
| `NHoldFirst` | added | 3 | attribute: N does not affect the first argument of f |
| `NHoldRest` | added | 3 | attribute: N affects only the first argument of f |
| `NameQ` | added | 4 | NameQ["string"]: True if any symbol name matches (abbreviated string patterns); ResolveContextAliases option |
| `Names` | added | 9 | Names["pattern"] (metacharacters * and @, a context prefix such as "Global`*", StringExpression or RegularExpression), Names[{p1, ...}], Names[] ; options IgnoreCase, ResolveContextAliases, SpellingCorrection -> False. Names are short when their context is $Context or on $ContextPath. System` contains the symbols MikoshiLang implements |
| `Needs` | added | 4 | Needs["ctx`"] loads the package (Get["ctx`"]) unless ctx` is in $Packages and puts ctx` on $ContextPath; Needs["ctx`" -> "alias`"] adds a context alias instead; Needs["ctx`" -> None] only loads; Needs["ctx`", "file"] loads the given file |
| `NonConstants` | added | 6 | option NonConstants -> {...} of Dt and D (symbols treated as constant / as depending on the variable) |
| `NonThreadable` | added | 3 | attribute: arithmetic and other Listable functions do not thread lists over f or f[...]; the threadable arguments still combine |
| `Once` | added | 7 | Once[expr] evaluates expr the first time and afterwards returns the cached result for the rest of the session (Once[expr, "KernelSession"]); other persistence locations raise; Once[expr] =. clears |
| `OperatorApplied` | added | 7 | OperatorApplied[f][y][x] = f[x, y]; OperatorApplied[f, n][x1]...[xn] = f[x1, ..., xn]; OperatorApplied[f, {i1, ...}] and k -> {i1, ...} reorder; bracket structure is irrelevant |
| `OptionValue` | added | 9 | OptionValue[name] inside f[..., OptionsPattern[]] := rhs gives the value of option name in the call (or f's default); OptionValue[f, name], OptionValue[f, opts, name], lists of names; OptionsPattern[{f, g}] searches several defaults |
| `Options` | added | 27 | Options[f] gives the default option rules of a user symbol (set by Options[f] = {...} or SetOptions); Options[f, name] or Options[f, {names}] selects; Options[expr] gives the options at the end of expr (f[x, a -> 1] gives {a -> 1}). Built-in option lists are not catalogued and raise |
| `OptionsPattern` | added | 9 | OptionsPattern[] matches a sequence of zero or more rules or lists of rules; OptionsPattern[f] or OptionsPattern[{f, ...}] names where OptionValue finds defaults |
| `Out` | added | 4 | Out[n] (%n) is the n-th output of the main loop (Session.evaluate_input / REPL / Jupyter), Out[] (%) the last, Out[-k] (%%...) the k-th previous; unevaluated when there is no such output |
| `OwnValues` | added | 4 | OwnValues[x]: {HoldPattern[x] :> value} for a symbol with a value, else {}; OwnValues[x] = {...} sets it |
| `Postfix` | added | 3 | Postfix[f[x]] prints as x//f and Postfix[f[x], h] as x<>h (display wrapper) |
| `Prefix` | added | 3 | Prefix[f[x]] prints as f@x and Prefix[f[x], h] as h<>x (display wrapper; the expression inside is evaluated) |
| `Protect` | added | 7 | Protect[s1, s2, ...] (symbols, names or string patterns) sets the Protected attribute (assignments then raise); returns the names whose protection changed |
| `ReadProtected` | added | 3 | attribute: Definition, FullDefinition and Information show only the attributes; the values are still used in evaluation and DownValues etc. still return them |
| `Remove` | added | 4 | Remove[s1, ...] removes symbols completely (values, attributes, options, the name: Names no longer lists it); Remove["ctx`*"] removes by pattern; protected symbols raise Remove::rmptc |
| `ResolveContextAliases` | added | 3 | option of Names, NameQ and Contexts: False ignores $ContextAliases |
| `SetOptions` | added | 4 | SetOptions[f, name -> value, ...] resets defaults that f already has (SetOptions::optnf for an unknown option), returning the new Options[f]; SetOptions[{f, g}, ...] sets several |
| `Stack` | added | 11 | Stack[] gives the tags (heads) of the evaluations in progress, outermost first, excluding Stack itself; Stack[patt] the expressions matching patt wrapped in HoldCompleteForm (Stack[_] all); MikoshiLang's internal evaluations made by library code also appear |
| `StackBegin` | added | 7 | StackBegin[expr] evaluates expr with a fresh evaluation stack (outer evaluations are not shown by Stack) |
| `StackComplete` | added | 3 | StackComplete[expr] evaluates expr keeping the earlier expressions of each evaluation chain on the stack (f[2] and g[4] both appear after f[x_] := g[x^2]) |
| `StackInhibit` | added | 3 | StackInhibit[expr] evaluates expr without adding its evaluations to the stack |
| `Stub` | added | 4 | attribute set by DeclarePackage: using the symbol loads its package |
| `SubValues` | added | 3 | SubValues[f]: rules for f[...][...] (HoldPattern[lhs] :> rhs); SubValues[f] = {...} replaces them |
| `SubValuesHoldAll` | added | 4 | attribute: in f[a...][s...], the subvalue arguments s are held (Unevaluated stripped, Sequence spliced) |
| `SyntaxInformation` | added | 4 | SyntaxInformation[f] gives the syntax properties set by SyntaxInformation[f] = {"ArgumentsPattern" -> {...}, ...} ({} if none); used only for advisories, not evaluation. Built-in syntax data is not catalogued and raises |
| `TagSet` | added | 4 | f /: lhs = rhs: attaches the rule to f, which must be the head of lhs (a DownValue or SubValue) or an argument of lhs or an argument's head (an UpValue); otherwise TagSet::tagnf is raised |
| `TagSetDelayed` | added | 3 | f /: lhs := rhs (delayed TagSet); returns Null |
| `TagUnset` | added | 3 | f /: lhs =. removes the rule for lhs attached to f (an UpValue, DownValue or SubValue); raises if there is none |
| `Temporary` | added | 3 | attribute of Module local symbols (and Unique[x, {Temporary}]); reported by Attributes |
| `Threaded` | added | 6 | f[a, Threaded[b]] for Listable f combines b with the lowest-level subarrays of a; Threaded[b, alev] and Threaded[b, 1 -> alev] choose the level (other blev raise) |
| `TraceAbove` | added | 3 | Trace option: True adds the first and last forms of every chain containing a match; All adds all forms of those chains |
| `TraceBackward` | added | 4 | Trace option: True also keeps the earlier forms of a chain in which form matched; All also their subevaluations |
| `TraceDepth` | added | 3 | Trace option: TraceDepth -> n keeps only the first n levels of nested lists |
| `TraceForward` | added | 3 | Trace option: True also keeps the later forms of a chain in which form matched; All also their subevaluations |
| `TraceOff` | added | 3 | Trace option: TraceOff -> patt does not trace inside evaluations of forms matching patt (the forms themselves and their results are kept) |
| `TraceOn` | added | 3 | Trace option: TraceOn -> patt traces only inside evaluations of forms matching patt |
| `TracePrint` | added | 3 | TracePrint[expr] prints the forms of the evaluation of expr indented by nesting level and returns the value; TracePrint[expr, form] only matching forms; Trace options accepted (forms are printed after evaluation completes) |
| `TraceScan` | added | 4 | TraceScan[f, expr] applies f to HoldForm of every form in the evaluation of expr and returns its value; TraceScan[f, expr, form] only matching forms; TraceScan[f, expr, form, fp] also applies fp to (HoldForm[form], HoldForm[result]) of each matching chain; f runs after the evaluation completes |
| `Unevaluated` | added | 8 | Unevaluated[expr] passes expr unevaluated as an argument of a function; the wrapper is removed when the function uses it, kept when the function returns the expression unchanged (Length[Unevaluated[1 + 2]] = 2) |
| `Unique` | added | 11 | Unique[] gives $nnn, Unique[x] gives x$nnn (using $ModuleNumber, then incrementing it), Unique["xxx"] gives xxxn with n counting up from 1 per prefix, Unique[{x, y}] gives a list; Unique[x, {attrs}] sets attributes |
| `Unprotect` | added | 5 | Unprotect[s1, ...] removes Protected, also from built-in symbols (definitions for them are then used before the built-in rules); returns the names whose protection changed. Special forms evaluated by the kernel itself (If, Set, Module, ...) still cannot get definitions |
| `Until` | added | 6 | Until[test, body] evaluates body then test, repeating until test is True (at least once); Until[test] has an empty body; Break[] exits, Continue[] skips to the test; returns Null |
| `UpSet` | added | 4 | lhs ^= rhs: rhs is evaluated and the rule is attached (as an upvalue) to every symbol that is an argument of lhs or the head of an argument (h[x_] in f[h[x_]] attaches to h); returns rhs |
| `UpSetDelayed` | added | 3 | lhs ^:= rhs: like UpSet with rhs kept unevaluated until the rule is used; returns Null |
| `UpValues` | added | 8 | UpValues[f]: rules attached to f by UpSet/TagSet (HoldPattern[lhs] :> rhs); UpValues[f] = {...} replaces them |
| `Update` | added | 3 | Update[s] / Update[] tell the system that values depending on s may have changed; MikoshiLang keeps no evaluation caches that could go stale, so this returns Null |
| `ValueQ` | added | 15 | ValueQ[expr] is True when expr has a value: a symbol with an OwnValue, or an expression changed by evaluation (Method -> "Legacy" default compares the result; "SymbolDefinitionsPresent" and "TrialEvaluation" also accepted) |

### external interfaces (W30)

| Function | Status | Cases | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$AllowInternet` | added | 7 | $AllowInternet is True by default; setting it to False (e.g. Block[{$AllowInternet = False}, ...]) makes every W30 network head refuse non-loopback hosts before connecting (URL functions give Failure["ConnectionFailure", ...], socket and lookup heads raise ValueError); 127.0.0.1/localhost stay reachable. A non-Boolean value raises ValueError when a network head reads it. The setting is not preserved between sessions. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and blocked/allowed cases in tests. |
| `$Cookies` | added | 11 | $Cookies is the session's list of cookie associations ({} initially). SetCookies and URLRead (with CookieFunction -> Automatic) append to it, requests with "Cookies" -> Automatic send the matching unexpired ones (domain, AllowSubdomains, path prefix and ConnectionType -> "HTTPS" respected), and assigning a list or Block[{$Cookies}, ...] replaces or localises it. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and cookies sent to and received from a local server in tests. |
| `$DefaultNetworkInterface` | added | 3 | $DefaultNetworkInterface is the name of the interface carrying the default route (e.g. "eth0"), read from /proc/net/route, or None when there is no default route; on systems without /proc/net/route it raises NotImplementedError. Check: exact (the name is one of socket.if_nameindex()) in tests. |
| `$DefaultProxyRules` | added | 4 | $DefaultProxyRules is <\|"UseProxy" -> Automatic, "HTTP" -> None, "HTTPS" -> None, "FTP" -> None, "Socks" -> None\|> (the documented default); URLRead and friends honour it: UseProxy -> Automatic uses the system proxy settings (http_proxy/https_proxy/no_proxy), None or False uses none, Manual or True uses the "HTTP"/"HTTPS" entries {host, port}. Assign the whole association to change it. Socks proxies raise NotImplementedError; malformed settings raise ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation default value) and a proxied request to a local server in tests. |
| `$MachineAddresses` | added | 3 | $MachineAddresses lists the IPv4 addresses of this computer's non-loopback network interfaces as strings ({} when offline), read from the interfaces (Linux SIOCGIFADDR) or, elsewhere, the source address of the default route (a UDP connect sends no packet). Check: exact (every entry is a valid non-loopback IPv4 address that a local socket can bind to) in tests. |
| `$UserAgent` | added | 3 | $UserAgent is the user agent of the HTTP request that started the current evaluation; MikoshiLang evaluations are never started by an HTTP request, so it is None (Wolfram's documented value outside a web request). Check: exact (documented value) in tests. |
| `$UserAgentString` | added | 3 | $UserAgentString is the user agent string of the HTTP request that started the current evaluation; None here (Wolfram's documented value outside a web request). The agent MikoshiLang itself sends is "MikoshiLang HTTPClient <version>". Check: exact (documented value) in tests. |
| `Authentication` | added | 4 | option of URLRead, URLExecute and URLDownload: Automatic or None (no credentials), or an association with "Username"/"Password" (HTTP Basic), "Headers" and "Query" entries added to the request; PermissionsKey, SecuredAuthenticationKey, SSH keys and other cloud/SSH settings raise NotImplementedError. Credentials are never read from disk. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and the Authorization header seen by a local server in tests. |
| `ConnectionSettings` | added | 4 | option of URLRead and related functions: Automatic or <\|"MaxDownloadSpeed" -> b, "MaxUploadSpeed" -> b\|> with b bytes per second (approximate throttling, as documented) or Automatic. Quantity speeds raise NotImplementedError, unknown keys or bad values ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and a throttled local download timed in tests. |
| `CookieFunction` | added | 3 | option of URLRead, URLExecute, URLDownload and HTTPRequest: Automatic (= SetCookies, the default) stores received cookies in $Cookies, None ignores them, f applies f to each cookie association (keys Domain, Path, Name, Content, ExpirationDate, AllowSubdomains, ConnectionType, ScriptAccessible). Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and cookies from a local server in tests. |
| `FindCookies` | added | 6 | FindCookies[] gives $Cookies; FindCookies[domain] the cookies whose Domain matches domain (a string, a * wildcard pattern as in FileNames, or a string pattern); FindCookies[assoc] those whose elements match every entry of assoc (string entries by pattern, others by equality). Unknown elements raise ValueError, other argument kinds TypeError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and SetCookies round trips in tests. |
| `FollowRedirects` | added | 3 | option of URLRead, URLExecute, URLDownload and HTTPRequest (default True): True follows 301/302/303/307/308 redirects (at most 20; 303, and 301/302 after a non-GET, switch to GET), False gives the redirect response itself (URLExecute then gives Failure). A non-Boolean raises ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and redirects from a local server in tests. |
| `HTTPRedirect` | added | 4 | HTTPRedirect[uri] and HTTPRedirect[uri, <\|"StatusCode" -> 302, "ContentType", "Cookies", "Headers"\|>] represent a redirect response (validated, otherwise inert, since there is no cloud deployment); r["prop"] gives the metadata, "Location" and "StatusCodeDescription", and "Headers" gains Location -> uri when not given. A non-3xx status or unknown element raises ValueError, CloudObject NotImplementedError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation defaults, RFC 9110 phrases) in tests. |
| `HTTPRequest` | added | 7 | HTTPRequest[url], HTTPRequest[assoc], HTTPRequest[url, assoc] and trailing options (CharacterEncoding, CookieFunction, FollowRedirects, Interactive, TimeConstraint, VerifySecurityCertificates) are a symbolic request (nothing is sent); HTTPRequest[url] is shown as HTTPRequest[url, <\|\|>]. Elements: URL components plus Method ("GET"), Body (string, ByteArray, File, byte list, form rules or multipart specs), ContentType, Username, Password, Cookies, UserAgent, Headers. req["prop"], req[{props}] and req[] give components, elements, "Body", "BodyByteArray", "BodyBytes", "FormRules", "PathString", "QueryString", "AbsolutePath", "AbsoluteDomain", "URL", "Properties", "PropertyAssociation". Unknown elements, options or properties raise ValueError, wrong kinds TypeError, CloudObject NotImplementedError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation examples) and requests echoed back by a local server in tests. |
| `HTTPResponse` | added | 4 | HTTPResponse[body] and HTTPResponse[body, <\|"StatusCode" -> 200, "ContentType" -> "text/html", "Cookies" -> {}, "Headers" -> {}\|>] (body a string, ByteArray or byte list; option CharacterEncoding) represent an HTTP response; URLRead returns one with a ByteArray body. resp["prop"], resp[{props}] and resp[] give the metadata plus "Body" (decoded with the charset of ContentType, UTF-8 for text types, byte-per-character otherwise), "BodyByteArray", "BodyBytes", "CharacterEncoding", "StatusCodeDescription" (http.HTTPStatus phrase) and "Properties". Bad metadata raises ValueError/TypeError, a body that is invalid in its charset raises ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation and RFC 9110 status phrases) and local-server responses in tests. |
| `HostLookup` | added | 6 | HostLookup[name] gives the IPv4 addresses of a host as IPAddress objects (IPv6 if it has no IPv4 address); HostLookup[address] (an IP string or IPAddress) gives the host name; HostLookup[spec, prop] gives "FullName", "IPv4Addresses", "IPv6Addresses" or All (an association); URLs are reduced to their host; lists thread. Resolution uses the system resolver (socket.getaddrinfo/gethostbyaddr), so localhost and literal addresses need no network. An unknown host gives Missing["NotFound"] (documented); with $AllowInternet = False only loopback names are looked up (others raise ValueError). Check: reference (Wolfram documentation localhost examples) and name/address round trips in tests. |
| `IPAddress` | added | 7 | IPAddress["address"] is a validated symbolic IPv4 or IPv6 address (checked with Python's ipaddress module; IPv6 text is kept as given); used by HostLookup, SocketConnect, URLResponseTime and socket properties. A malformed address raises ValueError, a non-string TypeError, a symbol stays unevaluated. Check: exact (ipaddress validation) and HostLookup round trips in tests. |
| `SetCookies` | added | 9 | SetCookies[assoc] or SetCookies[{assoc, ...}] adds cookies (elements Domain, Path, Name, Content, ExpirationDate, CreationDate, AllowSubdomains, ConnectionType, ScriptAccessible) to $Cookies, replacing a cookie with the same Domain, Path and Name, and returns its argument; an already expired cookie removes the stored one. Cookies live in the session (Block[{$Cookies}, ...] localises them); there is no persistent $CookieStore. Unknown elements or bad values raise ValueError, non-associations TypeError, a missing Name ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and SetCookies/FindCookies/$Cookies round trips in tests. |
| `SocketConnect` | added | 32 | SocketConnect[addr] and SocketConnect[addr, "TCP"] open a TCP connection and give SocketObject[...]; addr is {host, port}, {host, "service"}, "host:port", a local port, URL["url"] or "scheme://host" (port from the scheme's service), {IPAddress[...], port}, or a SocketObject from SocketOpen. "ZMQ", {"ZMQ", type}, "WS" and "WSS" raise NotImplementedError. A refused or unreachable address, or a non-loopback host with $AllowInternet = False, raises ValueError (Wolfram returns $Failed). Reading uses SocketReadMessage; writing uses SocketWriteMessage (Close/WriteString/BinaryWrite on sockets are wired to the W27 stream functions at integration through wl_external.close_socket/write_socket). Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and echo round trips with a local TCP server in tests. |
| `SocketListen` | added | 12 | SocketListen[socket, fun], SocketListen[port, fun], SocketListen["host:port", fun] and SocketListen[Automatic] start a background thread that applies fun to an event association for every chunk of data received on a TCP socket (for a server, on each connected client), and give a SocketListener; keys "Timestamp", "Socket", "SourceSocket", "Data" by default, also "DataBytes", "DataByteArray", "MultipartComplete" via HandlerFunctionsKeys; options CharacterEncoding (UTF-8), HandlerFunctions (<\|"DataReceived" -> f\|>), RecordSeparators (None or strings: fun gets each delimited record). fun runs in the session that started the listener, one event at a time; its errors are collected in listener["HandlerErrors"]. A socket made by SocketListen is closed with the listener. Unknown keys/options raise ValueError; ZMQ/web sockets NotImplementedError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and events from a local client in tests. |
| `SocketListener` | added | 5 | SocketListener["TCP-uuid"] represents an active listener made by SocketListen; listener["prop"] gives "Socket", "HandlerFunctions", "HandlerFunctionsKeys", "RecordSeparators", "CharacterEncoding", "EventCount" (events seen) and "HandlerErrors" (messages of handler calls that raised), and "Properties". DeleteObject stops it (wired at integration through wl_external.delete_listener). An id that is not active raises ValueError. Check: exact (listener state) and event counts from a local client in tests. |
| `SocketObject` | added | 5 | SocketObject["TCP-uuid"] represents an open TCP socket made by SocketConnect, SocketOpen or accepted by an open server; socket["prop"] gives "SourceIPAddress", "SourcePort", "DestinationIPAddress", "DestinationPort", "Protocol", "UUID", "Type" ("Client", "Server" or "Remote"), "ConnectedClients" (servers) and "Properties". A SocketObject that is not open raises ValueError when used; constructing one by hand with an unknown id raises ValueError. Check: exact (properties read from the OS socket) and cross-checked between the two ends of a local connection in tests. |
| `SocketOpen` | added | 7 | SocketOpen[port], SocketOpen[{host, port}], SocketOpen["host:port"], SocketOpen[{host, Automatic}] and SocketOpen[Automatic] (an available port on 127.0.0.1), with optional "TCP", open a listening TCP socket on this machine and give SocketObject[...]; incoming connections become socket["ConnectedClients"]. Only local addresses can be opened (a non-local address raises ValueError, as the OS refuses it); "ZMQ" protocols raise NotImplementedError; a port in use raises ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and SocketConnect round trips in tests. |
| `SocketReadMessage` | added | 10 | SocketReadMessage[socket] waits for data on a TCP SocketObject and gives the bytes currently in the operating-system buffer as a ByteArray (an empty ByteArray when the peer has closed the connection); on a server socket it reads the first connected client with data. The "MultipartComplete" option (web sockets only) is accepted and has no effect on TCP. A socket that is not open raises ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and echo round trips with a local TCP server in tests. |
| `SocketReadyQ` | added | 3 | SocketReadyQ[socket] gives True if data can be read from the TCP SocketObject immediately (for a server: from any connected client), without blocking; SocketReadyQ[socket, t] waits up to t seconds (a number or Quantity[t, "Seconds"]). A socket that is not open raises ValueError, a negative time ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and before/after-write cases with a local server in tests. |
| `SocketWaitAll` | added | 3 | SocketWaitAll[{s1, s2, ...}] waits until data is ready to read on every TCP SocketObject and gives {s1, s2, ...}; an empty list is returned at once. Sockets that are not open raise ValueError, non-lists TypeError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and SocketReadyQ on the result in tests. |
| `SocketWaitNext` | added | 3 | SocketWaitNext[{s1, s2, ...}] waits until data is ready on any of the TCP SocketObjects and gives that socket (the first ready one in list order). An empty list or sockets that are not open raise ValueError, non-lists TypeError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and the socket that received data in tests. |
| `SocketWriteMessage` | added | 14 | Partial. SocketWriteMessage[socket, ba] and SocketWriteMessage[socket, "string"] (UTF-8) write the bytes to a TCP SocketObject (a server writes to every connected client) and return Null. Deviation: Wolfram documents this head for web sockets only, which are not supported ("WS"/"WSS" sockets cannot be created); the <\|"DataByteArray", "Type", "MultipartComplete"\|> form raises NotImplementedError. A closed socket raises ValueError, other data TypeError. Check: reference (the bytes arrive unchanged at a local echo server) in tests. |
| `Sockets` | added | 4 | Sockets[] gives the open SocketObjects of the session (servers, clients and accepted remote ends); Sockets[spec] filters by "Local" (opened here: servers and clients), "Remote" (accepted connections), "Server", "Client", a protocol ("TCP"; "ZMQ", "WS", "WSS" give {}) or All. An unknown spec raises ValueError. Check: exact (registry contents) and before/after open cases in tests. |
| `URLBuild` | added | 12 | URLBuild[path, params], URLBuild[{base, seg, ...}], URLBuild[assoc] and URLBuild[assoc, params] build a URL string: path segments after the first are percent-encoded and joined with /, query values follow URLQueryEncode (lists repeat the key, None gives a bare key), existing query parameters are kept, a domain with an empty path gets / before ?; association keys Scheme, User, Domain, Port, Path, Query, Fragment; options CharacterEncoding, "SortQueries", "RemoveEmptyQueries". Unknown keys or options raise ValueError, wrong kinds TypeError, CloudObject NotImplementedError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation examples) and URLBuild[URLParse[u]] == u round trips in tests. |
| `URLDecode` | added | 7 | URLDecode[s] decodes %XX escapes (bytes interpreted in UTF-8 or CharacterEncoding -> enc) and turns + into a space; threads over lists. Invalid bytes for the encoding raise ValueError, a non-string TypeError, a symbol stays unevaluated. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation examples) and URLEncode round trips in tests. |
| `URLDownload` | added | 5 | URLDownload[url] saves the body to a new file in $TemporaryDirectory and gives File[path]; URLDownload[url, file] writes file (an existing directory gets the server's or the URL's file name, with a -n suffix if taken); URLDownload[{url, ...}] / [{url, ...}, dir] download into a new temporary directory or dir and give a list; URLDownload[req, loc, elem] gives "File", "Headers", "Cookies", "ContentType", "StatusCode", "StatusCodeDescription" or a list of them. Requests and options as for URLRead. Connection failures give Failure["ConnectionFailure", ...]; an HTTP status >= 400 raises ValueError and writes nothing. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and local-server downloads compared byte for byte in tests. |
| `URLEncode` | added | 13 | URLEncode[s] percent-encodes every byte of the UTF-8 (or CharacterEncoding -> enc) form of s except letters, digits and -_.~ (a space becomes %20, as in Wolfram); integers and machine numbers are converted to their InputForm text, None/Null/Missing give "", True/False give "true"/"false", URL["u"] encodes u; threads over lists. A symbol stays unevaluated; CloudObject raises NotImplementedError, other expressions raise TypeError/ValueError, and an unknown encoding ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation examples) and URLDecode round trips in tests. |
| `URLExecute` | added | 6 | URLExecute[url], URLExecute[url, params], URLExecute[url, params, fmt] (url a URL, association or HTTPRequest; params rules or an association) send the request (simple parameters go in the query string with GET, files, byte arrays and long values are POSTed as a form) and Import the body: by the given format, else by content type (JSON -> "JSON", text/* -> string, CSV, TSV, XML; HTML raises NotImplementedError since the plain-text extraction is not reproduced), else by sniffing the bytes. Options as for URLRead. A redirect left unfollowed (FollowRedirects -> False) and connection failures give Failure["ConnectionFailure", ...] (documented); an HTTP status >= 400 raises ValueError, an unrecognisable body raises from Import. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and local-server round trips in tests. |
| `URLExpand` | added | 5 | URLExpand[url] (a string or URL[...]; lists thread) follows the HTTP redirects of a shortened URL and gives the final URL as a string (a URL that does not redirect gives itself); options CookieFunction, Interactive (accepted), TimeConstraint and VerifySecurityCertificates. Deviation: Wolfram asks the Wolfram Cloud; MikoshiLang follows the redirects directly with a GET request (at most 20). A connection failure gives Failure["ConnectionFailure", ...] like URLRead; with $AllowInternet = False only loopback hosts are contacted. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and local-server redirects in tests. |
| `URLParse` | added | 11 | URLParse[url] gives <\|"Scheme", "User", "Domain", "Port", "Path", "Query", "Fragment"\|> (absent components None, Port an integer, Path a list with "" first for an absolute path and last for a trailing /, Query decoded rules); URLParse[url, comp] and URLParse[url, {comp, ...}] also give "PathString", "AbsoluteDomain", "AbsolutePath", "QueryString"; URL[...] accepted; threads over a list of URLs; option CharacterEncoding. An unknown component raises ValueError, a non-string TypeError, CloudObject NotImplementedError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation examples) and URLBuild[URLParse[u]] == u round trips in tests. |
| `URLQueryDecode` | added | 9 | URLQueryDecode["k1=v1&k2=v2"] gives {"k1" -> "v1", ...} (form decoding: + is a space, a key without = gets ""); URL["..."] uses its query part; threads over (nested) lists; options CharacterEncoding, "SortQueries", "RemoveEmptyQueries". Bytes invalid in the encoding raise ValueError, a non-string TypeError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation examples) and URLQueryEncode round trips in tests. |
| `URLQueryEncode` | added | 13 | URLQueryEncode[<\|k1 -> v1, ...\|>] or URLQueryEncode[{k1 -> v1, ...}] builds k1=v1&k2=v2 with keys and values form-encoded (a space becomes +); list values give repeated keys, None/Null/Missing give a bare key, True/False give true/false; options CharacterEncoding, "SortQueries" and "RemoveEmptyQueries". A non-rule argument raises TypeError, an unknown option ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation examples) and URLQueryDecode round trips in tests. |
| `URLRead` | added | 37 | URLRead[req], URLRead[req, elem], URLRead[req, {elems}] and URLRead[{req, ...}, ...] send HTTP(S) requests (req a URL, URL[...], association or HTTPRequest) with http.client and give an HTTPResponse (ByteArray body) or the elements "Body", "BodyByteArray", "BodyBytes", "Headers", "Cookies", "ContentType", "StatusCode", "StatusCodeDescription", All, Automatic; options Authentication (Automatic/None or <\|"Username", "Password", "Headers", "Query"\|>), CharacterEncoding, ConnectionSettings, CookieFunction, FollowRedirects (True), Interactive (no dialogs are ever shown), TimeConstraint, VerifySecurityCertificates. Lists are read one after another. A connection failure, too many redirects or $AllowInternet = False for a non-loopback host gives the documented Failure["ConnectionFailure", <\|..., "URL", "HTTPRequest"\|>]. "Stream", non-HTTP schemes and cloud authentication raise NotImplementedError; unknown elements/options ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and round trips against a local http.server in tests. |
| `URLResponseTime` | added | 5 | URLResponseTime[url] and URLResponseTime[url, prop] time one request for the first byte (GET with Range: bytes=0-0, no redirects) of url (a URL, URL[...] or bare host name, port 80 assumed) and give Quantity[t, "Seconds"], cumulative from the start like curl: "NameLookup", "HostConnection", "SSLHandshake" (0 for http), "PreTransfer", "TransferInitiation", "TransactionTotal" (the default), "HTTPRedirect" (0, redirects are not followed), "ConnectionTimes" or All for an association; option TimeConstraint (default 60). Deviation: an unreachable URL raises ValueError (Wolfram returns $Failed). The timings are verified to be non-decreasing and an ArithmeticError is raised otherwise. Check: self-check (monotone timing chain) and local-server timings bounded by AbsoluteTiming in tests. |
