| Function | Status | Cases | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$CompilationTarget` | added | 4 | $CompilationTarget is "WVM" (the documented default) and gives the default CompilationTarget of Compile; Block[{$CompilationTarget = "C"}, ...] changes it (results are identical since no machine code is generated); other values make Compile raise ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) in tests. |
| `$CompilerEnvironment` | added | 4 | $CompilerEnvironment is the CompilerEnvironmentObject FunctionCompile uses by default (initially CompilerEnvironmentObject[<\|"ID" -> "Default"\|>], empty); CompilerEnvironmentAppendTo[decls] adds to it and $CompilerEnvironment = CreateCompilerEnvironment[] replaces it. The environment lives for the Python process. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation examples) in tests. |
| `$TargetSystems` | added | 3 | $TargetSystems lists the documented TargetSystem names {"Linux-ARM", "Linux-x86-64", "MacOSX-ARM64", "MacOSX-x86-64", "Windows-x86-64"}; they are accepted by CreateCompilerEnvironment and FunctionCompile (no machine code is generated for any of them). Check: reference (Wolfram documentation output) in tests. |
| `AssumeDeterministic` | added | 3 | option of BayesianMinimization/BayesianMaximization (wl_linalg_optim): True assumes the objective gives the same value for the same configuration (no noise term), False (the default) does not. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and the optimiser result with both settings in tests. |
| `CompilationOptions` | added | 4 | option of Compile: Automatic or a list of "ExpressionOptimization", "InlineCompiledFunctions", "InlineExternalDefinitions" -> True\|False\|Automatic (validated; they only affect generated code, so results are unchanged); other settings raise ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) in tests. |
| `CompilationTarget` | added | 3 | option of Compile: "WVM" or "C" (default $CompilationTarget); recorded in the CompiledFunction, both evaluate the same way (no external C compiler is used); other values raise ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation example values) in tests. |
| `Compile` | added | 32 | Compile[{x1, ...}, expr], Compile[{{x, _Integer\|_Real\|_Complex\|True \| False}, ...}, expr] and Compile[{{x, t, rank}, ...}, expr] (HoldAll) give CompiledFunction[...]; options CompilationOptions ({"ExpressionOptimization" \| "InlineCompiledFunctions" \| "InlineExternalDefinitions" -> True\|False\|Automatic}), CompilationTarget ("WVM" or "C"; default $CompilationTarget), Parallelization, RuntimeAttributes ({} or {Listable}) and RuntimeOptions are validated (no machine code is generated, so "C" needs no C compiler and gives the same results). Applying the CompiledFunction to arguments of the declared types (integers are accepted for reals, full arrays of the declared rank) evaluates expr with them and gives machine numbers (integers stay integers); other arguments, e.g. symbolic ones, use ordinary evaluation as Wolfram documents. A wrong argument count raises ValueError; malformed specifications ValueError/TypeError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation examples) and agreement with N of the uncompiled expression in tests. |
| `Compiled` | added | 4 | option of numerical functions (NIntegrate, NSum, FindRoot, ... in wl_numcalc) saying whether to compile the integrand: accepted with True or False; MikoshiLang evaluates directly, so results are the same either way. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and identical results with True and False in tests. |
| `CompiledCodeFunction` | added | 3 | CompiledCodeFunction[<\|"Signature" -> TypeSpecifier[{types} -> type], "Input" -> f, "Declarations" -> {...}, "ErrorAction" -> ...\|>] is made by FunctionCompile ("InertExpression" stands for a result type that could not be inferred) and applied like the function: arguments of the wrong type or number give the documented Failure["ArgumentType"\|"ArgumentCount", <\|...\|>]. A malformed object raises TypeError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and agreement with the uncompiled function in tests. |
| `CompiledFunction` | added | 3 | CompiledFunction[HoldComplete[{vars}], {{type, rank}, ...}, HoldComplete[body], <\|...\|>] is made by Compile (the representation differs from Wolfram's register code) and applied to arguments: declared types are checked and coerced (_Real accepts integers and exact reals, _Complex any number, _Integer integers only, True \| False Booleans, rank-n full arrays), results are machine numbers, and non-conforming arguments fall back to ordinary evaluation (documented behaviour); RuntimeAttributes -> Listable threads over extra list levels. A wrong argument count raises ValueError and a malformed object TypeError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation examples) and agreement with N of the uncompiled expression in tests. |
| `CompilerEnvironment` | added | 3 | option of FunctionCompile: Automatic (use $CompilerEnvironment) or a CompilerEnvironmentObject whose declarations are available to the compiled function; other values raise ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation AddTwo example) in tests. |
| `CompilerEnvironmentAppendTo` | added | 6 | CompilerEnvironmentAppendTo[decls] appends FunctionDeclaration/TypeDeclaration/OperationDeclaration objects (one or a list) to $CompilerEnvironment, CompilerEnvironmentAppendTo[env, decls] to env; gives the environment. Declarations are validated when appended (bad types raise ValueError, unsupported kinds NotImplementedError when used). Check: reference (Wolfram documentation AddTwo examples) in tests. |
| `CompilerEnvironmentObject` | added | 3 | CompilerEnvironmentObject[<\|"ID" -> id, ...\|>] is a collection of declarations made by CreateCompilerEnvironment (or $CompilerEnvironment); env["Declarations"] lists them and env[TargetSystem] gives the stored target list ({} when none). An unknown id raises ValueError. Check: exact (registry contents) in tests. |
| `CompilerOptions` | added | 3 | option of FunctionCompile: Automatic or an association of pipeline settings (accepted; there is no compilation pipeline, so results are unchanged); other values raise ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) in tests. |
| `CompilerRuntimeErrorAction` | added | 4 | option of FunctionCompile for low-level runtime errors (integer overflow of the inferred integer result type): Automatic or "Evaluate" give the exact evaluated result (Wolfram's rerun), None gives Failure["RuntimeError", <\|..., "MessageParameters" -> {"IntegerOverflow"}\|>], f gives f[failure]. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation UnsignedInteger8 example) in tests. |
| `CreateCompilerEnvironment` | added | 16 | CreateCompilerEnvironment[] gives a new, empty CompilerEnvironmentObject[<\|"ID" -> n\|>]; the TargetSystem option is accepted (Inherited, Automatic, All, a system name or a list) and stored, since no machine code is generated. Other options raise ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and environments kept separate in tests. |
| `ForAllType` | added | 9 | ForAllType[x, type], ForAllType[x, cond, type] and ForAllType[{x1, ...}, cond, type] are inert polymorphic types for declarations: FunctionCompile binds the variables from the argument types and checks cond (Element/NotElement with a list of types or the abstract types "Integers", "SignedIntegers", "UnsignedIntegers", "Reals", "RealFloatingPoint", "Numbers", "Complex", "Ordered", "Strings", or TypeEvaluate[...]). Malformed forms raise TypeError/ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation polyFunc and addtwo examples) in tests. |
| `FunctionCompile` | added | 55 | FunctionCompile[f], FunctionCompile[{f1, ...}], FunctionCompile[<\|k -> f, ...\|>], FunctionCompile[decls, f] and FunctionCompile[decls, name] give CompiledCodeFunction objects; f is Function[{Typed[x, type], ...}, body] with types "Integer8"..."Integer128", "UnsignedInteger8"..."UnsignedInteger64", "MachineInteger", "Real32", "Real64", "ComplexReal64", "Boolean", "String", "InertExpression", TypeSpecifier["PackedArray"][t, r], TypeSpecifier["ListVector"][t], function types {...} -> t; declarations are FunctionDeclaration (with ForAllType, SequenceType, LiteralType, TypeEvaluate) and TypeDeclaration["Macro"\|"Alias", ...]. Calling checks each argument against its type (integers are accepted for reals) and gives the documented Failure["ArgumentCount", ...] or Failure["ArgumentType", ...] otherwise; the body is evaluated with IfCompiled taking its compiled branch, TypeHint/Typed giving their value and TypeOf the inferred type; exact non-integer results become machine numbers. Integer overflow of an inferred integer result type follows CompilerRuntimeErrorAction (Automatic/"Evaluate": the exact result, as Wolfram's rerun gives; None: Failure["RuntimeError", ...]; f: f[failure]). Options CompilerEnvironment, CompilerOptions, ProgressReporting, TargetSystem and UseEmbeddedLibrary are accepted (no machine code is generated). Product/abstract types, OperationDeclaration, KernelFunction and DownValuesFunction raise NotImplementedError; untyped parameters ValueError. Deviation: the "PackedArray"::[...] input syntax is not parsed; write TypeSpecifier["PackedArray"][...]. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation examples) and agreement with the uncompiled Function in tests. |
| `FunctionDeclaration` | added | 19 | FunctionDeclaration[name, Typed[{t1, ...} -> t]@Function[{x1, ...}, body], "Inline" -> ...] is a validated, inert declaration used by FunctionCompile and CompilerEnvironmentAppendTo; several declarations of one name with different types are overloads, ForAllType makes them polymorphic and SequenceType variadic. Malformed declarations raise TypeError/ValueError; KernelFunction and DownValuesFunction bodies NotImplementedError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation AddTwo, VarArgsAdd and ForAllType examples) in tests. |
| `IfCompiled` | added | 3 | IfCompiled[comp, uncomp] (HoldAll) evaluates uncomp when evaluated and comp inside FunctionCompile code, never both. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation example: "uncompiled" evaluated, "compiled" from FunctionCompile) in tests. |
| `LiteralType` | added | 3 | LiteralType[x] (x an integer, string or Boolean) is an inert literal type, e.g. the rank in TypeSpecifier["PackedArray"]["MachineInteger", LiteralType[2]] or a string argument type in a declaration; other x raise TypeError, a symbol stays unevaluated. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation examples) in tests. |
| `OperationDeclaration` | added | 3 | Partial. OperationDeclaration["type", "op", Typed[...]@Function[...]] is a validated, inert declaration; using it in FunctionCompile raises NotImplementedError because product types are not supported. Malformed declarations raise TypeError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation form) in tests. |
| `SequenceType` | added | 4 | SequenceType[var] is an inert type for zero or more trailing arguments in a declaration (FunctionCompile passes them on as a Sequence, as in Wolfram's VarArgsAdd example); var must be a symbol (TypeError otherwise). Check: reference (Wolfram documentation VarArgsAdd example) in tests. |
| `TargetSystem` | added | 4 | option of CreateCompilerEnvironment and FunctionCompile naming the machine architectures to target: Inherited/Automatic/All, a name from $TargetSystems or a list of them; CreateCompilerEnvironment stores it (env[TargetSystem] gives the list) and other strings raise ValueError. No code is generated, so results do not depend on it. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation: env[TargetSystem] gives {"Windows-x86-64"}) in tests. |
| `TypeDeclaration` | added | 8 | Partial. TypeDeclaration[kind, name, ...] is a validated, inert declaration (kinds "Product", "Abstract", "Alias", "Macro"); FunctionCompile uses "Macro" and "Alias" declarations as type names and raises NotImplementedError for product and abstract types (CreateTypeInstance is not available). Malformed declarations raise ValueError/TypeError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation fooInteger example) in tests. |
| `TypeEvaluate` | added | 4 | TypeEvaluate[expr] is an inert type computed by evaluating expr with the type variables of the enclosing ForAllType replaced by their literal values (e.g. a rank r + 1), also usable as a ForAllType condition; a result that is not a literal or TypeSpecifier raises ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation addRank example) in tests. |
| `TypeHint` | added | 3 | TypeHint[expr, type] gives expr when evaluated (the type, validated, only matters in compiled code, where FunctionCompile also gives expr); an unknown type raises ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation example TypeHint[1, "UnsignedInteger8"]) in tests. |
| `TypeOf` | added | 9 | TypeOf[expr], TypeOf[expr, Typed[x, t]], TypeOf[expr, {Typed[x, t], ...}] and TypeOf[expr, decls] (HoldFirst) infer the compiler type of expr without evaluating it and give TypeSpecifier[type]: literals (integers Integer64, reals Real64, complexes ComplexReal64, strings, Booleans), typed variables, arithmetic with the usual promotion (integer division and elementary functions give Real64), comparisons and logic (Boolean), StringLength/Length (Integer64), If, Module/With, lists, Range and Table (PackedArray), Dot, Total, Function with typed parameters ({...} -> t) and calls to declared functions. Expressions outside this subset raise NotImplementedError; bad types ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation examples) and the types of FunctionCompile results in tests. |
| `TypeSpecifier` | added | 14 | TypeSpecifier[type] represents a type (as TypeOf returns it) and TypeSpecifier[cons][t1, ...] a compound type ("PackedArray", "NumericArray", "ListVector" here; Tabular types such as TypeSpecifier["Date"][...] belong to the Tabular functions and are left alone); both stay as they are. A malformed native type inside TypeSpecifier[type] raises ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and FunctionCompile argument checks in tests. |
| `Typed` | added | 66 | Typed[x, type] annotates x with a compiler type and stays as it is when evaluated (Function[{Typed[x, t]}, body] binds x like a plain parameter, as documented; FunctionCompile uses the types); Typed[type] is an operator form: Typed[type][f] gives Typed[f, type]. The type is validated structurally (a string name, which may come from a TypeDeclaration, a function type, a compound or literal type); anything else raises ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation: Function[{Typed[x, "Real64"]}, x + 1]["two"] gives 1 + "two") in tests. |

### external interfaces: foreign functions (W30)

| Function | Status | Cases | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CreateForeignCallback` | added | 10 | CreateForeignCallback[f, {argtypes...} -> rettype] makes a C function pointer (ctypes CFUNCTYPE) that evaluates f on the converted arguments and converts the result to rettype; gives ManagedObject[ForeignCallback[f, type, <\|"FunctionPointer" -> OpaqueRawPointer[addr]\|>], ...]. A result of the wrong type raises TypeError when the callback is called (re-raised by the ForeignFunction call). The callback stays alive for the session. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and libc qsort with a comparison callback in tests. |
| `CreateManagedObject` | added | 7 | Partial. CreateManagedObject[expr, free] gives ManagedObject[expr, expr, free, <\|"ID" -> n\|>] (the ID is MikoshiLang's handle; Wolfram shows three arguments) and CreateManagedObject[expr, man] one sharing man's base value and freeing function. MikoshiLang has no reference counting, so the freeing function is never called automatically (this is the partial part); UnmanageObject deactivates the object. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation: man["Value"] is foo) in tests. |
| `ForeignCallback` | added | 3 | ForeignCallback[f, type, <\|"FunctionPointer" -> ...\|>] (made by CreateForeignCallback) is passed to foreign functions as a function pointer; properties "Function", "FunctionPointer" and "Type". An object whose pointer was not made by CreateForeignCallback raises ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and qsort in tests. |
| `ForeignFunction` | added | 4 | ForeignFunction[file, name, <\|"FunctionPointer" -> ..., "Type" -> ...\|>] (made by ForeignFunctionLoad) calls the C function: arguments are checked against the C types (wrong types raise TypeError like Wolfram's ForeignFunction::argtype, out-of-range integers ValueError); pointer arguments accept RawPointer, OpaqueRawPointer, ManagedObject and ForeignCallback; errors raised inside callbacks are re-raised after the call. A wrong argument count raises ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and libc results compared with Python (abs, strlen, toupper, qsort) in tests. |
| `ForeignFunctionLoad` | added | 25 | ForeignFunctionLoad[lib, "fun", {argtypes...} -> rettype] and ForeignFunctionLoad[ptr, type] (ptr from ForeignPointerLookup) load a C function with ctypes and give ForeignFunction[file, name, <\|"Type" -> ..., "FunctionPointer" -> OpaqueRawPointer[addr]\|>]. C types: "Integer8"..."Integer64", "UnsignedInteger8"..."UnsignedInteger64", "CUnsignedChar", "CSignedChar", "CShort", "CUnsignedShort", "CInt", "CUnsignedInt", "CLong", "CUnsignedLong", "CSizeT", "CFloat", "CDouble", "OpaqueRawPointer", TypeSpecifier["RawPointer"][t] and "Void" (result only); struct types raise NotImplementedError. Missing libraries or symbols raise ValueError, unknown pointers ValueError. Deviation: the "RawPointer"::[t] input syntax is not parsed. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and libc results (abs, strlen, atoi, toupper) compared with Python in tests. |
| `ForeignPointerLookup` | added | 6 | ForeignPointerLookup[lib, "sym"] gives OpaqueRawPointer[addr] for a symbol of a C-compatible library (lib a name resolved with ctypes.util.find_library, e.g. "c", or a path), like dlsym. A missing library or symbol raises ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and the address matching ForeignFunctionLoad's "FunctionPointer" in tests. |
| `ManagedObject` | added | 3 | Partial. ManagedObject[base, value, free, <\|"ID" -> n\|>] (made by CreateManagedObject, RawMemoryAllocate, RawMemoryExport and CreateForeignCallback) has properties "Value", "BaseValue", "FreeingFunction" and "Active"; functions expecting pointers unwrap it. The freeing function is not run automatically (no reference counting); RawMemoryFree frees managed memory explicitly. An unknown ID raises ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation property examples) in tests. |
| `NullRawPointerQ` | added | 6 | NullRawPointerQ[ptr] is True when the address of a RawPointer, OpaqueRawPointer or managed pointer is 0 and False otherwise (also False for non-pointers, as a predicate). Check: reference (Wolfram documentation: NullRawPointerQ[OpaqueRawPointer[0]] is True) in tests. |
| `OpaqueRawPointer` | added | 10 | OpaqueRawPointer[addr] is an untyped pointer (void*), as returned by ForeignPointerLookup; OpaqueRawPointer[ptr] casts a typed pointer; property "Address". A negative or non-integer address raises TypeError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) in tests. |
| `RawMemoryAllocate` | added | 14 | RawMemoryAllocate[type] and RawMemoryAllocate[type, n] allocate zeroed memory for one or n elements of a C type (sizes from ctypes) and give ManagedObject[RawPointer[addr, type], ...]; n must be a positive integer (ValueError) and type a known C type (ValueError). Check: reference (Wolfram documentation CInt and CFloat examples) and round trips in tests. |
| `RawMemoryExport` | added | 27 | RawMemoryExport[expr] copies a string (encoded, NUL-terminated, type "UnsignedInteger8") or a ByteArray into new memory, RawMemoryExport[expr, type] a number or a list of numbers of a C type; gives ManagedObject[RawPointer[addr, type], ...]. Option CharacterEncoding (default "UTF-8"). Values that do not fit the type raise ValueError/TypeError; NumericArray raises NotImplementedError (not available). Check: reference (Wolfram documentation: RawMemoryExport[-1, "CInt"] reads back -1) in tests. |
| `RawMemoryFree` | added | 4 | RawMemoryFree[ptr] frees memory from RawMemoryAllocate/RawMemoryExport (the start address of the block) and gives Null; later reads raise ValueError. Freeing other or already freed memory raises ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and the ValueError after freeing in tests. |
| `RawMemoryImport` | added | 15 | RawMemoryImport[ptr, "String"] reads a NUL-terminated string, {"String", n} n bytes, {"ByteArray", n} a ByteArray and {"List", n} n elements of the pointer's type; option CharacterEncoding (default "UTF-8"). Only MikoshiLang-allocated memory can be read (ValueError otherwise, including a missing terminator or a length past the block); {"NumericArray", n} raises NotImplementedError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation: "A string" bytes {65, 32, 115, ...}) in tests. |
| `RawMemoryRead` | added | 11 | RawMemoryRead[ptr] and RawMemoryRead[ptr, offset] read the element of the pointer's type at the given element offset (integers exact, CFloat/CDouble as reals, pointer elements as RawPointer). Only memory from RawMemoryAllocate/RawMemoryExport may be read: other addresses and out-of-bounds offsets raise ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation: CInt -1 round trip, string bytes) in tests. |
| `RawMemoryWrite` | added | 8 | RawMemoryWrite[ptr, val] and RawMemoryWrite[ptr, val, offset] store val as the pointer's element type at the element offset and give the (unmanaged) RawPointer; integers out of the type's range, wrong value types (TypeError) and addresses outside MikoshiLang-allocated blocks (ValueError) are rejected. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation: write 65 to "a string" gives "A string") in tests. |
| `RawPointer` | added | 12 | RawPointer[addr, type] is a typed pointer (made by RawMemoryAllocate, RawMemoryExport, UnmanageObject or a foreign function returning TypeSpecifier["RawPointer"][type]); properties "Address" and "Type"; RawPointer[ptr, type] casts a pointer. The address must be a non-negative integer and the type a C type (ValueError/TypeError otherwise). Check: reference (Wolfram documentation) and round trips through RawMemoryWrite/RawMemoryRead in tests. |
| `UnmanageObject` | added | 8 | UnmanageObject[man] deactivates the ManagedObject man (man["Active"] becomes False) and gives its value; deactivating twice raises ValueError, a non-managed argument TypeError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation: UnmanageObject[man] gives foo and man["Active"] becomes False) in tests. |

Check: exact; ReadString round trips and FileByteCount in tests. |

The default irreducible is the Conway polynomial |

| `FiniteFieldElementNorm` | added | 5 | FiniteFieldElementNorm[a] is the absolute norm (an integer 0..p-1, the product of the conjugates of a); [a, k] the norm relative to the p^k-element subfield (an element of FiniteField[p, k], identified through the standard embedding); [a, emb] relative to an embedding |

| `FromFiniteFieldIndex` | added | 5 | FromFiniteFieldIndex[ind, ff] = ff[ind]; listable in ind (vectors and matrices of indices) |

### graphics: rendering (W14)

| Function | Status | Cases | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Rasterize` | added | 44 | Rasterize[g, "Data"] the pixel array (integers 0-255, top row first, {r, g, b} or {r, g, b, a} with Background -> None) of a 2D Graphics drawn with matplotlib; Rasterize[g, "RasterSize"] its {width, height}; Rasterize[g, {elem1, ...}] a list. Options ImageSize (points, default 360 wide; Tiny/Small/Medium/Large), RasterSize (pixels), ImageResolution (dpi, default 72) and Background. Drawn: Point, Line, Polygon, Rectangle, Disk, Circle (and sectors), Text, Arrow, Raster, GraphicsComplex, GraphicsGroup, Style, Annotation, Translate/Rotate/Scale, colours, Opacity, Thickness, PointSize, Dashing, EdgeForm, FaceForm, CapForm, JoinForm, Arrowheads[s], Directive; PlotRange, PlotRangePadding, AspectRatio; and, through the W15 hooks (wl_plot_options), Axes, AxesOrigin, AxesLabel, AxesStyle, Ticks, TicksStyle, Frame, FrameLabel, FrameStyle, FrameTicks, FrameTicksStyle, GridLines, GridLinesStyle, PlotLabel, RotateLabel, LabelStyle, Epilog and Prolog. Anything else (Graphics3D, gradient fillings, insets, unsupported option settings, ...) raises NotImplementedError rather than being left out; Rasterize[g] / "Image" needs the Image object (image batch W21) and raises NotImplementedError until then. Pixels approximate, not reproduce, Wolfram's renderer. Requires matplotlib and numpy (NotImplementedError otherwise); symbolic input stays unevaluated. Check: self-check of the raster shape against RasterSize, and pixel read-back of filled regions in tests. |

| Function | Status | Cases | Notes |

| `BetweennessCentrality` | fixed | 9 | Graph or edge-rule input: list of unnormalised betweenness centralities in VertexList order (machine reals; directed graphs count ordered pairs; EdgeWeight respected); legacy: {v -> c} unnormalised betweenness (Wolfram BetweennessCentrality); legacy returned NetworkX's normalised values; exact rationals (Brandes, unweighted) |
| `BipartiteQ` | verified | 3 | 2-colourability test (BFS) |
| `ChromaticNumber` | fixed | 4 | exact chromatic number by backtracking (legacy used a greedy colouring, an upper bound only); graphs with more than 40 vertices raise |
| `ClusteringCoefficient` | fixed | 3 | ClusteringCoefficient[g] = mean local clustering (vertices of degree < 2 count 0, as Wolfram MeanClusteringCoefficient), [g, v] local coefficient; exact rationals (legacy floats) |
| `ConnectedComponents` | fixed | 9 | Graph or edge-rule input: connected components (strongly connected for directed graphs), largest first, vertices in VertexList order; legacy: components largest first (Wolfram), vertices in order of appearance; legacy returned NetworkX set order |
| `ConnectedQ` | verified | 3 | True when the graph is connected |
| `Dijkstra` | fixed | 3 | {v -> distance} for every reachable vertex, in vertex order |
| `GraphCenter` | fixed | 7 | vertices of minimum eccentricity; disconnected graphs raise; legacy: vertices of minimum eccentricity; disconnected graphs raise (legacy returned {} silently) |
| `GraphDiameter` | fixed | 8 | maximum eccentricity (Infinity when not (strongly) connected); weighted with EdgeWeight; legacy: maximum eccentricity; Infinity for disconnected graphs (legacy returned None) |
| `GraphRadius` | fixed | 7 | minimum eccentricity (Infinity when not (strongly) connected); legacy: minimum eccentricity; Infinity for disconnected graphs (legacy returned None) |
| `MaximalMatching` | verified | 3 | a maximum-cardinality matching (NetworkX max_weight_matching with unit weights), edges sorted; requires NetworkX |
| `MinimumSpanningTree` | fixed | 3 | edges of a minimum spanning forest (Kruskal, weights {u, v, w} supported); legacy needed NetworkX |
| `PageRank` | fixed | 3 | {v -> rank} PageRank with damping 0.85 treating each edge as two directed links (power iteration to 1e-12, matches NetworkX); legacy required NetworkX |
| `PathLength` | fixed | 3 | (weighted) shortest-path distance, Infinity when unreachable; unknown vertices raise |
| `ShortestPath` | fixed | 4 | vertex list of a shortest (weighted) path, {} when unreachable (Wolfram FindShortestPath); unknown vertices raise |
| `SpanningTree` | fixed | 3 | edges of a spanning forest (Kruskal) |
| `VertexDegree` | fixed | 15 | VertexDegree[g] = degrees in VertexList order, VertexDegree[g, v]; self-loops count 2, multi-edges counted; directed: in + out; legacy: number of incident edges (self-loops count twice, multi-edges counted); unknown vertices raise |

### image processing (W28)

| Function | Status | Cases | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `BilateralFilter` | added | 7 | BilateralFilter[data, σ, μ] replaces every element by the average of its neighbours within radius Round[5σ/2] (smaller neighbourhoods at the boundaries) weighted by the sampled Gaussian e^(-\|offset\|²/2σ²) times e^(-\|value difference\|²/2μ²), as documented (multichannel images use the Euclidean distance between pixel vectors). MaxIterations -> n repeats the filter n times (default 1). Arrays give machine reals, images a real type. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation example) in tests. |
| `Binarize` | added | 7 | Binarize[image] gives a "Bit" image with 1 where the grayscale value exceeds FindThreshold[image] (Method option as for FindThreshold); Binarize[image, t] uses t; Binarize[image, {t1, t2}] marks values with t1 <= v <= t2; Binarize[image, f] marks pixels for which f[v] is True (v the value, or the channel list of a multichannel pixel). Multichannel images are converted to grayscale first (luminance for RGB). Arrays raise TypeError (Binarize works on images); f returning a non-Boolean raises ValueError. Check: reference (direct comparisons with the threshold) in tests. |
| `BottomHatTransform` | added | 4 | BottomHatTransform[data, ker] = Closing[data, ker] - data (the documented definition), BottomHatTransform[data, r] with BoxMatrix[r]. ker is a flat structuring element (an array of 0s and 1s with odd dimensions, rank of the data) or r for BoxMatrix[r]; data is an Image/Image3D (every channel separately) or a numeric array of any rank (exact input stays exact). Even-sized or non-0/1 kernels raise NotImplementedError; symbolic entries stay unevaluated. Check: exact (data + BottomHatTransform == Closing) in tests. |
| `Closing` | added | 5 | Closing[data, ker] is the dilation by ker followed by the erosion by the reflected ker; Closing[data, r] uses BoxMatrix[r]. ker is a flat structuring element (an array of 0s and 1s with odd dimensions, rank of the data) or r for BoxMatrix[r]; data is an Image/Image3D (every channel separately) or a numeric array of any rank (exact input stays exact). Padding as for Dilation/Erosion. Even-sized or non-0/1 kernels raise NotImplementedError; symbolic entries stay unevaluated. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation example) and the identities Closing >= data, idempotence in tests. |
| `CommonestFilter` | added | 6 | CommonestFilter[data, r] replaces every element by the most common value of its range-r neighbourhood (smaller neighbourhoods at the boundaries), CommonestFilter[data, {r1, ...}] per dimension. If several values are commonest and the centre is one of them, the centre is kept, as documented; otherwise the first commonest value in scan order is used (Wolfram picks a random one). Arrays may hold any expressions (compared structurally); images: the commonest pixel vector, type kept. Non-integer radii raise NotImplementedError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation examples) in tests. |
| `ComponentMeasurements` | added | 11 | ComponentMeasurements[image, prop], [{image, lmat}, prop] and [lmat, prop] give {1 -> v1, 2 -> v2, ...} for the components (connected nonzero pixels of an image, CornerNeighbors -> True by default, or the labels of lmat); {prop1, ...} gives lists; ComponentMeasurements[..., prop, crit] keeps components for which crit (a pure function of #1, #2, ... and #name) is True; format "ComponentList" (default), "ComponentAssociation", "PropertyAssociation" or "ComponentPropertyAssociation". Supported properties: Count, Centroid, Medoid, Mean/Max/MinCentroidDistance, BoundingBox, BoundingBoxArea, PerimeterCount, PerimeterPositions, Neighbors, NeighborCount, AdjacentBorders, AdjacentBorderCount, and on images Min, Max, Mean, Median, StandardDeviation, Total (per channel; Byte/Bit16 values normalised to 0..1, as documented), the ...Intensity versions, Data, IntensityData, IntensityCentroid, Entropy (base E), Energy; LabelCount and Dimensions are global. Positions use the standard image coordinate system (pixel centres at half-integers, y up). Other properties (Area, the ellipse, convex hull, contour and shape properties, ...) raise NotImplementedError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation Count examples; hand-computed centroids and boxes) in tests. |
| `ContourDetect` | added | 6 | ContourDetect[data] marks the zero elements and the positive elements with a negative neighbour (CornerNeighbors -> True (default) or False); ContourDetect[data, delta] treats \|x\| < delta as 0; CornerNeighbors -> None works on the dual grid (a 2^d block is marked when it contains a zero or both signs), as documented. Images use the mean intensity and give a "Bit" image; arrays give 0/1 arrays (the documented SparseArray output is given as a normal array). Check: reference (Wolfram documentation examples) in tests. |
| `CornerNeighbors` | added | 9 | option of MorphologicalComponents, MaxDetect, FillingTransform, ComponentMeasurements, CrossingDetect, ... choosing 8 / 26 (True) or 4 / 6 (False) neighbours; an inert option name. Check: reference (used by the W28 heads in tests). |
| `CrossingDetect` | added | 8 | CrossingDetect[data] marks the positive elements with at least one negative neighbour (CornerNeighbors -> True (default): 8 / 26 neighbours, False: 4 / 6); CrossingDetect[data, delta] first treats values with \|x\| < delta as 0; CornerNeighbors -> None works on the dual grid (one element per 2^d block, marked when the block has both signs), as documented. Images use the mean intensity and give a "Bit" image (unsigned types never cross zero); arrays give 0/1 arrays (the documented SparseArray output is given as a normal array). Check: reference (Wolfram documentation examples) in tests. |
| `DeleteBorderComponents` | added | 5 | DeleteBorderComponents[image] removes (sets to background) the connected components of the nonzero pixels that touch the border; DeleteBorderComponents[m] replaces labels of a label matrix that occur on the border with 0. CornerNeighbors -> True (default) or False for images. Arrays must hold non-negative integers (ValueError otherwise). Check: reference (Wolfram documentation example) in tests. |
| `DeleteSmallComponents` | added | 7 | DeleteSmallComponents[image] removes the connected components of nonzero pixels (CornerNeighbors -> True by default) whose element count is at most a threshold chosen from the component sizes (Method -> "Cluster": FindThreshold of the list of sizes, the default; "Mean"; "Median"); with fewer than two distinct sizes nothing is removed. DeleteSmallComponents[x, n] removes components of n or fewer elements. A label matrix (non-negative integers) is handled per label. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation examples) in tests. |
| `Dilation` | added | 9 | Dilation[data, ker] gives max over the 1s k of ker of data(x + k) (Wolfram's orientation, checked on the documented asymmetric example); Dilation[data, r] uses BoxMatrix[r]. ker is a flat structuring element (an array of 0s and 1s with odd dimensions, rank of the data) or r for BoxMatrix[r]; data is an Image/Image3D (every channel separately) or a numeric array of any rank (exact input stays exact). Padding: images 0 (the default), a number, or None; data arrays ignore the outside (smaller neighbourhoods). Even-sized or non-0/1 kernels raise NotImplementedError; symbolic entries stay unevaluated. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation examples) in tests. |
| `DistanceTransform` | added | 12 | DistanceTransform[image] gives a "Real32" image whose foreground pixels (intensity > 0; > t for DistanceTransform[image, t]; multichannel: the mean intensity) hold the exact distance in pixels to the nearest background pixel, background 0. An image without background (Padding -> 1) raises ValueError. Check: reference (distances worked out by hand and brute force) in tests. |
| `EntropyFilter` | added | 6 | EntropyFilter[data, r] replaces every element by the entropy -Sum[p Log[p]] of the tally of its distinct values (natural logarithm, as Entropy) of its range-r neighbourhood (a (2r+1)^n block), EntropyFilter[data, {r1, ..., rn}] uses a radius per dimension; at the boundaries the neighbourhoods are smaller, as documented. data is a numeric array of any rank (exact input gives exact results, machine input machine numbers) or an Image/Image3D (radii {rows, columns}); images: every channel separately on the 0..1 values, real result type. Padding: images 1 (the default), a number, or None; data arrays ignore the outside. Even-sized or non-0/1 kernels raise NotImplementedError; symbolic entries stay unevaluated. | `Threshold` | added | 8 | Threshold[data] = Threshold[data, {"Hard", 10^-10}]; Threshold[data, δ] and {tfun, δ, ...} with the documented functions: "Hard" (0 for \|x\| <= δ), "Soft" (sgn(x)(\|x\| - δ)), "Firm" {δ, r, p}, "PiecewiseGarrote" (x - δ^2/x), "SmoothGarrote" {δ, n} (x^(2n+1)/(x^(2n) + δ^(2n)), n a positive integer), "Hyperbola" (sgn(x) Sqrt[x^2 - δ^2]); {"LargestValues", k} keeps the k largest absolute values (ties: the first in scan order). δ may be a function applied to the data (Abs of the values) or a FindThreshold method ("Cluster", "Mean", "Median", {"BlackFraction", b}) applied to the absolute values. Check: exact in tests. |
| `DominantColors` | added | 5 | DominantColors[image, n] clusters the pixel colours in LAB (k-means, k-means++ seeded deterministically; images with at most n distinct colours give exactly those) and returns the cluster colours (mean colour; RGBColor, or GrayLevel for grayscale images) ordered by size; DominantColors[image] is supported only for images with at most 12 distinct colours (the automatic cluster count is undocumented, otherwise NotImplementedError). Properties "Color", "LABColor", "HexRGBColor", "Count", "Coverage", "CoverageImage" (a "Bit" mask) or a list of them; MinColorDistance -> d merges clusters closer than d (ColorDistance, the larger keeping its colour); DistanceFunction for that merge. Method, ColorCoverage, Masking and output formats other than Automatic/"List" raise NotImplementedError. On natural images the clusters can differ from Wolfram's (undocumented method). Check: reference (images built from known colours) in tests. |
| `HistogramTransform` | added | 4 | HistogramTransform[image] equalises each channel (reference UniformDistribution[{0, 1}]); HistogramTransform[image, ref] matches the histogram of ref (an image, a list of values or a distribution with a numeric InverseCDF) by mapping the n equally spaced quantiles (default 256) of the image linearly onto those of ref; HistogramTransform[image, ref, n]; HistogramTransform[{x1, x2, ...}, ...] transforms values. Quantiles are numpy's linear-interpolation quantiles, so values can differ slightly from Wolfram's. Same type as the input (integer types clipped). Check: self-check (the transfer function is monotone, else ArithmeticError) and reference (equalised quantiles) in tests. |
| `HistogramTransformInterpolation` | added | 4 | HistogramTransformInterpolation[data] gives the piecewise-linear InterpolatingFunction (via Interpolation with InterpolationOrder -> 1) that maps the n equally spaced quantiles of data (default 256) onto those of UniformDistribution[{0, 1}] (the empirical CDF), or of ref in HistogramTransformInterpolation[data, ref] and [data, ref, n]; data may be a list of values or an image (one function per channel for multichannel images). HistogramTransform applies the same map. Check: self-check (monotone, else ArithmeticError) and exact (f[quantile] = reference quantile) in tests. |
| `Image` | added | 363 | Image[data] for a matrix of reals (one channel), an array of channel lists or a matrix of colour directives (RGB, with alpha when any colour has opacity); Image[data, type] with type "Bit", "Byte", "Bit16" (data must then be integers in the type's range, else ValueError), "Real32" (default) or "Real64"; options ColorSpace (Automatic gives "RGB" for 3 or 4 channels, Automatic otherwise; a space must match the channel count, with one extra channel taken as alpha) and Interleaving (False: channels first). Image[image, type] converts the type (rounding and clipping to integer types), Image[image, ColorSpace -> cs] relabels; Image[NumericArray[...]] takes the type from the array; Image[Raster[array]] reverses the rows (Raster rows run bottom up); Image[graphics] is Rasterize[graphics, "Image"] (needs matplotlib). The canonical form Image[data, type, ColorSpace -> cs, Interleaving -> True \| None] is inert. Display options (ImageSize, ImageResolution, MetaInformation, ...) raise NotImplementedError; real images are stored at double precision also for "Real32". Symbolic data stays unevaluated; ragged or non-finite data raises ValueError, non-numeric data TypeError. Check: exact (round trips through ImageData; reference values from the Image/ImageType documentation) in tests. |
| `Image3D` | added | 20 | Image3D[data] for a 3D array of reals (slices top to bottom, rows back to front, columns left to right) or of channel lists; Image3D[{image1, image2, ...}] stacks 2D images of equal size (largest type); types, ColorSpace and Interleaving as for Image. The canonical form Image3D[data, type, ColorSpace -> cs, Interleaving -> ...] is inert. Rendering options (ViewPoint, BoxRatios, ...) raise NotImplementedError. Check: exact (round trips through ImageData and Image3DSlices) in tests. |
| `Image3DProjection` | added | 6 | Image3DProjection[image] = Image3DProjection[image, Bottom, "Max"] projects onto the x-y plane (along the slices; the result's top row is the back row); modes "Max" (colour of the pixel of maximum intensity), "MaxIntensity" (maximum of the grayscale volume), "Mean" (per channel) and "MeanIntensity". Other directions (their image orientation is not documented) raise NotImplementedError. Check: exact (constant volumes; single bright voxel) in tests. |
| `Image3DSlices` | added | 7 | Image3DSlices[image] lists the slices (top to bottom) as 2D images; Image3DSlices[image, n], {s1, s2, ...}, m ;; n and All; Image3DSlices[image, spec, d] slices along dimension d (1 slices, 2 rows back to front, 3 columns), each 2D image keeping the remaining axes in order. Image3D[Image3DSlices[i]] == i. Check: exact (round trip through Image3D) in tests. |
| `ImageAccumulate` | added | 4 | ImageAccumulate[image] gives, per channel, the sum of all pixel values below and to the left of (and including) each pixel, padded with a row of zeros at the bottom and a column of zeros on the left, so the result is 1 + ImageDimensions[image] in size, as documented; real result type. Method -> "CompensatedSummation" is accepted (the sums are exact for integer types, double precision otherwise). Image3D raises NotImplementedError. Check: exact (differences of the result give back the image) in tests. |
| `ImageAdd` | added | 7 | ImageAdd[image, x1, x2, ...] adds the operands to each channel value. Operands: images of the same dimensions (a single-channel image is applied to every channel of the other; different channel counts raise ValueError; different dimensions NotImplementedError), numbers, colours (converted to the image's colour space) or channel lists; folds over several operands and accepts a single list. Alpha channels are kept from the first image. The result has the largest type of the images; integer types are clipped to 0..1, real types are not. For "Bit" images it is the logical OR. Check: exact (pixelwise sums) in tests. |
| `ImageAdjust` | added | 5 | ImageAdjust[image] rescales each colour channel from its own min..max to 0..1; ImageAdjust[image, c], {c, b} and {c, b, gamma} apply Clip[(b + 1)(c + 1) x^gamma - c/2, {0, 1}] (the documented formula; zero adjustment {0, 0, 1}); ImageAdjust[image, corr, {inmin, inmax}] first rescales inmin..inmax to 0..1 and ImageAdjust[image, corr, {inmin, inmax}, {outmin, outmax}] to outmin..outmax (clipped), Automatic meaning the channel minimum or maximum, per-channel lists allowed for every parameter. Colour images in spaces other than Grayscale/RGB are converted to RGB first; alpha is kept; type kept. A constant channel rescales to 0. Check: exact (ImageAdjust[i, -2] == ColorNegate[i], documented formula) in tests. |
| `ImageApply` | added | 5 | ImageApply[f, image] applies f to each pixel's channel list (a number for single-channel images) on the 0..1 scale and builds an image from the results (numbers or equal-length lists; colours give their RGB values); ImageApply[f, {image1, image2, ...}] passes the corresponding pixels as a sequence (largest type). Interleaving -> False applies f to each channel value. Evaluations are cached on the pixel value, as Wolfram allows. Integer types are clipped. Masking raises NotImplementedError. Check: exact (identity and closed-form maps) in tests. |
| `ImageApplyIndexed` | added | 4 | ImageApplyIndexed[f, image] applies f[pixel, {row, column}] (row 1 at the top; {slice, row, column} for Image3D) and builds an image from the results; ImageApplyIndexed[f, {image1, ...}] gives f[p1, p2, ..., {row, column}]. Interleaving -> False passes single channel values with {row, column, channel}. Check: exact in tests. |
| `ImageAspectRatio` | added | 4 | ImageAspectRatio[image] gives height/width as an exact rational (of the slices for Image3D). Check: exact in tests. |
| `ImageAssemble` | added | 6 | ImageAssemble[{{im11, ..., im1n}, ...}] and ImageAssemble[{im1, im2, ...}] (one row) join 2D images with commensurate sizes (equal heights along a row, equal widths down a column); the result has the largest type and a common colour space (grayscale with RGB gives RGB). Fitting methods, Missing[] tiles, Spacings, PaddingSize and Background raise NotImplementedError; incommensurate sizes raise ValueError. Check: exact (array concatenation) in tests. |
| `ImageChannels` | added | 6 | ImageChannels[image] gives the number of channels including alpha (1 grayscale, 2 grayscale + alpha, 3 RGB, 4 RGBA or CMYK, ...). Check: exact in tests. |
| `ImageClip` | added | 5 | ImageClip[image] clips channel values to [0, 1]; ImageClip[image, {min, max}] to [min, max] (per-channel lists allowed); ImageClip[image, {min, max}, {vmin, vmax}] gives vmin below min and vmax above max. Type kept. Check: exact in tests. |
| `ImageColorSpace` | added | 10 | ImageColorSpace[image] gives the colour space name or Automatic (no colour space; Image[data] of 1, 2 or 5+ channels). Check: exact in tests. |
| `ImageCompose` | added | 6 | ImageCompose[image, overlay] alpha-blends (Duff-Porter "over") an overlay image centred on image; {overlay, alpha} multiplies the overlay's opacity by alpha; ImageCompose[image, overlay, pos] puts the overlay centre at pos and [image, overlay, pos, opos] puts point opos of the overlay at pos, positions being pixel offsets {x, y} from the bottom-left, Scaled[{sx, sy}] or named positions; a list of overlays is composed in turn. The result has image's size, type and colour space (the overlay is converted) and an alpha channel only if image has one. Half-pixel offsets are rounded down (undocumented in Wolfram). Graphics, text and expression overlays and compositing fractions other than {1, 1, 1} raise NotImplementedError. Check: exact (opaque overlays copy pixels; alpha blends re-computed) in tests. |
| `ImageConvolve` | added | 5 | ImageConvolve[image, ker] convolves every channel with the kernel (a numeric matrix with odd dimensions, centred, or a single-channel image), equal to ListConvolve[ker, ArrayPad[data, Floor[Dimensions[ker]/2], "Fixed"]] as documented; Padding -> "Fixed" (default), "Periodic", "Reflected", "Reversed", a value or colour, or None (smaller image). The result has a real type. Kernels with an even dimension and 3D images raise NotImplementedError. Check: reference (direct sums written in tests). |
| `ImageCooccurrence` | added | 4 | ImageCooccurrence[image, n, ker] gives the n x n matrix of the relative frequencies (total 1) of intensity bin pairs {i, j}: a pixel in bin i (centre of the kernel) and a neighbour in bin j at each nonzero kernel offset, weighted by the kernel value; intensities (luma for colour images) on the 0..1 scale fall into n equal bins (1 in the last). The default kernel of ImageCooccurrence[image, n] is not given in the documentation text and raises NotImplementedError; ImageCooccurrence[{image1, image2}, ...] and Masking too. Check: exact (frequencies of hand-counted pairs) in tests. |
| `ImageCorrelate` | added | 4 | ImageCorrelate[image, ker] correlates every channel with the kernel (no flip; odd dimensions, centred); ImageCorrelate[image, ker, f] uses f in place of Dot: EuclideanDistance, SquaredEuclideanDistance, ManhattanDistance, CosineDistance, CorrelationDistance or NormalizedSquaredEuclideanDistance (the Wolfram definitions applied to the kernel and each neighbourhood). Padding as for ImageConvolve; real result type. Other functions, even kernels and 3D images raise NotImplementedError. Check: reference (direct sums written in tests; ImageCorrelate[i, k] == ImageConvolve[i, Reverse[k, {1, 2}]]). |
| `ImageCrop` | added | 7 | ImageCrop[image] removes the uniform borders found by BorderDimensions (tolerance 0.02); ImageCrop[image, size] with size w (height from the aspect ratio, rounded half to even), {w, h}, each dimension d, UpTo[d], {dmin, dmax}, Automatic or Full, removing or adding pixels symmetrically; ImageCrop[image, size, spec] with spec a side, Center, {side1, side2} or fractions {ax, ay} in [-1, 1]. With an odd number of pixels to remove symmetrically the extra pixel comes from the right/top (Wolfram does not document this). Added pixels use Padding (default 0). 2D only. Check: exact (array slicing, sizes verified) in tests. |
| `ImageData` | added | 181 | ImageData[image] gives the pixel array, top row first (channel lists for multichannel images, plain values for one channel): integers 0/1 for "Bit", values normalised to 0..1 for "Byte" and "Bit16", the raw values for real types. ImageData[image, type] converts ("Byte" gives Round[255 v] clipped to 0..255, real types the 0..1 scale); Automatic gives the stored values. Options Interleaving -> False (channels first) and DataReversed -> True (bottom row first). Wolfram files ImageData as needing curated data; it is implemented here because the image batches need it. Check: exact (round trips Image <-> ImageData) in tests. |
| `ImageDifference` | added | 4 | ImageDifference[image1, image2] gives \|image1 - image2\| per channel for images of equal dimensions (a single-channel image is compared with every channel of the other); largest type; for "Bit" images the logical XOR. Check: exact (symmetry and \|a - b\|) in tests. |
| `ImageDimensions` | added | 22 | ImageDimensions[image] gives {width, height} ({width, depth, height} for Image3D). Non-images raise TypeError. Check: exact in tests. |
| `ImageDistance` | added | 4 | ImageDistance[image1, image2] for images of the same dimensions gives DistanceFunction (default EuclideanDistance) of the flattened channel values (0..1 scale; a single-channel image is replicated to the other's channel count): any of EuclideanDistance, SquaredEuclideanDistance, ManhattanDistance, ChessboardDistance, CosineDistance, CorrelationDistance, NormalizedSquaredEuclideanDistance, BrayCurtisDistance, CanberraDistance (evaluated by the library functions of those names), "MeanEuclideanDistance" and "MeanSquaredEuclideanDistance" (mean over pixels of the per-pixel channel distance), or a function f[img1, img2] of the two images. Images of different dimensions and positions, the other named measures and Masking raise NotImplementedError. Check: reference (direct formulas in tests) and delegated (the named distance functions). |
| `ImageFileApply` | added | 5 | ImageFileApply[f, inputfile, outputfile] applies f to each pixel's channel list (0..1 scale; Interleaving -> False: each channel value) as ImageApply does and writes the result to outputfile, returning outputfile. Files are read and written with Pillow (optional: without it NotImplementedError); PNG, JPEG and single-frame TIFF in Pillow modes 1, L, LA, RGB, RGBA, CMYK, P and I;16 are supported, the output keeping the input's format, type and dimensions. Omitting outputfile ($WolframDocumentsDirectory) and Method suboptions raise NotImplementedError; results must have the input's channel count. Check: exact (round trip of a PNG written and read back) in tests. |
| `ImageFileFilter` | added | 4 | ImageFileFilter[f, inputfile, r, outputfile] applies f to the range-r neighbourhood of each pixel in each channel (as ImageFilter, Padding "Fixed" by default; {r_rows, r_columns}; Interleaving -> True passes channel lists) and writes outputfile, returning it. Files are read and written with Pillow (optional: without it NotImplementedError); PNG, JPEG and single-frame TIFF in Pillow modes 1, L, LA, RGB, RGBA, CMYK, P and I;16 are supported, the output keeping the input's format, type and dimensions. Padding -> None is not supported (as in Wolfram). Omitting outputfile raises NotImplementedError. Check: exact (Max filter of a written PNG re-read) in tests. |
| `ImageFileScan` | added | 7 | ImageFileScan[f, inputfile] evaluates f on each pixel's channel list (0..1 scale; Interleaving -> False: each channel value) row by row from the top left, as ImageScan does, and returns Null. Files are read and written with Pillow (optional: without it NotImplementedError); PNG, JPEG and single-frame TIFF in Pillow modes 1, L, LA, RGB, RGBA, CMYK, P and I;16 are supported, the output keeping the input's format, type and dimensions. Check: exact (pixel values collected with Sow/Reap match the file) in tests. |
| `ImageFilter` | added | 4 | ImageFilter[f, image, r] applies f to the (2r + 1) x (2r + 1) neighbourhood matrix of each pixel in each channel (values on the 0..1 scale); ImageFilter[f, image, {r_rows, r_columns}]; Padding -> "Fixed" (default), "Periodic", "Reflected", "Reversed", a value or None; Interleaving -> True passes matrices of channel lists and expects channel lists back. f must return numbers (lists with Interleaving -> True). Results are cached on the neighbourhood. Same type as the image (integer types clipped). Masking and 3D images raise NotImplementedError. Check: exact (Mean/Max filters against direct computations) in tests. |
| `ImageForwardTransformation` | added | 4 | ImageForwardTransformation[image, f] moves the pixel at p to f[p] (coordinates {{0, 1}, {0, h/w}} by default, DataRange Full/explicit), giving an image of the same size (or [image, f, w \| {w, h}]) with Background Black (0). For TransformationFunction[m] or a matrix the map is inverted exactly and sampled bilinearly (Method Automatic, "Interpolated"); for other functions Method -> None assigns each pixel to the nearest output pixel (later pixels win). Interpolating arbitrary forward maps (the default for general f) raises NotImplementedError since Wolfram's interpolation scheme is not documented; PlotRange other than Automatic too. Check: exact (identity and translations) in tests. |
| `ImageLevels` | added | 4 | ImageLevels[image] gives, per channel, {{lev1, k1}, {lev2, k2}, ...} with 256 equally spaced levels over the channel range ({0, 1}; the documented CIE ranges for XYZ/LAB/LCH/LUV images) where k_i counts lev_i <= v < lev_(i+1) and the last level counts v >= lev_n ("IncludeOutOfRange": values below the range go to the first bin, above to the last; "ExcludeOutOfRange" drops them); "Bit" images give {{0, n0}, {1, n1}}. ImageLevels[image, n], [image, All] (tally of the distinct values), [image, "Byte"] (256 levels after conversion to bytes) and [image, bspec, {min, max}]. A single-channel image gives one list, others a list per channel. Automatic binning raises NotImplementedError. Check: exact (counts total the pixel count) in tests. |
| `ImageMarker` | added | 5 | ImageMarker[pos], ImageMarker[pos, marker] and ImageMarker[{pos1, ...}, ...] are inert HighlightImage specifications: positions {x, y}, Scaled/ImageScaled/Offset forms or named positions, markers an image, graphics, any expression or a named shape ("Arrow", "Circle", "CircleBullet", "Cross", "GrayPoint", "OpenCross", "Point", "Star"); the expression stays unevaluated, unknown shape names raise ValueError. (HighlightImage itself is not implemented.) Check: reference (documented forms) in tests. |
| `ImageMeasurements` | added | 5 | ImageMeasurements[image, prop] for the global properties "AspectRatio", "Channels", "ColorSpace", "DataType", "Dimensions", "ImageDimensions", "Interleaving", "Transparency"; per-channel "Min", "Max", "MinMax", "Mean", "Median", "StandardDeviation" (n - 1), "Total", "Entropy" (natural log over the distinct values) and "Energy" (sum of squared value frequencies) on the 0..1 scale (a number for one channel, else a list); intensity properties ("MinIntensity", ..., "TotalIntensity", "IntensityCentroid" in image coordinates) use the Rec. 601 luma of colour images and the channel mean for ColorSpace Automatic. A list of properties gives a list; format "List", "Association" or "RuleList"; "Properties" lists the names; images lists map. Contour, "Skew", "DataRange" and "SampleDepth" raise NotImplementedError. Check: exact (agreement with Mean, Median, Total of ImageData) in tests. |
| `ImageMultiply` | added | 5 | ImageMultiply[image, x1, x2, ...] multiplies each channel value by the operands. Operands: images of the same dimensions (a single-channel image is applied to every channel of the other; different channel counts raise ValueError; different dimensions NotImplementedError), numbers, colours (converted to the image's colour space) or channel lists; folds over several operands and accepts a single list. Alpha channels are kept from the first image. The result has the largest type of the images; integer types are clipped to 0..1, real types are not. For "Bit" images it is the logical AND. Check: exact (pixelwise products) in tests. |
| `ImagePad` | added | 18 | ImagePad[image, m] pads every side with m black (0) pixels; ImagePad[image, m, padding] with padding a value, colour, channel list, "Fixed" (edge pixels repeated, corners copied), "Periodic" (cyclic repetition), "Reflected" (mirror without repeating the edge) or "Reversed" (mirror repeating the edge); ImagePad[image, {{left, right}, {bottom, top}}, ...]; negative widths remove pixels. 3D images take one width for every side. Padding a "Bit" image with a non-binary value gives "Real32"; integer types are rounded. Automatic and "TextureSynthesis" padding raise NotImplementedError. Check: exact (array padding; ImagePad[ImagePad[i, m], -m] == i) in tests. |
| `ImagePartition` | added | 7 | ImagePartition[image, s], [image, {w, h}] and [image, {w, h}, {dw, dh}] give the matrix of subimages (rows of tiles from the top), dropping incomplete tiles; ImagePartition[image, {s}] keeps incomplete tiles at the right/bottom edges. UpTo/Scaled/range tile specifications and Padding raise NotImplementedError; 2D only. Check: exact (array slicing; ImageAssemble[ImagePartition[i, s]] == i when s divides the size) in tests. |
| `ImagePerspectiveTransformation` | added | 5 | ImagePerspectiveTransformation[image, m] applies the forward map p -> m.p (2 x 2: linear; 3 x 3: linear fractional) or TransformationFunction[m] to pixel positions in DataRange coordinates (Automatic {{0, 1}, {0, h/w}}), i.e. the output at q samples the input at m^-1 q bilinearly, with the input size (size argument w or {w, h}) and Padding/Background 0 outside. Wolfram's Automatic output size is undocumented (the input size is used); PlotRange, Masking and 3D images raise NotImplementedError; singular matrices raise ValueError. Check: exact (identity matrix gives the image; m then m^-1 round-trips the interior) in tests. |
| `ImageQ` | added | 4 | ImageQ[expr] is True for a valid Image or Image3D object (the canonical form Image[...] evaluates to) and False for anything else, including unevaluated Image[...] calls with symbolic data. Check: exact (structural test) in tests. |
| `ImageRecolor` | added | 7 | ImageRecolor[image, region -> color] and a list of such rules recolour, in HSB, the pixels of the region: a colour (pixels within MaxColorDistance, default 0.1, under DistanceFunction, default CIE76 as in ColorDistance), ColorsNear[...] or a mask image (its values weight the change). Method "BrightnessPreserving" (default: hue and saturation replaced), "SaturationPreserving", "HuePreserving", "Brightness", "Saturation" or "Hue" (the named components replaced). Grayscale images become RGB; integer types are rounded. Wolfram does not document whether region edges are blended, so colour regions are recoloured fully. Marker images and videos raise NotImplementedError. Check: verify (recoloured pixels have the target's hue and the original brightness) in tests. |
| `ImageReflect` | added | 8 | ImageReflect[image] mirrors top-bottom; ImageReflect[image, side] mirrors so side goes to the opposite side; side1 -> side2 interchanges the sides (Top <-> Left and Bottom <-> Right transpose; Top <-> Right and Bottom <-> Left anti-transpose); All mirrors along every axis. 3D images support Top/Bottom, Left/Right, Front/Back (rows of the slices: back first) and All. Check: exact (involution: reflecting twice gives the image) in tests. |
| `ImageResize` | added | 8 | ImageResize[image, w] (height from the aspect ratio, rounded half to even), {w, h}, {w, d, h}, {s} (largest dimension s) and per-dimension d, {d} (at most d), Scaled[s], All and Automatic. Resampling -> "Linear" (bilinear, pixel centres aligned, edges extended) or "Nearest"; the default Automatic averages pixel areas when shrinking and interpolates linearly when enlarging. Wolfram's default resampling filter is not documented, so resized pixel values can differ (sizes agree); named sizes Tiny..Large raise NotImplementedError. Check: exact for identity sizes and constant images; integer shrink factors average blocks, in tests. |
| `ImageRotate` | added | 11 | ImageRotate[image] rotates 90 degrees counterclockwise; ImageRotate[image, theta] (radians, Degree allowed) about the centre, multiples of Pi/2 exactly (array rotation); ImageRotate[image, side] = Top -> side and side1 -> side2. Other angles are resampled bilinearly (Resampling -> "Nearest" or "Linear") onto the smallest enclosing rectangle (size Automatic, rounded up) or the input size (Full) or {w, h}, with Background (default 0) outside; Wolfram's default resampling and rounding are not documented, so pixel values near edges can differ. 3D rotation, Masking, All and cropping sizes raise NotImplementedError. Check: exact for quarter turns (four quarter turns give the image), centre pixel preserved, in tests. |
| `ImageScan` | added | 4 | ImageScan[f, image] evaluates f on each pixel (channel list, or a number for one channel, on the 0..1 scale) row by row from the top left and returns Null; Interleaving -> False scans single channel values. Check: exact (side effects collected with Sow/Reap or assignments) in tests. |
| `ImageSubtract` | added | 6 | ImageSubtract[image, x1, x2, ...] subtracts the operands from each channel value. Operands: images of the same dimensions (a single-channel image is applied to every channel of the other; different channel counts raise ValueError; different dimensions NotImplementedError), numbers, colours (converted to the image's colour space) or channel lists; folds over several operands and accepts a single list. Alpha channels are kept from the first image. The result has the largest type of the images; integer types are clipped to 0..1, real types are not. Check: exact (pixelwise differences; ImageAdd[ImageSubtract[i, j], j] == i for real images) in tests. |
| `ImageTake` | added | 6 | ImageTake[image, rows], ImageTake[image, rows, columns] and ImageTake[image3d, slices, rows, columns] with the standard sequence specifications n, -n, {n}, {m, n}, {m, n, s}, m ;; n, All and UpTo[n]; rows count from the top; indices beyond the image are dropped (elements present are returned); an empty result raises ValueError. Check: exact (array slicing; compared with Take on ImageData) in tests. |
| `ImageTransformation` | added | 8 | ImageTransformation[image, f] (backward mapping): the output pixel centred at p takes the input value at f[p], sampled bilinearly (Resampling -> "Nearest" or "Linear"), positions outside the image giving Padding/Background (default 0; Padding -> "Fixed" extends the edges). Coordinates use DataRange (Automatic {{0, 1}, {0, h/w}}, Full pixel units, or explicit ranges) and PlotRange Automatic; the output has the input size or ImageTransformation[image, f, w \| {w, h}]. f may be a function (evaluated once on symbolic {x, y} and vectorised when possible, else point by point) or TransformationFunction[m]. 3D images, other PlotRange and Masking settings raise NotImplementedError. Wolfram's default resampling is undocumented. Check: exact (identity map gives the image; translations shift pixels) in tests. |
| `ImageTrim` | added | 7 | ImageTrim[image, {{x1, y1}, ...}] gives the smallest subimage containing the points (image coordinates, origin at the bottom-left corner, integer coordinates on pixel corners so they include every pixel they touch); also Point[...], Rectangle[...] and a mask image (bounding box of its nonzero pixels); ImageTrim[image, roi, r] and {rx, ry} add margins; ImageTrim[image, {roi1, roi2, ...}] gives a list. Parts outside the image are dropped (Padding None). Other regions, DataRange and 3D images raise NotImplementedError. Check: exact (array slicing, verified on known boxes) in tests. |
| `ImageType` | added | 14 | ImageType[image] gives "Bit", "Byte", "Bit16", "Real32" or "Real64". Non-images raise TypeError; symbols stay unevaluated. Check: exact in tests. |
| `ImageValue` | added | 6 | ImageValue[image, {x, y}] gives the channel values at image coordinates {x, y} ({0, 0} the bottom-left corner, pixel centres at half-integers) by bilinear interpolation between pixel centres (Resampling -> "Linear", default) or the nearest pixel ("Nearest"; on a boundary the average of the adjacent pixels), with Padding (default 0, a colour or "Fixed") one pixel beyond the edges, so positions near or outside the border mix in the padding as the documented defaults imply; a list of positions gives a list; type argument as for PixelValue; DataRange Full (default), Automatic or explicit ranges. Other resampling methods and spans raise NotImplementedError. Check: exact (equals PixelValue at pixel centres, linear between them) in tests. |
| `ImageValuePositions` | added | 4 | ImageValuePositions[image, val] and ImageValuePositions[image, val, d] give the image coordinates of the centres of the matching pixels (PixelValuePositions - 1/2, as documented). val is a number, a channel list or a colour (converted to the image's space), or "Max" / "Min" for the pixels of largest / smallest intensity (luma for colour images, the channel mean for ColorSpace Automatic); with d, pixels whose channel vector lies within Euclidean distance d of val (0..1 scale) match, otherwise values must be equal. Positions are sorted by x then y. 2D only. Check: exact (the documented relation to PixelValuePositions) in tests. |
| `Interleaving` | added | 8 | option of Image, ImageData, ImageApply, ImageScan, ImageFilter... giving whether channel values are interleaved (True) or planar (False); Image/ImageData honour it and the pixel functions pass whole channel lists or single values accordingly. Inert as an expression. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation settings) in tests. |
| `LinearGradientImage` | added | 4 | LinearGradientImage[gcol, size, type] (default {Black, White}, {150, 150}, "Real32") colours each pixel centre by t = the normalised distance from the line through pos1 perpendicular to pos2 - pos1 (default pos1 = {Left, Center}, pos2 = {Right, Center}), clipped to [0, 1]; LinearGradientImage[{pos1, pos2} -> gcol, ...] with positions {x, y} in image coordinates or named sides. gcol: a colour list (piecewise linear in RGB, or in gray when all colours are GrayLevel, like Blend), {{x1, c1}, ...}, or a function returning colours (GrayLevel, Hue, pure functions, ColorDataFunction). Named ColorData schemes and 3D sizes raise NotImplementedError. Pixels are sampled at their centres, so values can differ from Wolfram's in the last digits. Check: exact (the formula for t, endpoint colours) in tests. |
| `Masking` | added | 3 | option naming a region of interest for image functions; the W21 functions support only the default All (other settings raise NotImplementedError). Inert as an expression. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation settings) in tests. |
| `MaxColorDistance` | added | 19 | option giving the largest colour distance allowed (FindMatchingColor, ColorDetect forms); inert as an expression. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation settings) in tests. |
| `MinColorDistance` | added | 4 | option of DominantColors: clusters whose representative colours are closer than d (by ColorDistance) are merged. Inert as an expression. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation settings) in tests. |
| `PixelValue` | added | 5 | PixelValue[image, {x, y}] gives the channel values (0..1 scale; a number for one channel) of the pixel in column x and row y counted from the bottom (integer coordinates at pixel centres, {1, 1} the bottom-left pixel); a non-integer position gives the nearest pixel and a position on a boundary the average of the adjacent pixels; a list of positions gives a list; PixelValue[image, pos, type] converts ("Byte" gives integers). Positions outside the image raise ValueError (no Padding); spans and marker images raise NotImplementedError; 2D only. Check: exact (agreement with ImageData) in tests. |
| `PixelValuePositions` | added | 4 | PixelValuePositions[image, val] and PixelValuePositions[image, val, d] give the pixel positions {x, y} ({1, 1} the bottom-left pixel) of the matching pixels. val is a number, a channel list or a colour (converted to the image's space), or "Max" / "Min" for the pixels of largest / smallest intensity (luma for colour images, the channel mean for ColorSpace Automatic); with d, pixels whose channel vector lies within Euclidean distance d of val (0..1 scale) match, otherwise values must be equal. Positions are sorted by x then y. 2D only. Check: exact (PixelValue at every returned position matches) in tests. |
| `PreserveColor` | added | 3 | option of ImageRestyle and related functions (not part of W21); inert as an expression. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation settings) in tests. |
| `RadialGradientImage` | added | 4 | RadialGradientImage[gcol, size, type] colours each pixel centre by t = \|p - pos1\| / \|pos2 - pos1\| (default pos1 = Center, pos2 = the top-right corner), clipped to [0, 1]; {pos1, pos2} -> gcol, gcol forms, sizes and types as for LinearGradientImage. Check: exact (the formula for t, symmetry) in tests. |
| `RandomImage` | added | 6 | RandomImage[] = RandomImage[1, {150, 150}]; RandomImage[max], RandomImage[{min, max}] (uniform) and RandomImage[dist] (values from RandomVariate[dist]) with size side, {w, h} or {w, d, h} and type (default "Real32"; integer types round the 0..1 values); ColorSpace -> cs gives that many channels per pixel. Reproducible after SeedRandom (the stream differs from Wolfram's). Check: reference (range, dimensions, type and sample statistics) in tests. |
| `RemoveAlphaChannel` | added | 4 | RemoveAlphaChannel[color] drops the opacity; RemoveAlphaChannel[color, bg] blends c a + bg (1 - a) and gives GrayLevel (both gray) or RGBColor; RemoveAlphaChannel[image] drops the alpha channel (the image itself when it has none) and RemoveAlphaChannel[image, bg] blends with the background colour, giving a Grayscale or RGB image. Check: exact (blend formula) in tests. |
| `ReplaceImageValue` | added | 4 | ReplaceImageValue[image, pos -> val] sets the pixel containing the image-coordinate position pos ({0, 0} the bottom-left corner, {w, h} the top-right; a position on a pixel boundary changes all adjacent pixels; spans set the pixels inside) to val (number, channel list or colour); lists of rules and a type argument as for ReplacePixelValue. DataRange other than Full raises NotImplementedError; positions outside the image raise ValueError. Check: exact (agreement with ReplacePixelValue at pos + 1/2) in tests. |
| `ReplacePixelValue` | added | 4 | ReplacePixelValue[image, pos -> val] sets the pixel at pixel position pos ({x, y} with {1, 1} the bottom-left pixel centre; a position on a boundary changes all adjacent pixels; spans xmin ;; xmax set a block) to val (a number, a channel list or a colour converted to the image's colour space); a list of rules applies them in turn; ReplacePixelValue[image, pos -> val, type] reads val in that type's range ("Byte": 0..255). Type kept (values clipped and rounded for integer types). Positions outside the image raise ValueError. Check: exact (read back with PixelValue) in tests. |
| `SetAlphaChannel` | added | 6 | SetAlphaChannel[color] and SetAlphaChannel[color, a] give the colour with opacity 1 or a (an existing opacity is replaced); SetAlphaChannel[image] = SetAlphaChannel[image, 1]; SetAlphaChannel[image, a] with a number or a single-channel image of the same dimensions (values clipped to 0..1). An Automatic single-channel image becomes "Grayscale"; other Automatic images raise ValueError, as Wolfram requires an explicit colour space. Result type: the larger of the two types (a "Bit" image with fractional opacity becomes "Real32"). Check: exact (AlphaChannel round trip) in tests. |
| `Sharpen` | added | 4 | Sharpen[image] = Sharpen[image, 2]; Sharpen[image, r] is the unsharp mask i + (i - Blur[i, r]) = 2 i - Blur[i, r] (the documented relation; Wolfram does not state its gain, so pixel values can differ), every channel separately; integer types are clipped; "Bit" images give "Real32". Sharpen is linear, as documented. Check: exact (2 i - Blur[i, r]; constant images are unchanged) in tests. |
| `Thumbnail` | added | 5 | Thumbnail[image, n] and Thumbnail[image, UpTo[n]] shrink the image (area averaging) so its larger dimension is n, keeping the aspect ratio; colour images become RGB (alpha kept). An image already within n is returned unresized with Padding -> None or UpTo[n]; Wolfram pads it otherwise, with an undocumented layout, so that raises NotImplementedError, as do Thumbnail[image] (the default size is undocumented), named sizes and files/URLs. Check: sizes and constant images verified in tests. |
| `ZoomCenter` | added | 3 | option of DynamicImage (a front-end display function); inert as an expression. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation settings) in tests. |
| `ZoomFactor` | added | 3 | option of DynamicImage (a front-end display function); inert as an expression. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation settings) in tests. |

| `PfaffianDet` | added | 9 | the Pfaffian of an antisymmetric matrix (Pf[m]^2 == Det[m], 0 for odd dimension): exact and machine numeric matrices by skew-symmetric (Parlett-Reid style) elimination with pivoting, symbolic matrices by expansion along the first row; Method -> Automatic, "ParlettReid", "Householder", "Hessenberg" and "Pauli" give the same value, "Det" gives Sqrt[Det[m]] (sign not conformed, as Wolfram); a non-antisymmetric matrix raises |
| `PolarDecomposition` | added | 5 | {u, p} with m == u.p, u with orthonormal columns (or rows) and p = MatrixPower[ConjugateTranspose[m].m, 1/2] positive semidefinite, via the SVD for machine matrices; exact and arbitrary-precision matrices raise (use N[m]); TargetStructure is accepted, but MikoshiLang has no structured arrays, so the factors are always ordinary (dense) matrices |
| `PopovDecomposition` | added | 14 | PopovDecomposition[m] or PopovDecomposition[m, x] gives {u, p} with u unimodular (Det[u] a nonzero constant), u.m == p and p the Popov form of the univariate polynomial matrix m: each nonzero row's pivot (last entry of highest degree) lies in its own column, pivot degrees increase (ties: leftmost pivot first), other entries of a pivot column have lower degree, and zero rows come last.  The form is unique up to row scaling; here pivots are made monic (Wolfram may normalise rows differently, e.g. to integer coefficients).  Exact rational, complex-rational and symbolic coefficients (then x must be given) work exactly; Modulus -> prime works over GF(p); approximate coefficients are converted to exact rationals, decomposed exactly and returned as machine numbers. |

| `SmithDecomposition` | added | 5 | {u, r, v} with u.m.v == r, u and v unimodular and r the Smith normal form (diagonal, non-negative, each entry dividing the next) for integer matrices; rational matrices are handled by clearing denominators (as Wolfram); the transformation matrices are not unique and can differ from Wolfram's; inexact, Gaussian-integer and symbolic matrices raise; TargetStructure is accepted, but MikoshiLang has no structured arrays, so the factors are always ordinary (dense) matrices |
