### linear algebra (batch 3)

| Function | Status | Cases | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Adjugate` | added | 6 | the adjugate (transposed cofactor matrix), Det[m] Inverse[m] for invertible m, defined for singular m too; exact (machine matrices are computed exactly from their binary values and rounded) |
| `AntihermitianMatrixQ` | added | 3 | m == -ConjugateTranspose[m] (exact; Tolerance / SameTest as for HermitianMatrixQ) |
| `AntisymmetricMatrixQ` | added | 4 | m == -Transpose[m] (exact; Tolerance / SameTest as for HermitianMatrixQ) |
| `ArrayRules` | added | 5 | ArrayRules[array] gives {pos -> value, ...} for the entries that differ from 0 (in lexicographic position order) followed by {_, _, ...} -> 0; ArrayRules[array, default]; works on explicit rectangular arrays (SparseArray evaluates to its dense array in MikoshiLang) |
| `BoxMatrix` | added | 5 | 1s in a box extending r index positions to each side: BoxMatrix[r] is (2r+1) x (2r+1) ones, BoxMatrix[r, w] (w x w, box centred), BoxMatrix[{r1, r2, ...}] and sizes {w1, ...}; integer radii only; an off-centre box (w - 2r - 1 odd) raises |
| `CauchyMatrix` | added | 4 | entries 1/(x_i + y_j) (CauchyMatrix[x] = CauchyMatrix[x, x]), returned as the dense matrix; a zero denominator raises |
| `ConjugateTranspose` | added | 12 | Conjugate[Transpose[m]] (and ConjugateTranspose[m, perm]); a vector or non-array raises like Transpose |
| `CrossMatrix` | added | 3 | 1s on the central row and column (central lines in higher dimensions) extending r positions: CrossMatrix[r] is (2r+1) x (2r+1), CrossMatrix[r, w], CrossMatrix[{r1, ...}]; integer radii only |
| `Det` | fixed | 51 | kernel builtin replaced in batch 3: non-square input raises a clear error (legacy raised SymPy's NonSquareMatrixError), a symbol leaves Det unevaluated (legacy raised TypeError), machine matrices use LAPACK, arbitrary-precision matrices keep their precision, symbolic determinants are expanded |
| `Diagonal` | added | 11 | Diagonal[m] = {m[[1,1]], m[[2,2]], ...} (rectangular matrices too); Diagonal[m, k] is the k-th superdiagonal (k < 0: subdiagonal); entries are returned unevaluated-as-given |
| `DiagonalizableMatrixQ` | added | 5 | m == s.d.Inverse[s] for a diagonal d (over the complex numbers): exact via SymPy; machine matrices test that the eigenvector matrix is well-conditioned (condition number < 10^8) |
| `DiamondMatrix` | added | 4 | 1s where the Manhattan distance from the centre is at most r: DiamondMatrix[r] is (2r+1) x (2r+1), DiamondMatrix[r, w]; integer radii only, equal radii per dimension |
| `Dot` | fixed | 23 | kernel builtin replaced in batch 3: any number of arguments and tensors of any rank (contracts the last index of each factor with the first of the next); symbolic factors leave Dot unevaluated (legacy raised); Dot[x] = x; incompatible shapes raise; infix a.b parses as Dot |
| `DotProduct` | fixed | 5 | MikoshiLang alias of Dot for two vectors (now the batch-3 Dot) |
| `Eigensystem` | added | 6 | {Eigenvalues[m], Eigenvectors[m]} with matching order (decreasing absolute value); Eigensystem[m, k] and UpTo[k]; generalized {m, a} raises |
| `FourierMatrix` | added | 4 | FourierMatrix[n]: entries Exp[2 Pi I (r - 1)(s - 1)/n]/Sqrt[n] (Wolfram's default FourierParameters {0, 1}); exact |
| `HankelMatrix` | added | 5 | HankelMatrix[n] (successive integers, zeros below the antidiagonal), HankelMatrix[c] (first column c, zeros below the antidiagonal), HankelMatrix[c, r] (first column c, last row r; r[[1]] is ignored and c[[-1]] used, as in Wolfram); always a dense matrix |
| `HermitianMatrixQ` | added | 6 | m == ConjugateTranspose[m] (exact zero test; Tolerance -> t for approximate matrices, default 1e-12 at machine precision; SameTest -> f); False for non-matrices |
| `HilbertMatrix` | added | 15 | entries 1/(i + j - 1); HilbertMatrix[n] and HilbertMatrix[{m, n}]; exact (use N for machine numbers) |
| `IndefiniteMatrixQ` | added | 5 | the quadratic form takes both signs (neither positive nor negative semidefinite); the quadratic form is Re[Conjugate[x].m.x], so only the Hermitian part (m + ConjugateTranspose[m])/2 matters (Wolfram); exact matrices use principal minors, machine matrices the eigenvalues of the Hermitian part with a tolerance of n*$MachineEpsilon*max\|eigenvalue\|; False for symbolic matrices unless every sign can be proved, and for non-matrices |
| `Inverse` | fixed | 28 | kernel builtin replaced in batch 3: a symbol leaves Inverse unevaluated (legacy raised), non-square and singular matrices raise clear errors, machine matrices use LAPACK, symbolic entries are cancelled |
| `JordanDecomposition` | added | 6 | {s, j} with m == s.j.Inverse[s] and j in Jordan normal form (exact, SymPy); a machine matrix must be numerically diagonalizable (eigenvector matrix condition number < 10^8) and gives {eigenvectors as columns, diagonal eigenvalues}; otherwise it raises. The order of the Jordan blocks and the scaling of s can differ from Wolfram's (the decomposition is not unique) |
| `LeastSquares` | added | 6 | the x minimising Norm[m.x - b] (minimum-norm solution when several exist, = PseudoInverse[m].b); b a vector or matrix; exact for exact input, LAPACK lstsq for machine input |
| `LeviCivitaTensor` | added | 11 | the rank-d totally antisymmetric tensor (Signature of the index list), as a dense array: LeviCivitaTensor[d] (Wolfram returns the equivalent SparseArray; Normal gives this array) and LeviCivitaTensor[d, List] |
| `LowerTriangularize` | added | 4 | zeros above the k-th diagonal (keeps m[[i,j]] with j - i <= k; default k = 0); rectangular matrices |
| `MatrixForm` | added | 4 | display wrapper: MatrixForm[expr] stays as MatrixForm[expr] and does not affect evaluation of expr (as in Wolfram, it is not a matrix); the text REPL prints it as an aligned grid (matrix_form_text) |
| `MatrixFunction` | added | 7 | MatrixFunction[f, m] for a square matrix and any scalar function f (symbol or pure function): exact via the Jordan form (SymPy analytic_func, derivatives of f on Jordan blocks); machine matrices via the eigendecomposition, which must be well-conditioned (else raises); f is evaluated by MikoshiLang |
| `MatrixMinimalPolynomial` | added | 6 | the monic polynomial p of least degree with p(m) == 0 (exact; Krylov dependence of I, m, m^2, ...); inexact matrices raise |
| `Minors` | added | 9 | Minors[m, k]: determinants of all k x k submatrices, rows and columns subsets in lexicographic order (Wolfram); Minors[m] = Minors[m, Min[Dimensions[m]] - 1]; Minors[m, k, f] applies f instead of Det; Minors[m, 0] = {{1}} |
| `NegativeDefiniteMatrixQ` | added | 3 | Re[Conjugate[x].m.x] < 0 for all non-zero x; the quadratic form is Re[Conjugate[x].m.x], so only the Hermitian part (m + ConjugateTranspose[m])/2 matters (Wolfram); exact matrices use principal minors, machine matrices the eigenvalues of the Hermitian part with a tolerance of n*$MachineEpsilon*max\|eigenvalue\|; False for symbolic matrices unless every sign can be proved, and for non-matrices |
| `NegativeSemidefiniteMatrixQ` | added | 3 | Re[Conjugate[x].m.x] <= 0 for all x; the quadratic form is Re[Conjugate[x].m.x], so only the Hermitian part (m + ConjugateTranspose[m])/2 matters (Wolfram); exact matrices use principal minors, machine matrices the eigenvalues of the Hermitian part with a tolerance of n*$MachineEpsilon*max\|eigenvalue\|; False for symbolic matrices unless every sign can be proved, and for non-matrices |
| `NormalMatrixQ` | added | 4 | m.ConjugateTranspose[m] == ConjugateTranspose[m].m |
| `OrthogonalMatrixQ` | added | 16 | p x q matrix: Transpose[m].m == IdentityMatrix[q] when p >= q, m.Transpose[m] == IdentityMatrix[p] when p <= q (no conjugation, as in Wolfram); options Normalized -> False (only orthogonal columns/rows), Tolerance -> t (infinity norm of the defect), SameTest -> f |
| `Orthogonalize` | added | 9 | Gram-Schmidt orthonormal basis using the standard inner product Conjugate[u].v; the output has as many vectors as the input, linearly dependent vectors become zero vectors; machine vectors whose residual norm is at most 100 $MachineEpsilon (about 2.2*10^-14) of the original are treated as dependent (Tolerance -> t overrides); Orthogonalize[list, f] uses the inner product f on arbitrary elements |
| `Permanent` | added | 5 | sum over permutations of products of entries (SymPy Matrix.per); square matrices |
| `PositiveDefiniteMatrixQ` | added | 12 | Re[Conjugate[x].m.x] > 0 for all non-zero x; the quadratic form is Re[Conjugate[x].m.x], so only the Hermitian part (m + ConjugateTranspose[m])/2 matters (Wolfram); exact matrices use principal minors, machine matrices the eigenvalues of the Hermitian part with a tolerance of n*$MachineEpsilon*max\|eigenvalue\|; False for symbolic matrices unless every sign can be proved, and for non-matrices |
| `PositiveSemidefiniteMatrixQ` | added | 5 | Re[Conjugate[x].m.x] >= 0 for all x; the quadratic form is Re[Conjugate[x].m.x], so only the Hermitian part (m + ConjugateTranspose[m])/2 matters (Wolfram); exact matrices use principal minors, machine matrices the eigenvalues of the Hermitian part with a tolerance of n*$MachineEpsilon*max\|eigenvalue\|; False for symbolic matrices unless every sign can be proved, and for non-matrices |
| `Projection` | added | 8 | Projection[u, v] = (u.Conjugate[v]/v.Conjugate[v]) v; Projection[u, v, f] uses the inner product f[u, v]/f[v, v] v; projection onto the zero vector raises |
| `ReflectionMatrix` | added | 5 | IdentityMatrix[n] - 2 v.ConjugateTranspose[v]/(Conjugate[v].v): reflection in the hyperplane normal to the numeric vector v |
| `RotationMatrix` | added | 17 | RotationMatrix[t] (2D, counterclockwise), RotationMatrix[t, w] (3D, right-handed about the numeric axis w), RotationMatrix[t, {u, v}] (n-D, in the plane of u and v, from u towards v), RotationMatrix[{u, v}] (rotation taking the direction of u to that of v, in their plane; antiparallel vectors raise) |
| `ScalingMatrix` | added | 3 | ScalingMatrix[{s1, ..., sn}] = DiagonalMatrix[{s1, ..., sn}]; ScalingMatrix[s, v] scales by s along the numeric direction v: IdentityMatrix + (s - 1) v.Transpose[v]/v.v |
| `ShearingMatrix` | added | 7 | ShearingMatrix[t, v, n] = IdentityMatrix + Tan[t] Outer[Times, vp, Normalize[n]] where vp is the unit vector along the part of v perpendicular to n (Wolfram uses the projection for non-orthogonal v); determinant 1 |
| `SingularValueList` | added | 16 | non-zero singular values in decreasing order (exact for exact matrices, LAPACK for machine matrices, where values below 100*10^-p times the largest are dropped); SingularValueList[m, k] (k < 0: smallest) and UpTo[k] use all Min[Dimensions[m]] values, zeros included; Tolerance -> t keeps values >= t times the largest; symbolic and generalized {m, a} inputs raise |
| `SparseArray` | added | 27 | SparseArray[{pos -> v, ...}], SparseArray[rules, dims], SparseArray[rules, dims, default] and SparseArray[list] (positions may be patterns such as {i_, i_} -> 1; the first matching rule wins). MikoshiLang has no sparse storage: the result is the equivalent dense array, i.e. Normal[SparseArray[...]] in Wolfram (Head is List, not SparseArray); Band[...] -> v specifications are expanded (see Band) |
| `SquareMatrixQ` | added | 4 | True for a matrix with as many rows as columns, False for anything else |
| `TensorContract` | added | 6 | TensorContract[t, {{s1, s2}, ...}] sums over each pair of slots of an explicit array; the remaining slots keep their order; paired slots must have equal dimensions and appear once |
| `TensorDimensions` | added | 3 | Dimensions of an explicit rectangular array ({} for a number); symbolic tensors stay unevaluated |
| `TensorProduct` | added | 8 | tensor (outer) product of explicit arrays, dimensions concatenated (Outer[Times, a, b] for arrays); numbers act as rank-0 tensors; TensorProduct[t] = t; symbolic factors leave it unevaluated |
| `TensorRank` | added | 4 | the number of indices of an explicit rectangular array (ArrayDepth), 0 for a number; symbols and ragged lists stay unevaluated |
| `TensorTranspose` | added | 4 | TensorTranspose[t, perm] for an explicit array: Transpose[t, perm] with perm a full permutation list of the slots (Cycles specifications are not supported) |
| `ToeplitzMatrix` | added | 6 | ToeplitzMatrix[n] (symmetric, successive integers), ToeplitzMatrix[c] (symmetric, first column c), ToeplitzMatrix[c, r] (first column c, first row r; r[[1]] is ignored and c[[1]] used, as in Wolfram); always a dense matrix (Wolfram's TargetStructure option is not supported) |
| `UnitaryMatrixQ` | added | 5 | as OrthogonalMatrixQ with ConjugateTranspose; options Normalized, Tolerance, SameTest |
| `UpperTriangularize` | added | 5 | zeros below the k-th diagonal (keeps m[[i,j]] with j - i >= k; default k = 0); rectangular matrices |
| `VandermondeMatrix` | added | 5 | rows {1, x_i, x_i^2, ...}: VandermondeMatrix[{x1, ..., xn}] (n x n) and VandermondeMatrix[x, k] (n x k), returned as the dense matrix (Wolfram returns a structured array whose Normal this is); confluent (repeated) nodes raise |

### logic (batch 6)

| Function | Status | Cases | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Boole` | added | 6 | Boole[True] = 1, Boole[False] = 0; other arguments stay unevaluated |
| `BooleanConvert` | added | 22 | forms "DNF"/"SOP" (default), "CNF"/"POS" (minimal two-level forms), "ANF" (unique algebraic normal form, Xor of Ands), "ESOP" (given as the ANF, which is an exclusive sum of products), "NAND", "NOR", "AND", "OR" (two-level with Not); BooleanConvert[expr, form, cond] uses cond as a care set for DNF/CNF; other forms (IMPLIES, ITE, BFF, BDT, binary NAND/NOR) raise |
| `BooleanCountingFunction` | added | 7 | BooleanCountingFunction[kmax, n] (at most kmax True), [{k}, n] (exactly k), [{k1, k2, ...}, n], [{{kmin, kmax}}, n] pure functions; with a variable list gives an equivalent minimal DNF |
| `BooleanFunction` | added | 18 | BooleanFunction[k, n] pure function (truth table IntegerDigits[k, 2, 2^n] in Tuples[{True, False}, n] order; BooleanFunction[8, 2] is And) applied to True/False arguments; BooleanFunction[k, {vars}] and BooleanFunction[table, {vars}] give an equivalent minimal disjunctive normal form; BooleanFunction[table] gives BooleanFunction[k, n] |
| `BooleanTable` | added | 23 | truth values over Tuples[{True, False}, n] (BooleanTable[expr] uses BooleanVariables); nested tables for several variable lists (outermost first); pure BooleanFunction / BooleanCountingFunction / Function; non-Boolean expressions are substituted (BooleanTable[f[a, b], {a, b}]) |
| `BooleanVariables` | added | 5 | the distinct variables (non-connective atoms) of a Boolean expression in canonical order |
| `Conjunction` | added | 3 | Conjunction[expr, {a1, ...}]: And of expr over all True/False values of the a_i, as an equivalent minimal DNF |
| `Disjunction` | added | 3 | Disjunction[expr, {a1, ...}]: Or of expr over all True/False values of the a_i, as an equivalent minimal DNF |
| `Exists` | added | 9 | Exists[x, expr] and Exists[x, cond, expr] (x a symbol or list of symbols); evaluates when the body does not depend on the variables (e.g. Exists[x, True] = True), otherwise stays for Resolve |
| `ForAll` | added | 11 | ForAll[x, expr] and ForAll[x, cond, expr] (x a symbol or list of symbols); evaluates when the body does not depend on the variables (e.g. ForAll[x, True] = True), otherwise stays for Resolve |
| `LogicalExpand` | added | 8 | expands Boolean connectives into a disjunction of conjunctions (distributing And over Or, pushing Not inwards, expanding Xor/Implies/Equivalent), removing contradictory and absorbed terms; equations between lists are split elementwise; non-Boolean atoms (equations, inequalities) are kept as they are (LogicalExpand[x y == 0] is not split into cases) |
| `Majority` | added | 14 | True when more than half of the (odd number of) arguments are True, False when more than half are False; symbolic arguments stay unevaluated unless the count is already decided; an even number of arguments raises |
| `Resolve` | added | 12 | eliminates ForAll/Exists from purely Boolean formulas (variables over Booleans) and returns an equivalent minimal DNF; quantifiers over non-Boolean formulas (real/complex/integer quantifier elimination) raise; quantifier-free input is returned unchanged |
| `SatisfiabilityCount` | added | 9 | number of assignments (of BooleanVariables or the given variables, so extra variables double the count) that make the expression True |
| `SatisfiabilityInstances` | added | 8 | SatisfiabilityInstances[expr, vars], [expr, vars, m], [expr, vars, All] and pure-function forms: lists of truth values that make expr True, enumerated with False before True (lexicographic); {} if unsatisfiable. Wolfram does not document which instances it returns first; every returned instance is valid |
| `SatisfiableQ` | added | 6 | True if some assignment of the variables makes the expression True (exact truth table up to 22 variables, SymPy SAT solver beyond) |
| `TautologyQ` | added | 22 | True if every assignment of the variables makes the expression True |

### messages, exceptions & testing (W02)

| Function | Status | Cases | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$Aborted` | added | 4 | inert symbol: the result of an aborted computation (MemoryConstrained, TimeConstrained, CheckAbort); FailureQ[$Aborted] is True |
| `$AssertFunction` | added | 5 | if set, $AssertFunction[HoldComplete[Assert[test, ...]]] is evaluated when an enabled assertion fails, instead of issuing Assert::asrtf |
| `$Canceled` | added | 3 | inert symbol for a canceled input; Confirm treats it as a failure |
| `$Failed` | added | 16 | inert symbol returned when an operation cannot be done; FailureQ[$Failed] is True |
| `$MessageGroups` | added | 3 | {"name" :> {s::t, ...}, ...} named message groups used by On, Off, Quiet and Check (assignable; the predefined groups list the messages MikoshiLang can issue) |
| `$MessageList` | added | 5 | list of HoldForm[s::t] for messages printed in the session ({} initially; assignable and Block-able; Quiet-ed and switched-off messages are not added) |
| `$MessagePrePrint` | added | 3 | Automatic by default; if set to a function f, message arguments are rendered as f[HoldForm[arg]] |
| `$Messages` | added | 4 | output channels for messages: {OutputStream["stdout", 1]} by default; assign {} to silence messages or OutputStream["stderr", 2] to redirect them |
| `$NewMessage` | added | 3 | if set, $NewMessage[s, "t"] is evaluated when the text of s::t is not defined, and the lookup is retried |
| `$TestFileName` | added | 4 | "" interactively; the absolute file name while TestReport[file] runs the file's tests |
| `$TimedOut` | added | 3 | inert symbol for an operation that timed out |
| `Abort` | added | 10 | Abort[] aborts the computation: it raises AbortSignal ($Aborted), caught by CheckAbort; inside AbortProtect the abort takes effect when the AbortProtect finishes |
| `AbortProtect` | added | 3 | AbortProtect[expr] (HoldAll) evaluates expr completely, saving any Abort[] or TimeConstrained / MemoryConstrained abort until it finishes (a CheckAbort inside still catches them) |
| `AbsoluteTiming` | added | 5 | AbsoluteTiming[expr] (HoldAll) gives {real seconds elapsed while evaluating expr, result} (time.perf_counter) |
| `Assert` | added | 5 | Assert[test] / Assert[test, tag] (HoldAll): disabled by default (returns Null without evaluating test); after On[Assert] a test that is not True issues Assert::asrtf (Assert::asrtfl for a {line, file} tag) or evaluates $AssertFunction[HoldComplete[Assert[...]]] when that is set; returns Null |
| `ByteCount` | added | 4 | ByteCount[expr] gives the bytes MikoshiLang uses to store expr (Python object sizes, every part counted separately, no sharing); symbols (including True, False, Null) are shared and count 0. Values differ from Wolfram's own memory layout, as the documentation allows between systems |
| `CatchExceptions` | added | 8 | CatchExceptions[expr, spec] (HoldFirst) returns expr's value, or for a thrown exception matching spec (All, tag, {tags}, tag -> handler, {tagspec -> handler, ...}; first matching clause; subtypes match their parents) handler[exceptionData] or, without a handler, the exception's Failure; other exceptions propagate. The operator form CatchExceptions[spec][expr] holds expr |
| `Check` | added | 23 | Check[expr, failexpr] / Check[expr, failexpr, msgs] (HoldAll): returns failexpr if expr generated a matching message that is not switched off and not quieted inside the Check; a raised MikoshiLang error counts as the message f::evalerr |
| `CheckAbort` | added | 14 | CheckAbort[expr, failexpr] (HoldAll) returns failexpr if an abort occurs in expr; option PropagateAborts: Automatic (default: absorb Abort[], propagate constraint aborts after failexpr), True (propagate all), False (absorb all) |
| `ClearSystemCache` | added | 5 | ClearSystemCache[] clears MikoshiLang's internal caches (SymPy's cache and the evaluator memo table); ClearSystemCache["Symbolic"] / ["Numeric"] clear the symbolic (SymPy) / numeric (mpmath) caches; returns Null |
| `Confirm` | added | 10 | Confirm[expr] returns expr unless it is a Failure, Missing, $Failed, $Canceled or $Aborted, in which case Failure["ConfirmationFailed", <\|...\|>] is thrown to the lexically enclosing Enclose (info is evaluated only on failure; a ConfirmationFailed failure with Null info is rethrown unchanged); Confirm[expr, info, tag] is caught dynamically by Enclose[..., f, tag]; with no tag and no Enclose: message confirmnotag |
| `ConfirmAssert` | added | 3 | ConfirmAssert[test] returns Null if test is True, else throws Failure["ConfirmationFailed", <\|"MessageTemplate" -> "Assertion failed.", ..., "Test" -> value\|>] to the enclosing Enclose |
| `ConfirmBy` | added | 3 | ConfirmBy[expr, f] returns expr if f[expr] is True, else throws Failure["ConfirmationFailed", ...] with "Expression" and "Function" to the enclosing Enclose; info/tag as for Confirm |
| `ConfirmMatch` | added | 3 | ConfirmMatch[expr, form] returns expr if it matches form, else throws Failure["ConfirmationFailed", ...] with "Expression" and "Pattern" to the enclosing Enclose; info/tag as for Confirm |
| `ConfirmQuiet` | added | 4 | ConfirmQuiet[expr, mspec] evaluates expr and returns it unless a matching message is generated (not switched off and not quieted inside); evaluation stops at the first such message, which is quieted, and Failure["ConfirmationFailed", ...] with "HeldExpression", "HeldMessageName" and "HeldMessageCall" is thrown to the enclosing Enclose; a raised MikoshiLang error counts as f::evalerr |
| `Echo` | added | 12 | Echo[expr] prints >> expr and returns expr; Echo[expr, label] prints >> label  expr; Echo[expr, label, f] prints f[expr]; output is suppressed inside QuietEcho |
| `EchoEvaluation` | added | 4 | EchoEvaluation[expr] (HoldFirst) prints << expr before and >> result after evaluating (nested calls use <<<< / >>>>); EchoEvaluation[expr, l1 -> l2], EchoEvaluation[expr, labels, f] and EchoEvaluation[expr, labels, g -> f] as documented; returns the result |
| `EchoFunction` | added | 3 | operator form: EchoFunction[f][expr] prints >> f[expr], EchoFunction[label, f][expr] prints >> label  f[expr]; both return expr; EchoFunction[][expr] is Echo[expr] |
| `EchoLabel` | added | 3 | operator form: EchoLabel[label][expr] prints >> label  expr and returns expr; EchoLabel[][expr] is Echo[expr] |
| `EchoTiming` | added | 3 | EchoTiming[expr] / EchoTiming[expr, label] (HoldFirst) evaluates expr, prints >> [label  ]seconds and returns the result; Method -> AbsoluteTiming (default), Timing, RepeatedTiming or a holding function returning {timing, result} |
| `Enclose` | added | 23 | Enclose[expr] (HoldAll) evaluates expr; an untagged confirmation lexically inside throws its Failure to it (untagged confirmations are rewritten with a private tag, inner untagged Enclose blocks keep their own); Enclose[expr, f] gives f[failure] (f a string: failure[f]); Enclose[expr, f, form] catches only confirmations whose tag matches form, dynamically |
| `Exception` | added | 9 | Exception[spec] / Exception[spec, payload] builds the validated object Exception[{tags...}, <\|data..., "ExceptionValidated" -> True, "ExceptionAPIVersion" -> "1"\|>] with tag expansion through registered parent types; spec may be a tag, a list of tags, an Exception, a Failure carrying "ExceptionTagList" or an association; malformed input issues Exception::untagged / Exception::invargs and stays unevaluated; exc["prop"] gives the documented properties |
| `ExceptionQ` | added | 7 | ExceptionQ[expr] is True for a validated Exception object; ExceptionQ[expr, tag \| {tags}] also requires one of the tags in its (expanded) tag list |
| `ExceptionTypeRegisteredQ` | added | 4 | ExceptionTypeRegisteredQ[sym] is True if sym is a registered exception type; with a second argument, True if it is registered and one of the given types is among its ancestors |
| `ExceptionTypes` | added | 4 | ExceptionTypes[] / ExceptionTypes[All] lists the registered exception types in registration order; ExceptionTypes[tag \| {tags}] lists the registered types that are the given types or their descendants |
| `Failsafe` | added | 8 | operator form: Failsafe[f][x1, ...] gives f[x1, ...] unless some xi is a failure (Failure, Missing, $Failed, $Canceled, $Aborted), then the first such xi; Failsafe[f, test][...] gives Failure["FailsafeFailed", ...] when test[x1, ...] is not True; Failsafe[f, test, failf] gives failf[...] |
| `Failure` | added | 8 | Failure["tag", assoc] is inert; failure["prop"] gives assoc values and the derived properties "Message" (template applied to "MessageParameters"), "MessageTemplate", "MessageName", "HeldMessageTemplate", "Tag" and "Properties" (sorted); failure[{p1, p2}] gives a list |
| `FailureQ` | added | 6 | FailureQ[expr] is True for Failure[...], $Failed and $Aborted, False otherwise |
| `HandlerFunctions` | added | 9 | option of TestReport: <\|event -> f, ...\|> handlers for the report's events; inert as an expression |
| `HandlerFunctionsKeys` | added | 6 | option of TestReport: the keys of the association passed to the handler functions (Automatic or a list); inert as an expression |
| `IntermediateTest` | added | 6 | IntermediateTest[input, expected, messages, opts] (HoldAllComplete) evaluates a test (without printing messages) and returns the evaluated input; inside VerificationTest / TestEvaluate a failing intermediate test makes the enclosing test fail (IntermediateTestFailure / IntermediateTestMessagesFailure) |
| `Interrupt` | added | 3 | Interrupt[] generates an interactive interrupt: in MikoshiLang (Python) that is KeyboardInterrupt, the same effect as pressing Ctrl-C at that point |
| `MaxMemoryUsed` | added | 3 | MaxMemoryUsed[] gives the peak resident memory (bytes) of the process (getrusage); MaxMemoryUsed[expr] (HoldAll) gives the peak additional Python heap bytes (tracemalloc) used while evaluating expr |
| `MemoryAvailable` | added | 3 | MemoryAvailable[] gives the bytes the operating system reports as available (MemAvailable in /proc/meminfo on Linux, psutil elsewhere) |
| `MemoryConstrained` | added | 5 | MemoryConstrained[expr, b] / MemoryConstrained[expr, b, failexpr] (HoldAll) evaluates expr, aborting it when the additional Python heap memory it allocates (tracemalloc) exceeds b bytes, and returns $Aborted (or failexpr); b may be Infinity or a byte Quantity |
| `MemoryConstraint` | added | 6 | option of the test functions: bytes a test may allocate (default Infinity; exceeding it gives MemoryConstraintFailure); inert as an expression |
| `MemoryInUse` | added | 3 | MemoryInUse[] gives the resident memory (bytes) of the MikoshiLang process (/proc/self/statm on Linux, psutil elsewhere); MemoryInUse[$FrontEnd] raises because there is no front end |
| `Message` | added | 34 | Message[s::t, e1, ...] prints s::t: text (StringForm of the message text with the ei) on $Messages unless switched off or quieted, appends HoldForm[s::t] to $MessageList and returns Null; the text is looked up as s::t, then General::t, then via $NewMessage, else '-- Message text not found --' |
| `MessageName` | added | 4 | s::t (parsed as MessageName[s, "t"], HoldFirst) evaluates to the message text assigned with s::t = "text" or to MikoshiLang's built-in text; otherwise it stays unevaluated |
| `Messages` | added | 4 | Messages[s] gives {HoldPattern[s::t] :> text, ...} for the messages assigned to s (sorted by tag); messages switched off are given as HoldPattern[s::t] :> $Off[text] |
| `Monitor` | added | 3 | Monitor[expr, mon] (HoldAll) evaluates and returns expr; the monitor display is a notebook feature, so in MikoshiLang's text interface nothing is shown (as in a Wolfram text-based session) |
| `Off` | added | 9 | Off[s::t, ...] switches messages off (Off[General::t] switches off every s::t that has not been switched on explicitly); Off["group"] uses $MessageGroups; Off[Assert] disables assertions; Off[s] (tracing) and Off[] are accepted and change nothing because symbol tracing is never on |
| `On` | added | 7 | On[s::t, ...] and On["group"] switch messages back on; On[Assert] enables assertions.  On[s] for symbol tracing is not supported (the evaluator has no per-symbol trace printing) and raises |
| `Pause` | added | 30 | Pause[n] waits at least n seconds (n a non-negative real number or a Quantity of time) and returns Null |
| `Print` | added | 11 | Print[e1, e2, ...] writes the ei concatenated (OutputForm: strings without quotes) and a newline to $Output (stdout) and returns Null |
| `PrintTemporary` | added | 3 | text interface: PrintTemporary[e1, ...] prints like Print (there are no notebook cells to delete afterwards) and returns Null |
| `PropagateAborts` | added | 5 | option name for CheckAbort (Automatic, True or False); used as a function it stays unevaluated |
| `Quiet` | added | 20 | Quiet[expr] / Quiet[expr, moff] / Quiet[expr, moff, mon] (HoldAll): messages in moff are not printed, those in mon are; the innermost Quiet specification for a message wins; Check outside is unaffected. A raised MikoshiLang error is not a message and still propagates |
| `QuietEcho` | added | 3 | QuietEcho[expr] (HoldFirst) evaluates expr without Echo, EchoLabel, EchoFunction, EchoEvaluation or EchoTiming printing anything; messages and Print are not affected |
| `RegisterExceptionType` | added | 9 | RegisterExceptionType[sym] / [sym, parent \| {parents}] (HoldFirst) registers the symbol sym as an exception type in this session and returns Success["RegisteredExceptionType", <\|"ExceptionType" -> sym, "ParentExceptionTypes" -> {...}, "OwnerContext" -> "Global`"\|>]; registering twice issues RegisterExceptionType::regd and returns $Failed |
| `RepeatedTiming` | added | 3 | RepeatedTiming[expr] / RepeatedTiming[expr, t] (HoldFirst) evaluates expr at least 4 times and for at least t seconds (default 1) and gives {trimmed mean of the timings without the lower and upper quartiles, result of the first evaluation} |
| `SameTest` | added | 18 | option of TestCreate / VerificationTest / IntermediateTest / TestReport giving the function that compares the actual and expected outputs (default SameQ); inert as an expression |
| `SessionTime` | added | 3 | SessionTime[] gives the real seconds since the MikoshiLang (Python) process started (procfs on Linux; elsewhere since the library was loaded) |
| `Success` | added | 5 | Success["tag", assoc] is inert; success["prop"] gives assoc values, "Message", "Tag" and "Properties" (the association keys in order) |
| `TerminatedEvaluation` | added | 4 | TerminatedEvaluation["reason"] is the inert representation of an evaluation stopped by a session limit ("IterationLimit", "RecursionLimit", ...); a non-string reason raises |
| `TestCreate` | added | 46 | TestCreate[input] / [input, expected] / [input, expected, messages] (HoldAllComplete) creates an unevaluated TestObject; options MemoryConstraint, MetaInformation, SameTest, TestID (Automatic = hash of the test), TimeConstraint |
| `TestEvaluate` | added | 8 | TestEvaluate[test] runs a TestObject (messages are recorded, not printed) and gives the evaluated TestObject with "ActualOutput", "ActualMessages", timings and the "Outcome" / "FailureType"; TestEvaluate[<\|"Input" :> ..., "ExpectedOutput" -> ..., ...\|>] builds the test from an association |
| `TestEvaluationFunction` | added | 4 | option of TestReport: the function used to evaluate each created test (default TestEvaluate); inert as an expression |
| `TestID` | added | 8 | option of TestCreate / VerificationTest / IntermediateTest: the test's identifier (Automatic = a hash of the test); inert as an expression |
| `TestObject` | added | 4 | TestObject[<\|...\|>] is the inert test result (from TestCreate / TestEvaluate / VerificationTest); test["prop"] for "Outcome" (Success, Failure, MessagesFailure, NotEvaluated), "FailureType", "Input", "ExpectedOutput", "ActualOutput", "ActualMessages", "TestID", "TestKey", "TestCreate", "Created", timings, ...; test[{p1, ...}] gives an association; "Properties" |
| `TestReport` | added | 30 | TestReport[{tests}] / TestReport[test] evaluates the NotEvaluated TestObjects and gives a TestReportObject; TestReport[{reports}] merges reports; TestReport["file.wl"] evaluates a plain-text test file with $TestFileName set (notebooks raise). Options HandlerFunctions (events ReportStarted, TestCreated, TestEvaluated, RuntimeFailure, FileStarted, FileCompleted, ReportCompleted, UnhandledEvent), HandlerFunctionsKeys, TestEvaluationFunction, SameTest, TimeConstraint, MemoryConstraint |
| `TestReportObject` | added | 4 | TestReportObject[<\|...\|>] is the inert result of TestReport; report["prop"] for "Results", "ResultsByOutcome", "ResultsByTestID", "ResultsByTestFileName", "ResultsDataset", "ReportSucceeded", "RuntimeFailures", "Title", timings, "TestsSucceededCount", the key lists ... |
| `ThrowException` | added | 9 | ThrowException[args] throws Exception[args] (to CatchExceptions; Catch[..., _] also intercepts it); malformed arguments throw an "ErrorHandlingException" exception after an Exception:: message; uncaught exceptions reach the top level as an Uncaught Throw error |
| `TimeConstrained` | added | 14 | TimeConstrained[expr, t] / TimeConstrained[expr, t, failexpr] (HoldAll) evaluates expr, aborting it after t seconds of real time and returning $Aborted (or failexpr, evaluated only then); t may be Infinity or a Quantity in seconds; AbortProtect postpones the abort |
| `TimeConstraint` | added | 9 | option of the test functions: seconds a test may run (default Infinity; exceeding it gives TimeConstraintFailure); inert as an expression |
| `TimeRemaining` | added | 3 | TimeRemaining[] gives the seconds (real time) left before the earliest enclosing TimeConstrained aborts, or Infinity outside TimeConstrained |
| `TimeUsed` | added | 4 | TimeUsed[] gives the CPU seconds used so far by the MikoshiLang (Python) process (time.process_time); Pause is not counted |
| `Timing` | added | 4 | Timing[expr] (HoldAll) gives {CPU seconds used by this process while evaluating expr, result} (time.process_time); time spent in Pause is not counted |
| `VerificationTest` | added | 27 | VerificationTest[input, expected, messages, opts] (HoldAllComplete) = TestEvaluate[TestCreate[...]]: evaluates the test immediately without printing messages and gives the evaluated TestObject |
| `WithCleanup` | added | 5 | WithCleanup[expr, cleanup] / WithCleanup[init, expr, cleanup] (HoldAll) returns expr's value and always evaluates cleanup, also after an abort, Throw, Confirm or error in expr; aborts during init and cleanup are postponed until cleanup is done (an abort in init skips expr) |

### number theory

| Function | Status | Cases | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Ackermann` | fixed | 4 | exact closed forms for m <= 3; larger m raise instead of recursing until RecursionError |
| `BaseConvert` | fixed | 4 | BaseConvert[n, from, to] reads the decimal digits of n as base-'from' digits; legacy accepted invalid digits (BaseConvert[19, 2, 10] = 3); now raises. Returns an integer for to = 10, else a digit list |
| `Bell` | fixed | 3 | alias of BellB; legacy truncated non-integer arguments with int(); now exact integers only |
| `BellB` | promoted | 3 | BellB[n] and Bell polynomials BellB[n, x] |
| `BellNumber` | fixed | 3 | alias of BellB; legacy truncated non-integer arguments with int(); now exact integers only |
| `Bernoulli` | fixed | 3 | Bernoulli[1] returned +1/2 (SymPy >= 1.12 convention); Wolfram BernoulliB[1] = -1/2 |
| `BernoulliB` | promoted | 3 | BernoulliB[n] and BernoulliB[n, x] |
| `BernoulliNumber` | fixed | 3 | Bernoulli[1] returned +1/2 (SymPy >= 1.12 convention); Wolfram BernoulliB[1] = -1/2 |
| `CarmichaelLambda` | fixed | 4 | CarmichaelLambda[-n] = CarmichaelLambda[n]; 0 raises; legacy truncated non-integer arguments with int(); now exact integers only |
| `Catalan` | fixed | 5 | Wolfram constant Catalan = 0.915965594177219... (SymPy Catalan; N[Catalan, n] to any precision, Sum[(-1)^k/(2k+1)^2, {k, 0, Infinity}] -> Catalan); Catalan[...] used as a function raises ValueError pointing to CatalanNumber; legacy Catalan[n] gave Catalan numbers |
| `CatalanNumber` | fixed | 6 | exact for any exact argument, symbolic n stays unevaluated; legacy truncated non-integer arguments with int(); now exact integers only |
| `ChineseRemainder` | fixed | 3 | smallest non-negative solution; non-coprime moduli handled; no solution leaves the call unevaluated (legacy returned an Error expression) |
| `CollatzLength` | fixed | 4 | number of terms of CollatzSequence[n] (including n and 1); legacy looped forever for n <= 0 |
| `CollatzSequence` | fixed | 3 | legacy looped forever for n <= 0; now n must be a positive integer |
| `ContinuedFractionConvergents` | fixed | 3 | convergents p/q of [a0; a1, ...] as {p, q} pairs (MikoshiLang); legacy raised for integer convergents |
| `DigitCount` | fixed | 3 | legacy returned the number of digits; Wolfram DigitCount[n] is the list of counts of digits 1, 2, ..., 9, 0; DigitCount[n, b] and DigitCount[n, b, d] also supported |
| `DigitSum` | fixed | 3 | DigitSum[n] and DigitSum[n, b] (sum of base-b digits of \|n\|); legacy truncated non-integer arguments with int(); now exact integers only |
| `DiophantineSolve` | fixed | 3 | legacy called sympy.diophantine.diophantine (AttributeError for every input); now the general integer solution via SymPy diophantine, parameters t0, t1, ... in sorted order |
| `DivisorCount` | fixed | 3 | number of divisors; legacy truncated non-integer arguments with int(); now exact integers only |
| `DivisorSigma` | fixed | 4 | DivisorSigma[k, n] = sum of d^k over divisors of n; exact for any exact k (legacy truncated k) |
| `Divisors` | fixed | 4 | Divisors[-n] = Divisors[n]; 0 raises; legacy truncated non-integer arguments with int(); now exact integers only |
| `EulerE` | promoted | 3 | EulerE[n] and EulerE[n, x] |
| `EulerNumber` | verified | 3 | Euler numbers E_n (E_1 = 0, E_4 = 5) |
| `EulerPhi` | fixed | 4 | EulerPhi[0] = 0 and EulerPhi[-n] = EulerPhi[n] (legacy raised / gave wrong values) |
| `ExtendedGCD` | fixed | 3 | returned {x, y, g}; Wolfram order is {g, {x, y}} with g = a x + b y |
| `FactorInteger` | fixed | 8 | FactorInteger[1] returned {} (Wolfram {{1,1}}), 0 and rationals failed; now {{-1,1},...} for negatives, negative exponents for rationals |
| `Fibonacci` | fixed | 9 | symbolic n raised TypeError (now unevaluated); negative n, real n and Fibonacci[n, x] added |
| `FibonacciNumber` | fixed | 3 | MikoshiLang alias of Fibonacci |
| `FromDigits` | fixed | 12 | now accepts digit strings (letters a-z = 10-35), symbolic digits and digits >= base as Wolfram; legacy silently used base 10 for invalid bases |
| `GCD` | fixed | 7 | now variadic, exact for rationals, GCD[] = 0; legacy truncated reals (GCD[2.5, 5] = 1) |
| `HarmonicNumber` | fixed | 10 | HarmonicNumber[n] for rational n in closed form (HarmonicNumber[1/2] = 2 - 2 Log[2], legacy left it unevaluated); HarmonicNumber[n, r] |
| `IntegerDigits` | fixed | 8 | legacy silently used base 10 for a non-integer base; now IntegerDigits[n], [n, b], [n, b, len] (digits of \|n\|, padded/truncated on the left) |
| `IsPrime` | verified | 4 | MikoshiLang alias of PrimeQ (same kernel implementation) |
| `JacobiSymbol` | fixed | 4 | m must be a positive odd integer (clear error otherwise); legacy truncated non-integer arguments with int(); now exact integers only |
| `JordanTotient` | fixed | 4 | legacy called a SymPy function that does not exist (AttributeError); now J_k(n) = n^k prod(1 - p^-k), JordanTotient[n] = EulerPhi[n] |
| `KroneckerSymbol` | fixed | 4 | legacy called a SymPy function that does not exist (AttributeError); now the full Kronecker symbol (n = 0, even and negative n) |
| `LCM` | fixed | 3 | now variadic, exact for rationals, LCM[] = 1; legacy truncated reals |
| `LegendreSymbol` | fixed | 4 | p must be an odd prime (clear error otherwise); legacy truncated non-integer arguments with int(); now exact integers only |
| `Lucas` | fixed | 3 | MikoshiLang alias of LucasL; negative and real n added; legacy truncated non-integer arguments with int(); now exact integers only |
| `LucasL` | fixed | 8 | LucasL[n, x] Lucas polynomials L_0 = 2, L_1 = x, L_n = x L_(n-1) + L_(n-2) (LucasL[3, x] = x^3 + 3 x); the 2-argument form was missing |
| `ModularInverse` | fixed | 3 | raises a clear error when no inverse exists (legacy leaked a Python ValueError) |
| `MoebiusMu` | fixed | 6 | MoebiusMu[-n] = MoebiusMu[n]; 0 raises |
| `MultiplicativeOrder` | fixed | 7 | raises a clear error when gcd(k, n) != 1; legacy truncated non-integer arguments with int(); now exact integers only |
| `NextPrime` | fixed | 4 | legacy truncated reals and ignored negative primes; now NextPrime[x] is the smallest prime > x (primes include -2, -3, ... as in Wolfram) and NextPrime[x, k] the k-th |
| `PowerMod` | fixed | 10 | negative exponents use the modular inverse and raise when it does not exist; rational exponents raise |
| `Prime` | fixed | 4 | Prime[n] for positive integers only; legacy truncated non-integer arguments with int(); now exact integers only |
| `PrimeFactorization` | fixed | 3 | MikoshiLang alias of FactorInteger |
| `PrimePi` | fixed | 5 | PrimePi[x] for real x counts primes <= x (legacy truncated with int(), wrong for negative floats) |
| `PrimePowerQ` | fixed | 4 | True for p^k with k >= 1; False for 0, 1 and non-integers; negative integers raise (Gaussian/negative conventions not supported); legacy truncated reals |
| `PrimitiveRoot` | fixed | 6 | smallest primitive root; legacy returned None (displayed as nothing) when none exists, now unevaluated like Wolfram |
| `PrimitiveRootQ` | fixed | 3 | PrimitiveRootQ[a, n]: True when a generates the units mod n; False when gcd(a, n) != 1 (legacy raised a SymPy ValueError) |

| `Radical` | fixed | 3 | product of the distinct primes dividing n; Radical[0] raises; legacy truncated non-integer arguments with int(); now exact integers only |
| `RationalReconstruct` | fixed | 3 | legacy used nsimplify, so RationalReconstruct[1.4142135623730951] returned Sqrt[2] (not a rational); now the exact rational with the same decimal digits, simplest within machine precision |

| `NDEigensystem` | added | 7 | NDEigensystem[op, u, region, n] -> {{lambda1, ...}, {u1, ...}} with the eigenvalues as for NDEigenvalues and the eigenfunctions as InterpolatingFunction objects (ifun[x] when u is given as u[x]; two-dimensional InterpolatingFunction[{{a, b}, {c, d}}, ...] on rectangles) normalised to Integrate[Abs[u]^2] == 1 over the region (Clenshaw-Curtis quadrature) with the phase fixed so that the largest nodal value is positive (Wolfram leaves the sign arbitrary). Check: self-check — eigenvalues are compared across two grid resolutions (ArithmeticError on disagreement); tests also verify op[u_i] == lambda_i u_i at sample points and the analytic spectra of Laplacians. |
| `NDEigenvalues` | added | 21 | NDEigenvalues[op, u, {x, a, b}, n] (also u[x], x in Interval[{a, b}], {x, a, b}, {y, c, d} and {x, y} in Rectangle[...], and NDEigenvalues[eqns, u, t, region, n] for time-dependent equations, where D[u, t] -> lambda u and D[u, {t, 2}] -> lambda^2 u) -> the n eigenvalues of smallest magnitude of a linear operator of order at most two (constant or variable coefficients), sorted by increasing absolute value; op may contain Inactive[Div] flux terms and NeumannValue terms, and be given with DirichletCondition, PeriodicBoundaryCondition or periodic two-point equations u[a] == u[b]; no condition = natural (Neumann 0) boundary; Chebyshev spectral collocation (SciPy generalized eigensolver) instead of finite elements, so values agree with Wolfram's to within Wolfram's own discretisation error. Disks and general regions, coupled systems, 3-D and Method settings raise NotImplementedError; inhomogeneous conditions raise ValueError. Check: self-check — the eigenvalues are recomputed on a finer grid and an ArithmeticError is raised unless they agree to 1e-6 (relative). |
| `NeumannBoundaryUnitNormal` | added | 4 | NeumannBoundaryUnitNormal[{x, ...}] (inert symbolic outward unit normal) appears in the values returned by the PDE boundary heads (e.g. MassFluxValue, HeatSymmetryValue) unless "BoundaryUnitNormal" is given; the solvers here require explicit normals or scalar fluxes. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation outputs of the *Value heads) in tests. |
| `NeumannValue` | added | 5 | NeumannValue[g - q u, pred] (inert): in NDSolve / NDEigensystem a term f + NeumannValue[...] on the right-hand side sets the outward flux n.(c Grad u + alpha u - gamma) to g - q u where pred holds (on the left-hand side the sign flips); no condition = NeumannValue[0, ...]; produced by the *Value PDE boundary heads. Check: reference (Wolfram NDEigensystem example -Laplacian + NeumannValue[u, x == 1] -> 0.740174) in tests. |
| `ParametricFunction` | added | 4 | ParametricFunction[{p, ...}, Hold[NDSolveValue[...]]] from ParametricNDSolve / ParametricNDSolveValue: pf[v, ...] solves with the numerical values substituted (symbolic values stay unevaluated, wrong counts and out-of-range values raise ValueError), pf["Parameters"] lists the parameters. Check: delegated (NDSolveValue). |
| `ParametricNDSolve` | added | 5 | ParametricNDSolve[eqns, u, {x, xmin, xmax}, pars] -> {u -> ParametricFunction[...]} (one rule per unknown for systems {u, v}); (u /. sol)[p][x] evaluates NDSolveValue for that unknown with the parameter values substituted; same forms and errors as ParametricNDSolveValue. Check: delegated (NDSolveValue; tests compare with closed-form solutions). |
| `ParametricNDSolveValue` | added | 12 | ParametricNDSolveValue[eqns, u, {x, xmin, xmax}, {p1, p2, ...}] (parameters may be {p, pmin, pmax}) -> ParametricFunction[{p1, ...}, Hold[NDSolveValue[eqns, u, {x, xmin, xmax}, opts]]]; pf[v1, ...] substitutes the numerical parameter values and calls NDSolveValue (initial-value problems with WhenEvent and step options, boundary-value problems), so pf[1.][t] or pf[1.][t0] evaluate the solution; symbolic parameter values stay unevaluated, values outside {pmin, pmax} or the wrong number of values raise ValueError; parameter sensitivities (D with respect to a parameter) are not supported. Check: delegated (NDSolveValue with the parameters substituted; tests compare with closed-form solutions). |
| `PeriodicBoundaryCondition` | added | 4 | PeriodicBoundaryCondition[k u[x], pred, f] (inert): in 1-D NDEigensystem / NDSolve boundary-value problems identifies u at the end point where pred holds with k u at the other end f[x] (and the fluxes likewise); 2-D periodic conditions raise NotImplementedError. Check: reference (Bloch spectrum (n + alpha/(2 Pi))^2 for k = Exp[I alpha]) in tests. |
| `PoissonPDEComponent` | added | 3 | PoissonPDEComponent[vars, pars] -> Inactive[Div][IdentityMatrix[n] . Inactive[Grad][u, X], X] - f with "PoissonSourceTerm" f (default 1) and "RegionSymmetry"; time-dependent vars add no time term (as documented). Check: reference (Wolfram documentation: PoissonPDEComponent[{u[x], {x}}, <\|\|>] -> -1 + Inactive[Div][{{1}} . Inactive[Grad][u[x], {x}], {x}]) in tests. |
| `PrecisionGoal` | added | 7 | PrecisionGoal -> p (option): honoured by NDSolve / NDSolveValue (relative tolerance max(10^-p, 2.3*10^-14)) ; accepted by NIntegrate / FindRoot. Check: numeric cross-check in tests (looser goals take fewer NDSolve steps). |
| `ReactionPDETerm` | added | 3 | ReactionPDETerm[vars, a] and [vars, a, pars] -> a u (systems: {Sum[a_ij u_j]} for an m x m matrix a); symbol keys of pars are substituted (ReactionPDETerm[{u[x], {x}}, a, <\|a -> 2\|>] -> 2 u[x]); a list coefficient for a single variable raises ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation forms). |
| `SchrodingerPDEComponent` | added | 4 | SchrodingerPDEComponent[vars, pars] -> -I hbar D[Psi, t] (time-dependent vars) + Inactive[Div][-(hbar^2/2) (1/m) . Inactive[Grad][Psi, X], X] + V Psi with "Mass" m (scalar, or a matrix used elementwise as 1/m_ij), "SchrodingerPotential" V, "ReducedPlanckConstant" hbar or "PlanckConstant" h (hbar = h/(2 Pi)); the default hbar is exact (h = 662607015*10^-42); "MagneticVectorPotential" and "AzimuthalQuantumNumber" settings other than the defaults raise NotImplementedError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation forms, hbar^2/2 = 662607015^2/(8 Pi^2 10^84)) in tests. |
| `SolidBoundaryLoadValue` | added | 5 | SolidBoundaryLoadValue[pred, vars, pars] and SolidBoundaryLoadValue[pred, vars, pars, lkey] (lkey: a key of pars holding a localized association, or an association) -> {NeumannValue[p_i - k u_i - c D[u_i, t], pred], ...} (zero components omitted as NeumannValue[0, pred]) for a "Pressure" (traction) vector p, "SpringConstant" k and "DampingConstant" c (time vars); pars as for the PDE component; symbol keys are substituted; unknown keys raise ValueError; non-association pars raise TypeError. "Force", "NormalForce" (need the boundary area) and "NormalPressure" raise NotImplementedError; "DampingConstant" without time vars raises ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation forms) in tests. |
| `SolidDisplacementCondition` | added | 3 | SolidDisplacementCondition[pred, vars, pars] and SolidDisplacementCondition[pred, vars, pars, lkey] (lkey: a key of pars holding a localized association, or an association) -> DirichletCondition[{u == d1, v == d2, w == d3}, pred] with "Displacement" {d1, d2, d3} (default 0; None entries leave that component free); pars as for the PDE component; symbol keys are substituted; unknown keys raise ValueError; non-association pars raise TypeError. A displacement of the wrong length raises ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation forms) in tests. |
| `SolidFixedCondition` | added | 3 | SolidFixedCondition[pred, vars, pars] and SolidFixedCondition[pred, vars, pars, lkey] (lkey: a key of pars holding a localized association, or an association) -> DirichletCondition[{u == 0, v == 0, ...}, pred] (all displacements fixed); pars as for the PDE component; symbol keys are substituted; unknown keys raise ValueError; non-association pars raise TypeError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation forms) in tests. |
| `SolidMechanicsPDEComponent` | added | 7 | SolidMechanicsPDEComponent[{{u, v, w}, {x, y, z}}, pars] for linear elastic isotropic 3-D solids: rows -Div[sigma(u)]_i - f_i (+ rho D[u_i, {t, 2}] for time vars, - rho omega^2 u_i for frequency vars) written, as Wolfram does, as Sum_j Inactive[Div][-C_ij . Inactive[Grad][u_j, X], X] with (C_ij)_kl = lambda d_ik d_jl + mu (d_ij d_kl + d_il d_jk); any two of "YoungModulus", "PoissonRatio", "LameParameter", "ShearModulus", "BulkModulus", "PWaveModulus" (pairs that do not fix the Lame parameters uniquely raise NotImplementedError), "MassDensity", "BodyLoad" f, "BodyLoadValue" g (adds -rho g); 2-D plane stress/strain forms, other material models/symmetries, "Material" entities and eigenmode analysis raise NotImplementedError. Check: Activate compared with the Navier-Cauchy equations (lambda + mu) Grad[Div[u]] + mu Laplacian[u] in tests. |
| `SolidMechanicsStrain` | added | 5 | SolidMechanicsStrain[vars, pars, displ] -> SymmetrizedArray of the infinitesimal strains of displacement displ = {du, dv, dw} in 3-D: normal strains D[d_i, x_i] and engineering shear strains D[d_i, x_j] + D[d_j, x_i] ("EngineeringStrain" -> False gives the tensor strains, half of those); 2-D plane forms and InterpolatingFunction displacements on meshes raise NotImplementedError; a displacement of the wrong length raises ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation example: torsion displacement {-a y z, a x z, w[x, y]}) and the identity strain = {{1,2,2},{2,1,2},{2,2,1}} * tensor strain in tests. |
| `SolidMechanicsStress` | added | 5 | SolidMechanicsStress[vars, pars, strain] -> SymmetrizedArray of the Cauchy stresses of a linear elastic isotropic 3-D solid: sigma_ii = lambda tr(eps) + 2 mu eps_ii, tau_ij = mu gamma_ij for engineering shear strains (2 mu eps_ij with "EngineeringStrain" -> False); strain is a 3 x 3 symmetric matrix or SymmetrizedArray as returned by SolidMechanicsStrain; moduli as for SolidMechanicsPDEComponent; other "OutputStressMeasure" values, initial strains/stresses and 2-D forms raise NotImplementedError. Check: reference (Hooke's law; Wolfram documentation example tau = Y gamma/(2 (1 + nu))) in tests. |
| `SourcePDETerm` | added | 3 | SourcePDETerm[vars, f] and [vars, f, pars] -> f (the right-hand side of operator == SourcePDETerm[...]); systems: {f1, f2, ...} from {{f1}, {f2}, ...} or {f1, f2, ...}; a list for a single variable raises ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation forms). |
| `StartingStepSize` | added | 3 | StartingStepSize -> h (option): NDSolve's first step size (SciPy first_step); larger than the range raises ValueError. Check: numeric cross-check in tests. |
| `StepMonitor` | added | 8 | StepMonitor :> expr (option): evaluated after every accepted step of NDSolve (x, y[x], y'[x] replaced by the step values; the monitor runs once the integration finishes); FindRoot / NIntegrate / NSolve raise NotImplementedError for it rather than ignore it. Check: reference in tests. |
| `Tolerance` | added | 8 | Tolerance -> t (option): honoured by SingularValueList (singular values below t times the largest are dropped) and the other linear-algebra heads that document it. Check: reference in tests. |
| `VerifyConvergence` | added | 4 | VerifyConvergence -> True \| False (option): accepted by NSum, which raises ValueError for a divergent sum such as Sum[1/n]. Check: reference in tests. |
| `VonMisesStress` | added | 5 | VonMisesStress[vars, pars, stress] -> Sqrt[((sxx - syy)^2 + (syy - szz)^2 + (szz - sxx)^2 + 6 (txy^2 + txz^2 + tyz^2))/2] for a symmetric 3 x 3 (or 2 x 2, padded with zeros) stress matrix or SymmetrizedArray; numeric stresses give a number, symbolic ones a formula; non-symmetric or wrongly shaped input raises ValueError. Check: reference (uniaxial stress s -> \|s\|, pure shear t -> Sqrt[3] \|t\|) in tests. |
| `WavePDEComponent` | added | 3 | WavePDEComponent[{u[t, x...], t, {x...}}, pars] -> D[u, {t, 2}] + Inactive[Div][-c^2 . Inactive[Grad][u, X], X] with "WaveCoefficient" c (scalar, or an n x n matrix whose square c.c is used; default 1) and "RegionSymmetry"; stationary vars raise ValueError. Check: reference (Wolfram documentation forms) in tests. |
| `WhenEvent` | added | 10 | WhenEvent[event, action] (HoldAll, inert) inside NDSolve / NDSolveValue initial-value problems: events a == b (either crossing) or a > b / a < b (becoming True) located by SciPy root finding; actions "StopIntegration" (the solution domain ends there), "RemoveEvent", resets y[t] -> value / y'[t] -> value, lists of actions and any expression evaluated for side effects (Sow, counters) with the current state substituted; discrete variables, event options and integration in both directions from an interior initial point raise NotImplementedError. Check: reference (bouncing ball impact time Sqrt[2 h/g] and restitution) in tests. |
| `WorkingPrecision` | added | 32 | WorkingPrecision -> MachinePrecision (option): NDSolve and the W26 solvers compute in machine precision (other values raise NotImplementedError); higher precision is honoured by NIntegrate / FindRoot / N where implemented. Check: reference in tests. |

| `WeierstrassP` | added | 8 | WeierstrassP[u, {g2, g3}] via the Jacobi form e3 + (e1 - e3)/sn^2(Sqrt[e1 - e3] u \| m), m = (e2 - e3)/(e1 - e3), with e_i the roots of 4 t^3 - g2 t - g3 (valid for any ordering of the roots); approximate arguments only; degenerate invariants raise |
| `WeierstrassPPrime` | added | 5 | derivative of WeierstrassP[u, {g2, g3}] with respect to u |
| `Zeta` | fixed | 9 | Zeta[s, a] = Sum[((k + a)^2)^(-s/2), {k, 0, Infinity}] (terms with k + a = 0 excluded); this differs from HurwitzZeta[s, a] = Sum[(k + a)^-s] only for Re(a) < 0 (legacy returned the Hurwitz value there: Zeta[3, -1.5] = 0.118 instead of 16.71); exact values from SymPy (Zeta[2, 1/2] = Pi^2/2) |

| Function | Status | Cases | Notes |

### statistical models (W18)

| Function | Status | Cases | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AbsoluteCorrelation` | added | 7 | AbsoluteCorrelation[v1, v2] = Mean[v1 Conjugate[v2]] (non-centred correlation); [m] the matrix of the values between columns of m, [m1, m2] between the columns of m1 and m2; exact for exact data; complex data allowed. Symbolic entries stay unevaluated; unequal lengths raise ValueError; non-numeric data TypeError; distribution arguments NotImplementedError. Check: exact; reference values worked out from the definition. |
| `AlternativeHypothesis` | added | 19 | option of the hypothesis tests (ZTest, SignTest, MannWhitneyTest, the correlation tests, ...): "Unequal" (default), "Less" or "Greater"; other values raise ValueError in the tests; inert as an expression. Check: inert (stays unevaluated as a symbol, an expression or in a rule). |
| `AndersonDarlingTest` | added | 8 | AndersonDarlingTest[data, dist] and [data, dist, prop]: A^2 = -n - Sum[(2 i - 1)(Log[u_i] + Log[1 - u_(n+1-i)])]/n; p-value from Marsaglia & Marsaglia's (2004) finite-n Anderson-Darling distribution. The statistic is computed from the probability-integral transforms CDF[dist, x_i] of the sorted data. Only fully specified continuous univariate distributions are supported: AndersonDarlingTest[data] / [data, Automatic] (normality with estimated parameters, Monte Carlo p-values in Wolfram), symbolic parameters, two-sample and multivariate forms, discrete distributions and Method settings raise NotImplementedError; options SignificanceLevel, VerifyTestAssumptions. Check: reference values from the classical asymptotic critical points (A^2 = 2.492 at 5%, 3.857 at 1%) and the closed-form statistic. |
| `Around` | added | 26 | Around[x, d] is x with uncertainty d >= 0; Around[x, {dm, dp}] asymmetric; Around[x, Scaled[r]] = Around[x, r Abs[x]]; Around[Interval[{a, b}]] = Around[(a + b)/2, (b - a)/2]; Around[{x1, x2, ...}] = Around[Mean, StandardDeviation] of the samples. Arithmetic (Plus, Times, Power) and the elementary functions propagate uncertainty to first order assuming independent arguments (Sqrt[Sum[(df/dxi di)^2]], asymmetric parts propagated separately); a["Value"], a["Uncertainty"] and a["Interval"] give the parts. Comparisons stay unevaluated; negative uncertainties raise ValueError; non-numeric values TypeError; symbolic arguments stay unevaluated; Around of complex numbers raises NotImplementedError. Check: first-order propagation formulas checked against hand derivatives in tests. |
| `AroundReplace` | added | 6 | AroundReplace[expr, {x1 -> Around[v1, d1], ...}] evaluates expr at the values and propagates the (symmetric) uncertainties to first order treating the xi as independent: Around[f(v), Sqrt[Sum[(df/dxi di)^2]]]; rules whose right side is a plain number substitute it exactly; a single rule need not be in a list. Asymmetric uncertainties and the Assumptions option raise NotImplementedError; a non-rule TypeError. Check: identical to Around arithmetic for expressions with each variable once (tested). |
| `AugmentedSymmetricPolynomial` | added | 7 | AugmentedSymmetricPolynomial[{r1, ..., rk}, data] = Sum[x_i1^r1 ... x_ik^rk] over distinct indices i1, ..., ik, computed from power sums by Moebius inversion over the set partitions of {1, ..., k} (column-wise for matrices); AugmentedSymmetricPolynomial[{r1, ...}] stays as the formal object. Orders must be positive integers (ValueError); a non-list TypeError. Check: equals the brute-force sum over distinct index tuples (tested) and AugmentedSymmetricPolynomial[{r}, data] = PowerSymmetricPolynomial[r, data]. |
| `AutocorrelationTest` | added | 7 | AutocorrelationTest[data], [data, k] and [data, k, spec] for univariate data: the Ljung-Box statistic n (n + 2) Sum[r_i^2/(n - i), {i, k}] (the automatic test, as documented) or Box-Pierce n Sum[r_i^2] against ChiSquareDistribution[k], r_i the sample autocorrelations; k = Automatic is Ceiling[Log[n]]; spec is "LjungBox", "BoxPierce", a list of them or {prop, test}. Multivariate data, TemporalData and All raise NotImplementedError; k >= n or k < 1 ValueError. Check: reference values from statsmodels.stats.diagnostic.acorr_ljungbox (lb and bp statistics). |
| `BirnbaumImportance` | added | 6 | BirnbaumImportance[rdist, t] for ReliabilityDistribution and FailureDistribution: the list (in component order) of R(t \| component i works) - R(t \| component i failed), by exact enumeration of the Boolean structure function with independent component survival functions; t may be symbolic. Other distributions raise TypeError; discrete components (rejected by the distribution) NotImplementedError. Check: for a series system x && y the importance of x is the survival of y (tested), parallel x \|\| y gives 1 - F_y. |
| `BiweightLocation` | added | 8 | BiweightLocation[list] and [list, c] (default c = 6): Tukey's biweight M-estimate of location, iterated from the median to the fixed point x* = x* + Sum[(x - x*)(1 - u^2)^2]/Sum[(1 - u^2)^2] over \|u\| < 1, u = (x - x*)/(c MedianDeviation about x*); a matrix gives the column-wise estimates; the result is a machine number (iterative). Symbolic data stays unevaluated; non-numeric data raises TypeError, c <= 0 ValueError; dates and quantities are not supported. Check: self-check (the estimating equation is verified at the returned fixed point) and reference values from the Wolfram documentation examples. |
| `BiweightMidvariance` | added | 7 | BiweightMidvariance[list] and [list, c] (default c = 9): n Sum[(x - M)^2 (1 - u^2)^4] / Sum[(1 - u^2)(1 - 5 u^2)]^2 over \|u\| < 1 with M = Median, u = (x - M)/(c MedianDeviation); exact for exact data and c; a matrix gives the column-wise values; 0 when the median deviation is 0. Symbolic data stays unevaluated; non-numeric data raises TypeError, c <= 0 ValueError. Check: exact; reference values from the Wolfram documentation examples and astropy.stats.biweight_midvariance. |
| `BlomqvistBeta` | added | 6 | BlomqvistBeta[v1, v2] = Correlation[Sign[v1 - Median[v1]], Sign[v2 - Median[v2]]] (Blomqvist's medial correlation, as documented); exact for exact data; [m] and [m1, m2] give matrices between columns. Check: exact; reference values from the documented definition (Pearson correlation of the median signs, numpy.corrcoef). |
| `BlomqvistBetaTest` | added | 6 | BlomqvistBetaTest[v1, v2] and [v1, v2, prop]: the statistic is BlomqvistBeta and the p-value is Fisher's exact test on the 2x2 table of signs about the medians (values equal to a median dropped; two-sided = 2 Min[tails]; reproduces the Wolfram documentation example beta = -0.48, n = 100, p = 2.8183*10^-6); options AlternativeHypothesis, SignificanceLevel. Matrix (multivariate) arguments raise NotImplementedError; unequal lengths or constant vectors ValueError; non-numeric data TypeError; symbolic data stays unevaluated. Check: exact hypergeometric tail; reference values from scipy.stats.fisher_exact and the Wolfram documentation example. |

| `ClusteringTree` | added | 12 | ClusteringTree[{e1, ...}, ClusterDissimilarityFunction -> l] gives the agglomerative hierarchy as a Graph tree: vertices 1, 2, ... in preorder (root 1; the child holding the lower-index element first), edges parent -> child, VertexWeight -> the merge dissimilarity (0 at leaves) and VertexLabels -> the leaf elements; ClusteringTree[data, d] first merges all clusters at dissimilarity < d, and those clusters (lists) become the leaves. | `CoxModelFit` | added | 35 | CoxModelFit[edata] (no covariates) and CoxModelFit[{covariates, edata}, {f1, ...}, {x1, ...}] (a covariate vector or matrix with one row per subject; edata a list of times or EventData[times, flags] / EventData[Automatic, {times, flags, None}], flag 1 = right-censored) fit the proportional hazards model h(t) = h0(t) Exp[b.f(x)] by Newton-Raphson on the partial likelihood with Method -> "Breslow" (default) or "Efron" ties and give a CoxModel; the baseline is the Breslow estimate at x = 0. (c/(c - a))); exact for exact a; 1 when a >= c (unstable queue: every customer waits). Symbolic a or c stays unevaluated; c not a positive integer or a < 0 raises ValueError. Check: the covariance of the d form is DiagonalMatrix[d^2] (tested). |
| `VerifyTestAssumptions` | added | 5 | option of the hypothesis tests (Automatic, All, None, True/False, or a list or rules of assumptions); accepted, assumptions are not diagnosed; inert as an expression. Check: inert (stays unevaluated as a symbol, an expression or in a rule). |
| `WatsonUSquareTest` | added | 5 | WatsonUSquareTest[data, dist] and [data, dist, prop]: U^2 = W^2 - n (Mean[u] - 1/2)^2; p-value from the asymptotic series 2 Sum[(-1)^(k-1) Exp[-2 k^2 Pi^2 U*]] of Stephens' modified U* = (U^2 - 0.1/n + 0.1/n^2)(1 + 0.8/n). The statistic is computed from the probability-integral transforms CDF[dist, x_i] of the sorted data. Only fully specified continuous univariate distributions are supported: WatsonUSquareTest[data] / [data, Automatic] (normality with estimated parameters, Monte Carlo p-values in Wolfram), symbolic parameters, two-sample and multivariate forms, discrete distributions and Method settings raise NotImplementedError; options SignificanceLevel, VerifyTestAssumptions. Check: reference values from the closed-form statistic and Stephens' (1970) critical values (U* = 0.187 at 5%). |
| `Weights` | added | 9 | option of the fitting functions and of MeanShift / estimators: weights for the data (Automatic, a list or a pure function); inert as an expression. Check: inert (stays unevaluated as a symbol, an expression or in a rule). |
| `WilksW` | added | 6 | WilksW[m1, m2] = 1 - Det[S]/(Det[S11] Det[S22]) for the pooled covariance matrix S of the columns of m1 and m2 (as documented); machine-precision result. Unequal lengths or singular blocks raise ValueError; non-numeric data TypeError; symbolic arguments stay unevaluated. Check: for two vectors WilksW = Correlation^2 (tested). |
| `WilksWTest` | added | 6 | WilksWTest[m1, m2, "TestStatistic"] gives WilksW[m1, m2]; the p-value and other properties raise NotImplementedError (Wolfram's null approximation is not documented). Check: identical to WilksW (tested). |
| `ZTest` | added | 17 | ZTest[data], [data, s2], [data, s2, mu0] and [{data1, data2}, s2 \| {s1^2, s2^2}, mu0] with an optional trailing property: the z-test of mean = mu0 (or difference of means = mu0) with known variance s2 (the sample variance when omitted or Automatic, as documented); p-value from NormalDistribution[]; options AlternativeHypothesis ("Unequal", "Less", "Greater"), SignificanceLevel, VerifyTestAssumptions (accepted; assumptions are not diagnosed). Multivariate data and covariance matrices raise NotImplementedError; s2 <= 0 or a bad option ValueError; symbolic data stays unevaluated. Check: reference values from the closed form and statsmodels.stats.weightstats.ztest. |

Deviation note: Wolfram's Details write the projection divided by 4, which gives E[\|X_ij\|^2] = sigma^2/2, but its own worked examples (spectral edge 2 Sqrt[2 n], Tracy-Widom scaling (Max[Eigenvalues] - 2 Sqrt[2 n]) (n/4)^(1/6)) only hold at E[\|X_ij\|^2] = sigma^2, so that scale is used. PDF E^(-Tr[X.X]/(4 sigma^2))/((2 Pi sigma^2)^(n/2) (Pi sigma^2)^(n (n - 1))) on such X (0 otherwise; Lebesgue measure on the quaternion coordinates z0 (symmetric) and z1, z2, z3 (antisymmetric)); Mean 0; elementwise Variance; RandomVariate. | `StandbyDistribution` | added | 8 | StandbyDistribution[dist1, {dist2, ...}] (cold standby, perfect switching): lifetime = sum of the component lifetimes; PDF/CDF by exact convolution, mean, variance, MGF, RandomVariate; imperfect switching and warm standby raise NotImplementedError. Check: exact; exponential components give HypoexponentialDistribution. |
| `SurvivalDistribution` | added | 5 | SurvivalDistribution[{t1, t2, ...}] for uncensored event times (the Kaplan-Meier estimate is then the empirical distribution); censored data and censor weights raise NotImplementedError. Check: exact; agrees with EmpiricalDistribution in tests. |
| `SuzukiDistribution` | added | 6 | SuzukiDistribution[mu, nu] = ParameterMixtureDistribution[RayleighDistribution[s], s ~ LogNormalDistribution[mu, nu]]; exact moments, numeric PDF/CDF for machine-number x. Check: exact moments; numeric cross-check. |
| `TracyWidomDistribution` | added | 13 | TracyWidomDistribution[beta] for beta = 1, 2, 4 (largest eigenvalue of the GOE, GUE, GSE at the edge): CDF and PDF in machine precision from Bornemann's Fredholm determinants (F2 = det(I - K_Airy), F1 = det(I - B), F4 = (det(I - B) + det(I + B))/2 at Sqrt[2] x, B(x, y) = AiryAi[x + y + s]) and their exact derivatives, for machine-number x >= -9, -7, -7 (beta = 1, 2, 4; deeper left-tail values lose relative accuracy and raise NotImplementedError); exact x raises NotImplementedError (no closed form); Mean and Variance as 13-digit machine numbers (Bornemann 2010); InverseCDF, Median and RandomVariate by bisection (machine numbers, also for exact probabilities); NExpectation by Gauss-Legendre quadrature; other beta raise ValueError. Check: self-check (two quadrature orders must agree, else ArithmeticError); reference values (Bornemann's moments recomputed from the CDF, Monte Carlo GUE/GOE/GSE edge statistics) in tests. |
| `TruncatedDistribution` | added | 8 | TruncatedDistribution[{xmin, xmax}, dist] for univariate dist: PDF f/(F[xmax] - F[xmin]) on the interval, CDF, quantile (when dist has one), moments by exact integration/summation, RandomVariate; multivariate truncation raises NotImplementedError. Check: exact; PDF normalisation and SciPy truncnorm in tests. |
| `TsallisQExponentialDistribution` | added | 7 | TsallisQExponentialDistribution[lambda, q] (q < 2): PDF (2 - q) lambda e_q(-lambda x), CDF, quantile, moments (Infinity when divergent); q = 1 is ExponentialDistribution[lambda]. Check: exact; quantile/CDF round trip. |
| `TsallisQGaussianDistribution` | added | 6 | TsallisQGaussianDistribution[mu, beta, q] (q < 3) and [q] = [0, 1, q]: PDF e_q(-(x - mu)^2/(2 beta^2))/(beta Sqrt[2] C_q); q = 1 is NormalDistribution[mu, beta], q = 2 CauchyDistribution[mu, beta Sqrt[2]]; CDF through the equivalent scaled Beta (q < 1) or StudentT (1 < q < 3) distribution. Check: exact; the normal and Cauchy special cases in tests. |
| `TukeyLambdaDistribution` | added | 7 | TukeyLambdaDistribution[lambda] and [lambda, mu, sigma]: quantile mu + sigma (p^lambda - (1 - p)^lambda)/lambda (logistic for lambda = 0); exact mean, variance and moments (Beta integrals); PDF and CDF numeric for machine-number x (closed for lambda = 0, 1); the generalised [{l1, l2}, mu, {s1, s2}] form raises. Check: exact moments; SciPy tukeylambda reference values. |
| `UniformSumDistribution` | added | 7 | UniformSumDistribution[n, {a, b}] (default {0, 1}): sum of n uniforms (Irwin-Hall); exact piecewise PDF/CDF, mean, variance, MGF. Check: exact; Irwin-Hall reference values and the identity PDF = CDF' in tests. |
| `VarianceGammaDistribution` | added | 5 | VarianceGammaDistribution[lambda, alpha, beta, mu]: Bessel-K PDF, MGF, mean, variance; numeric CDF. Check: exact moments; numeric cross-check of the normalisation. |
| `VoigtDistribution` | added | 7 | VoigtDistribution[delta, sigma]: convolution of CauchyDistribution[0, delta] and NormalDistribution[0, sigma]; PDF via the Faddeeva function, characteristic function; moments Indeterminate; numeric CDF. Check: SciPy voigt_profile reference values. |
| `VonMisesDistribution` | added | 5 | VonMisesDistribution[mu, kappa] on [mu - Pi, mu + Pi]: PDF E^(kappa Cos[x - mu])/(2 Pi BesselI[0, kappa]); mean mu; variance and CDF numeric for machine-number input. Check: SciPy vonmises reference values. |
| `WakebyDistribution` | added | 6 | WakebyDistribution[alpha, beta, gamma, delta, mu]: quantile mu + alpha/beta (1 - (1 - p)^beta) - gamma/delta (1 - (1 - p)^-delta); exact mean and variance; PDF/CDF numeric for machine-number x. Check: exact; quantile/CDF round trip. |
| `WalleniusHypergeometricDistribution` | added | 5 | WalleniusHypergeometricDistribution[n, nsucc, ntot, w]: Wallenius' PDF Binomial[m1, k] Binomial[m2, n - k] Integrate[(1 - t^(w/D))^k (1 - t^(1/D))^(n - k), {t, 0, 1}]; exact for rational w, numeric for machine w. Check: exact; SciPy nchypergeom_wallenius reference values. |
| `WaringYuleDistribution` | added | 6 | WaringYuleDistribution[alpha] (= [alpha, 1]) and [alpha, beta] on k >= 0: PDF alpha Pochhammer[beta, k]/Pochhammer[alpha + beta, k + 1], moments (Infinity when divergent). Check: exact. |
| `WignerSemicircleDistribution` | added | 5 | WignerSemicircleDistribution[r] and [a, r]: PDF 2/(Pi r^2) Sqrt[r^2 - (x - a)^2], CDF, moments (Catalan numbers). Check: exact; SciPy semicircular reference values. |
| `WishartMatrixDistribution` | added | 8 | WishartMatrixDistribution[nu, Sigma] (nu > p - 1): PDF Det[X]^((nu - p - 1)/2) E^(-Tr[Inverse[Sigma].X]/2)/(2^(nu p/2) Det[Sigma]^(nu/2) MultivariateGamma), Mean nu Sigma, elementwise Variance nu (S_ij^2 + S_ii S_jj), RandomVariate (Bartlett). Check: exact; SciPy wishart reference values. |
| `ZipfDistribution` | added | 7 | ZipfDistribution[rho] (PDF k^(-rho - 1)/Zeta[rho + 1], k >= 1) and the truncated [n, rho] (HarmonicNumber normalisation); CDF, moments. Check: exact; SciPy zipf (a = rho + 1) reference values. |

| Function | Status | Cases | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|

A user assignment (or Block) takes precedence over the default. Check: exact (follows $DefaultParallelKernels) in tests. |
| `$CreationDate` | added | 3 | $CreationDate: a DateObject for when this copy of MikoshiLang was created (the modification time of the installed package; there is no separate build date). Check: reference (Python platform/os/sys values) in tests. |
| `$CurrentTask` | added | 5 | $CurrentTask: the TaskObject of the task being evaluated (also inside its handler functions), None outside tasks. Check: exact (a task reads its own TaskUUID) in tests. |
