| `$DefaultParallelKernels` | added | 5 | $DefaultParallelKernels: the kernels launched by LaunchKernels[] and automatically by the first parallel command: {KernelConfiguration["Local", "KernelCount" -> Automatic]} ($ProcessorCount local kernels); assign e.g. {2} or {} (no kernels: parallel commands then evaluate on the master). The value is not remembered between sessions. A user assignment (or Block) takes precedence over the default. Check: exact (LaunchKernels[] launches the configured number) in tests. |
| `$DefaultRemoteKernel` | added | 3 | $DefaultRemoteKernel: "localhost", the default remote kernel specification; assignments are kept for the session only (remote evaluation is not supported). A user assignment (or Block) takes precedence over the default. Check: exact (default "localhost"; Block assignment) in tests. |
| `$Display` | added | 3 | $Display: {}: the files and pipes for a user-defined $DisplayFunction (initial setting {} as documented). A user assignment (or Block) takes precedence over the default. Check: exact (the documented initial {}) in tests. |
| `$DistributedContexts` | added | 3 | $DistributedContexts: the contexts whose definitions parallel commands distribute automatically: by default the value of $Context ("Global`"); All, None, a context or a list of contexts may be assigned. A user assignment (or Block) takes precedence over the default. Check: exact (ctx` symbols are not distributed by default) in tests. |
| `$DistributedDefinitions` | added | 5 | $DistributedDefinitions: the symbols whose definitions have been distributed to parallel kernels, as HoldForm[s] in order of distribution. Check: exact (after DistributeDefinitions/ClearDistributedDefinitions) in tests. |
| `$Echo` | added | 3 | $Echo: the streams every main-loop input (Session.evaluate_input, the REPL) is echoed to: {} by default; OutputStream["stdout", 1], OutputStream["stderr", 2] or W27 output streams (files) may be assigned. A user assignment (or Block) takes precedence over the default. Check: exact (Session.evaluate_input echoes the input line to a W27 file stream) in tests. |
| `$EvaluationEnvironment` | added | 6 | $EvaluationEnvironment: "Session" in the main session, "Subkernel" in a parallel subkernel. Check: exact ("Session" on the master, "Subkernel" in ParallelEvaluate) in tests. |
| `$FontFamilies` | added | 3 | $FontFamilies: {}: there is no notebook front end, and Wolfram documents $FontFamilies as typically {} without one. Check: exact (the documented {} without a front end) in tests. |
| `$IgnoreEOF` | added | 3 | $IgnoreEOF: False: the REPL ends at end-of-file; set it to True to make an interactive REPL ignore end-of-file (it is always False for non-terminal input, as documented). A user assignment (or Block) takes precedence over the default. Check: exact (default False; Block assignment) in tests. |
| `$InitializationContexts` | added | 3 | $InitializationContexts: has no value by default (evaluates to itself); MikoshiLang reads no packages at start-up, so an assignment only stores the list. Check: exact (evaluates to itself) in tests. |
| `$Input` | added | 3 | $Input: the name of the stream input is read from: the file name given to Get (<<) while it reads, and "" otherwise. A user assignment (or Block) takes precedence over the default. Check: exact (inside Get it is the file name, "" afterwards) in tests. |
| `$KernelCount` | added | 9 | $KernelCount: the number of running parallel kernels (0 before any are launched); in a subkernel the master's count, as documented. Check: exact (after LaunchKernels/CloseKernels) in tests. |
| `$KernelID` | added | 10 | $KernelID: the id of the parallel kernel the evaluation runs on: 0 on the master kernel, 1, 2, ... (in launch order) on subkernels. Check: exact (ParallelEvaluate gives the kernel ids) in tests. |
| `$Language` | added | 3 | $Language: "English", the language of system messages (only English message texts exist). A user assignment (or Block) takes precedence over the default. Check: exact (default "English"; Block assignment) in tests. |
| `$MachineDomains` | added | 3 | $MachineDomains: the network domains of the host: the domain part of socket.getfqdn(), or {} if no domain is defined. Check: reference (Python platform/os/sys values) in tests. |
| `$MachineID` | added | 3 | $MachineID: a stable identification code for this computer in the MathID layout dddd-ddddd-ddddd, derived from /etc/machine-id (or the network hardware address); it is not a Wolfram license MathID. Check: reference (Python platform/os/sys values) in tests. |
| `$MachineName` | added | 3 | $MachineName: the host name without its domain (socket.gethostname()); "" if none. Check: reference (Python platform/os/sys values) in tests. |
| `$MachineType` | added | 3 | $MachineType: the general machine family; "PC" on every current system, as in Wolfram. Check: reference (Python platform/os/sys values) in tests. |
| `$NoValue` | added | 3 | $NoValue: inert symbol: assigned to InitializationValue[...] to mean "initialise with no value"; it evaluates to itself. Check: exact (evaluates to itself) in tests. |
| `$OperatingSystem` | added | 4 | $OperatingSystem: "Unix" (Linux and other Unix systems), "MacOSX" or "Windows". Check: reference (Python platform/os/sys values) in tests. |
| `$Output` | added | 5 | $Output: the channels Print writes to: {OutputStream["stdout", 1]}; assign {} to silence Print, or a list of stdout/stderr streams. A user assignment (or Block) takes precedence over the default. Check: exact (Print output reaches the assigned channel; {} silences it) in tests. |
| `$ParentProcessID` | added | 4 | $ParentProcessID: the process id of the process that started this kernel (os.getppid()). Check: reference (Python platform/os/sys values) in tests. |
| `$ProcessID` | added | 20 | $ProcessID: the operating-system process id of this kernel (os.getpid()). Check: reference (Python platform/os/sys values) in tests. |
| `$ProcessorCount` | added | 4 | $ProcessorCount: the number of processor cores available to this process (os.sched_getaffinity, else os.cpu_count); Protected, but it may be reset after Unprotect to change the default number of parallel kernels. Check: reference (Python platform/os/sys values) in tests. |
| `$ProcessorType` | added | 3 | $ProcessorType: the processor architecture: "x86-64", "x86", "ARM64", "ARM" (from platform.machine()). Check: reference (Python platform/os/sys values) in tests. |
| `$ProgressReporting` | added | 3 | $ProgressReporting: False: no progress panels are shown in this text interface; True or Automatic may be assigned (functions with a ProgressReporting option then warn that progress reporting is unavailable). A user assignment (or Block) takes precedence over the default. Check: exact (default False; results of functions are unchanged when set) in tests. |
| `$RandomGeneratorState` | added | 11 | $RandomGeneratorState: the current state of the library's pseudorandom generator as a RandomGeneratorState; it changes whenever random numbers are generated and is reset by SeedRandom. Check: exact (BlockRandom[..., RandomSeeding -> $RandomGeneratorState] repeats the numbers) in tests. |
| `$ReleaseNumber` | added | 3 | $ReleaseNumber: the release (patch) number of the MikoshiLang version, the last integer of major.minor.release. Check: reference (Python platform/os/sys values) in tests. |
| `$ScriptCommandLine` | added | 3 | $ScriptCommandLine: {}: MikoshiLang is not running from a wolframscript-style script launcher, so (as documented for that case) the list is empty. Check: exact (the documented {} outside a script launcher; a child Python process reports no script arguments either) in tests. |
| `$ScriptInputString` | added | 3 | $ScriptInputString: None: no script launcher supplied standard input (documented value outside wolframscript). Check: exact (the documented None outside a script launcher) in tests. |
| `$SessionID` | added | 3 | $SessionID: a number unique to this session, derived from $MachineID, the process id and the start time. Check: reference (Python platform/os/sys values) in tests. |
| `$SharedFunctions` | added | 4 | $SharedFunctions: the list Hold[f] of functions shared with SetSharedFunction. Check: exact (SetSharedFunction/UnsetShared) in tests. |
| `$SharedVariables` | added | 4 | $SharedVariables: the list Hold[x] of variables shared with SetSharedVariable. Check: exact (SetSharedVariable/UnsetShared) in tests. |
| `$SyntaxHandler` | added | 3 | $SyntaxHandler: unset by default; when assigned a function f, a main-loop input (Session.evaluate_input / the REPL) with a syntax error is replaced by f["text", pos] where pos is the (1-based) position of the character where the error was detected: a string result is parsed instead, $Failed abandons the input. A user assignment (or Block) takes precedence over the default. Check: exact (handler called with the text and offset, replacement parsed) in tests. |
| `$System` | added | 3 | $System: a description such as "Linux x86 (64-bit)", "Mac OS X ARM (64-bit)" or "Microsoft Windows (64-bit)". Check: reference (Python platform/os/sys values) in tests. |
| `$SystemID` | added | 3 | $SystemID: a short id such as "Linux-x86-64", "MacOSX-ARM64" or "Windows-x86-64". Check: reference (Python platform/os/sys values) in tests. |
| `$SystemShell` | added | 3 | $SystemShell: the system shell: "/bin/sh" on Unix and macOS, %COMSPEC% (cmd.exe) on Windows; Run uses it. Check: reference (Python platform/os/sys values) in tests. |
| `$SystemWordLength` | added | 4 | $SystemWordLength: the bit length of machine pointers: 64 or 32 (sys.maxsize). Check: reference (Python platform/os/sys values) in tests. |
| `$Urgent` | added | 7 | $Urgent: the channels for urgent output (the prompts of Input and InputString): {OutputStream["stdout", 1]}. A user assignment (or Block) takes precedence over the default. Check: exact (Input/InputString prompts are written to it) in tests. |
| `$Username` | added | 3 | $Username: the login name of the user running the kernel (getpass.getuser()), None if there is none. Check: reference (Python platform/os/sys values) in tests. |
| `$Version` | added | 5 | $Version: MikoshiLang's version string: "<version> for <$System> (<creation date>)". Check: reference (Python platform/os/sys values) in tests. |
| `$VersionNumber` | added | 4 | $VersionNumber: MikoshiLang's version number major.minor as a machine real (3.8 for 3.8.0). Check: reference (Python platform/os/sys values) in tests. |
| `AbortKernels` | added | 4 | AbortKernels[] aborts the evaluations running on parallel kernels (their kernels are restarted with the same ids and the current distributed definitions) and discards the queued ParallelSubmit evaluations (they give $Aborted); gives the list of running KernelObjects. Check: exact (queued evaluations give $Aborted, kernels keep working) in tests. |
| `AutoRemove` | added | 4 | AutoRemove: option of SessionSubmit, LocalSubmit and ScheduledTask; True removes the task (as TaskRemove) after its final run, False (default) keeps it in Tasks[]. Check: exact (TaskStatus "Removed" after the last run) in tests. |
| `BlockRandom` | added | 23 | BlockRandom[expr] evaluates expr with all pseudorandom generators localized: the library's Mersenne Twister (SeedRandom, RandomReal, RandomInteger, RandomChoice, RandomVariate, ...), Python's global random and NumPy's global generator are saved before and restored after, even on error or abort, so random numbers generated afterwards are the same as if expr had not been evaluated. Option RandomSeeding -> Inherited (default: start from the current state), Automatic (a fresh random seed), an integer or string seed, or a RandomGeneratorState. HoldFirst. Check: exact (the numbers after BlockRandom equal those generated without it) in tests. |
| `ClearDistributedDefinitions` | added | 5 | ClearDistributedDefinitions[] removes every distributed definition from the parallel kernels and forgets them (the master's definitions are kept), giving the list of HoldForm[s] cleared; ClearDistributedDefinitions[s1, ...] only those symbols. HoldAll. Check: exact ($DistributedDefinitions afterwards; kernels no longer know the definition) in tests. |
| `CloseKernels` | added | 16 | CloseKernels[] terminates all running parallel kernels; CloseKernels[k], CloseKernels[{k1, ...}] or CloseKernels[id] only those; gives the list of KernelObjects closed. Distributed definitions are kept and sent again to kernels launched later. Check: exact ($KernelCount afterwards) in tests. |
| `CriticalSection` | added | 7 | CriticalSection[{l1, l2, ...}, expr] evaluates expr while holding the locks li (symbols), so that at most one parallel kernel (or master task) at a time runs code guarded by the same lock; the locks are released afterwards, also on error or abort. The locks are managed by the master kernel. HoldAll. Check: exact (a guarded shared-variable update is not lost) in tests. |
| `DistributeDefinitions` | added | 9 | DistributeDefinitions[s1, s2, ...] sends the current definitions (values, down/sub/up values, attributes, options) of the symbols and of the user symbols they depend on to all parallel kernels, also to kernels launched later, and gives the list of HoldForm[s] distributed; a string "ctx`" means every symbol with definitions in that context. HoldAll. Check: exact (ParallelEvaluate sees the definition) in tests. |
| `DistributedContexts` | added | 9 | DistributedContexts: option of ParallelMap, ParallelTable, ParallelSum, ParallelProduct, ParallelDo, ParallelArray, ParallelCombine, ParallelCases, ParallelSelect, ParallelTry, Parallelize and ParallelEvaluate giving the contexts whose symbols' definitions are distributed automatically: $DistributedContexts (default, i.e. $Context), All or Automatic (every context), None, a context "ctx`" or a list of contexts. Check: exact (None leaves a function undefined on the kernels) in tests. |
| `Environment` | added | 8 | Environment["var"] gives the value of an operating-system environment variable (os.environ), or $Failed if it is not set (documented result). Check: reference (os.environ) in tests. |
| `EvaluationObject` | added | 3 | EvaluationObject[id, expr] (HoldAllComplete, inert) represents an evaluation queued by ParallelSubmit; WaitAll and WaitNext give its result; eo["Process"] (HoldForm of expr), eo["State"] ("ready for processing", "queued", "running", "received", "finished"), eo["Result"] (HoldComplete[value], Missing["NotAvailable"] before), eo[All] and eo["Properties"]. Check: exact in tests. |
| `Exit` | added | 6 | Exit[] / Exit[n] terminates the MikoshiLang kernel with exit code n (0-255, default 0): $Epilog is evaluated, then SystemExit(n) is raised, which ends the REPL or script (a host program embedding a Session can catch SystemExit). Same as Quit. Check: exact (SystemExit code) in tests. |
| `GetEnvironment` | added | 7 | GetEnvironment[] gives every environment variable as "var" -> "value" rules (in os.environ order); GetEnvironment["var"] gives "var" -> value, with None for an unset variable; GetEnvironment[{v1, ...}] gives a list of rules. Check: reference (os.environ) in tests. |
| `InitialEvaluationHistory` | added | 4 | InitialEvaluationHistory: option of BayesianMinimization and BayesianMaximization giving earlier evaluations {conf1 -> value1, ...} to start the optimization from (handled by the W08 optimizers). Check: exact (a history containing the optimum is used) in tests. |
| `Input` | added | 3 | Input[] / Input[prompt] writes the prompt to $Urgent, reads an expression from standard input (continuing over further lines while the expression is incomplete) and evaluates it; EndOfFile at end of input, Null for an empty line. A syntax error raises ValueError. The init and dialog-option arguments are ignored (no front end). Check: exact (stdin replaced by known text) in tests. |
| `InputString` | added | 3 | InputString[] / InputString[prompt] writes the prompt to $Urgent and reads one line of text from standard input, returned as a string without its newline; EndOfFile at end of input. The init and window-option arguments of the notebook dialog are accepted and ignored (there is no front end). Check: exact (stdin replaced by known text) in tests. |
| `KernelConfiguration` | added | 8 | KernelConfiguration["Local", "KernelCount" -> n] (or KernelConfiguration[n], KernelConfiguration[<\|"Name" -> "Local", "KernelCount" -> n\|>]) describes local parallel kernels for LaunchKernels, $DefaultParallelKernels and $ConfiguredKernels; "KernelCount" -> Automatic means $ProcessorCount. Other settings and remote specifications raise NotImplementedError when launched. kc["prop"] reads a setting. Check: exact (number of kernels launched) in tests. |
| `KernelObject` | added | 3 | KernelObject[id, "Local"] represents a running parallel subkernel (from LaunchKernels, Kernels[] or ParallelKernels[]); ko["prop"] gives "KernelID", "Name", "Class", "KernelCommand", "ProcessID", "Running", "StartTime"; ko[All] an association and ko["Properties"] the names. Check: exact (ProcessID matches ParallelEvaluate[$ProcessID, ko]) in tests. |
| `Kernels` | added | 18 | Kernels[] gives the list of running parallel KernelObjects in launch order (supporting head used by ParallelEvaluate/CloseKernels). Check: exact in tests. |
| `KillProcess` | added | 7 | KillProcess[proc] terminates a process: SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after the ProcessOptions KillTimeout (default 1 s) for processes started by StartProcess; SIGTERM for other ProcessObjects. Returns Null; a finished process is left alone. Check: exact (ProcessStatus becomes "Finished") in tests. |
| `LaunchKernels` | added | 10 | LaunchKernels[] launches the default parallel kernels ($DefaultParallelKernels; Automatic counts mean $ProcessorCount) when none are running; LaunchKernels[n] launches n more local kernels; LaunchKernels["Local"\|"localhost"], LaunchKernels[KernelConfiguration["Local", "KernelCount" -> n]] and lists of these. Subkernels are separate local MikoshiLang processes (Python sys.executable) that receive distributed definitions, shared variables/functions and ParallelNeeds contexts; returns the new KernelObject[id, "Local"] list. LaunchKernels[] with kernels already running raises ValueError; remote specs (ssh://, wstp://, lwg://, file:// Wolfram kernels, cloud) raise NotImplementedError. Check: exact ($KernelCount, distinct $ProcessID values) in tests. |
| `LocalEvaluate` | added | 6 | LocalEvaluate[expr] evaluates expr in a new local MikoshiLang kernel (a separate process, discarded afterwards) and gives the result; LocalEvaluate["Local", expr] names the kernel ($DefaultLocalKernel), LocalEvaluate[{k1, k2, ...}, expr] uses one new kernel per element and gives a list. With IncludeDefinitions -> True (default) the definitions expr depends on are sent along. Other kernel specs (ssh://, wstp://, file:// Wolfram kernels, cloud) raise NotImplementedError. HoldAll. Check: exact (a different $ProcessID; the definitions are available) in tests. |
| `LocalSubmit` | added | 5 | LocalSubmit[expr] evaluates expr asynchronously in a new local MikoshiLang kernel (a separate process, with the definitions expr needs) and gives a TaskObject at once; LocalSubmit[ScheduledTask[expr, spec]] repeats it on a schedule as SessionSubmit does. Options HandlerFunctions (also PrintOutputGenerated, FailureOccurred), HandlerFunctionsKeys, AutoRemove. TaskAbort kills the kernel process. HoldAll. Check: exact (a different $ProcessID; result via TaskWait) in tests. |
| `OperatingSystem` | added | 42 | OperatingSystem: option of FileNameJoin, FileNameSplit and related file-name functions giving the naming conventions to use: "Unix", "MacOSX" or "Windows" (default $OperatingSystem); handled by the W27 file-name functions. Check: exact (Windows vs Unix separators) in tests. |
| `ParallelArray` | added | 5 | ParallelArray[f, n] gives {f[1], ..., f[n]} computed in parallel; ParallelArray[f, {n1, n2, ...}] an n1 x n2 x ... array of f[i1, i2, ...]; ParallelArray[f, dims, r] starts the indices at r (or {r1, ...}); ParallelArray[f, dims, r, h] uses head h at every level. Options Method, DistributedContexts. Check: reference (Array gives the same result) in tests. |
| `ParallelCases` | added | 6 | ParallelCases[list, patt] gives the elements of list (any head) that match patt (or patt -> rhs transformed), searching chunks in parallel; ParallelCases[list, patt, levelspec, n] at most n; level specifications other than {1} use Cases on the master. Options Method, DistributedContexts. Check: reference (Cases gives the same result) in tests. |
| `ParallelCombine` | added | 5 | ParallelCombine[f, h[e1, ..., en]] evaluates f[h[ei, ...]] on chunks of the elements in parallel and combines the results with h if h is Flat (Plus, Times, ...) or Join otherwise; ParallelCombine[f, h[...], comb] combines with comb. Chunks follow Method (Automatic: two per kernel). Check: reference (the sequential f[h[...]]) in tests. |
| `ParallelDo` | added | 6 | ParallelDo[expr, iter1, ...] evaluates expr for each iterator value in parallel (for side effects such as shared variables, shared functions or files) and returns Null; non-enumerable iterators use Do on the master. HoldAll; options Method, DistributedContexts. Check: exact (a shared variable collects the values) in tests. |
| `ParallelEvaluate` | added | 43 | ParallelEvaluate[expr] evaluates expr on every parallel kernel and gives the list of results (each evaluated again on the master, as in Wolfram); ParallelEvaluate[expr, k] on one KernelObject (a single result), ParallelEvaluate[expr, {k1, ...}] on several, ParallelEvaluate[expr, kernels, h] wraps the results in h before they are evaluated on the master (h = Hold prevents it). Option DistributedContexts (default $DistributedContexts). Kernels are launched if none run; inside a subkernel or with no kernels configured it evaluates once on the master and gives {result}. HoldFirst. Check: exact ($KernelID values, distinct $ProcessID values) in tests. |
| `ParallelKernels` | added | 4 | ParallelKernels[] gives the KernelObjects of the running parallel kernels in launch order (same as Kernels[]); ParallelKernels["OneKernelPerMachine"] the first kernel (all kernels are local). Check: exact (after LaunchKernels/CloseKernels) in tests. |
| `ParallelMap` | added | 19 | ParallelMap[f, expr] applies f to the elements of expr (any head, or the values of an association) in parallel, chunked by Method (Automatic: two evaluations per kernel, "FinestGrained", "CoarsestGrained", "EvaluationsPerKernel" -> e, "ItemsPerEvaluation" -> m); definitions of f and of the elements are distributed automatically (DistributedContexts). ParallelMap[f, expr, levelspec] parallelizes level 1 ({1} or 1) and evaluates other level specifications with Map on the master. Check: reference (Map gives the same result) in tests. |
| `ParallelNeeds` | added | 5 | ParallelNeeds["ctx`"] evaluates Needs["ctx`"] on every running parallel kernel and remembers it for kernels launched later (the master is not affected); errors from Needs are raised. Returns Null. Check: exact (the context appears in $Packages / $ContextPath of the kernels) in tests. |
| `ParallelProduct` | added | 5 | ParallelProduct[expr, iter1, ...] computes Product[expr, iter1, ...] by multiplying the parts for each value of the outer iterator computed in parallel; non-enumerable iterators use Product on the master. HoldAll; options Method, DistributedContexts. Check: reference (Product gives the same result) in tests. |
| `ParallelSelect` | added | 5 | ParallelSelect[list, crit] gives the elements of list for which crit gives True, testing chunks in parallel; ParallelSelect[list, crit, n] the first n. Options Method, DistributedContexts. Check: reference (Select gives the same result) in tests. |
| `ParallelSubmit` | added | 16 | ParallelSubmit[expr] queues expr for evaluation on a parallel kernel and gives EvaluationObject[id, expr] at once; ParallelSubmit[{x, y, ...}, expr] first inserts the current values of x, y, ... into expr (as With). Queued evaluations are sent to kernels by WaitAll/WaitNext; definitions are not distributed automatically (use DistributeDefinitions). HoldAllComplete. eo["Process"\|"State"\|"Result"\|All\|"Properties"] inspects an EvaluationObject. Check: exact (WaitAll results) in tests. |
| `ParallelSum` | added | 7 | ParallelSum[expr, iter1, ...] computes Sum[expr, iter1, ...] by summing the parts for each value of the outer iterator in parallel (then Plus on the master); iterators that cannot be enumerated (symbolic bounds, infinite sums) are given to Sum on the master. HoldAll; options Method, DistributedContexts. Check: reference (Sum gives the same result) in tests. |
| `ParallelTable` | added | 8 | ParallelTable[expr, iter1, iter2, ...] builds Table[expr, iter1, ...] in parallel: the values of the outer iterator are computed on the master and the parts are evaluated on the kernels (inside Block with the iterator variable set), chunked by Method; options Method, DistributedContexts. Iterators with symbolic bounds are evaluated with Table on the master. HoldAll. Check: reference (Table gives the same result) in tests. |
| `ParallelTry` | added | 5 | ParallelTry[f, {a1, a2, ...}] evaluates f[ai] in parallel and gives the first result (in order of completion) that is not $Failed, or $Failed if all fail; ParallelTry[f, list, k] gives a list of the first k such results (shorter if fewer exist). Evaluations still running when enough results are in are aborted (their kernels restarted). Without kernels the ai are tried in order. Options DistributedContexts. Check: exact (a single non-$Failed candidate) in tests. |
| `Parallelize` | added | 12 | Parallelize[expr] evaluates expr using the parallel kernels when its form is recognized: Map, Table, Sum, Product, Do, Array, Select, Cases, Count, MapIndexed, MapThread, Scan, Apply at level {1}, a Listable function of one list, compound expressions (each part) and x = expr; any other expression is evaluated on the master, as Wolfram does for expressions that cannot be parallelized. HoldFirst; options Method, DistributedContexts, ProgressReporting. Check: reference (the sequential evaluation gives the same result) in tests. |
| `ProcessConnection` | added | 6 | ProcessConnection[proc, "StandardInput"] gives the OutputStream["in:k", n] writing to a started process's standard input; "StandardOutput" and "StandardError" give InputStream["out:k", n] / ["err:k", n] reading its output (W27 stream functions work on them; Close on the input stream sends end-of-file). Check: exact (round trip through a sys.executable -c echo program) in tests. |
| `ProcessDirectory` | added | 6 | ProcessDirectory: option of RunProcess and StartProcess giving the child's working directory: Inherited (default, the current Directory[]) or an existing directory (string or File); others raise ValueError. Check: exact (the child reports its working directory) in tests. |
| `ProcessEnvironment` | added | 7 | ProcessEnvironment: option of RunProcess and StartProcess: Inherited (default, this kernel's environment) or an association "var" -> "value" merged into the inherited environment (None unsets a variable). Check: exact (the child reports the variable) in tests. |
| `ProcessInformation` | added | 8 | ProcessInformation[proc] gives <\|"ExitCode" -> n\|> for a process started with StartProcess (None while it is running; 128+s if killed by signal s); ProcessInformation[proc, "prop"] gives "ExitCode" or one of "PID", "PPID", "Program", "Arguments", "StartTime", "Status". Check: exact (exit codes of sys.executable -c programs) in tests. |
| `ProcessObject` | added | 4 | ProcessObject[<\|"ManagedProcess" -> True, "UID", "PID", "PPID"\|>] represents a process started by StartProcess, ProcessObject[<\|"ManagedProcess" -> False, ...\|>] a system process from SystemProcesses, and ProcessObject[pid] the system process with that id; it is used by ProcessStatus, ProcessInformation, ProcessConnection, KillProcess and the W27 read/write functions, and proc["prop"] gives a property. Check: exact (properties of a started process) in tests. |
| `ProcessStatus` | added | 10 | ProcessStatus[proc] gives "Running" or "Finished" for a ProcessObject (one started by StartProcess, or a system process from SystemProcesses / ProcessObject[pid]); ProcessStatus[proc, "status"] gives True if the process has that status. Check: exact (process exits after it is told to) in tests. |
| `Processes` | added | 4 | Processes[] lists the ProcessObjects of the external processes started in this session by StartProcess that are still running, in start order. Check: exact (before/after KillProcess) in tests. |
| `ProgressReporting` | added | 5 | ProgressReporting: option of Parallelize and the parallel commands (and of other long computations) saying whether to show a progress panel; accepted and ignored, since this text interface has no progress panels (default $ProgressReporting). Check: exact (results unchanged) in tests. |
| `Quit` | added | 5 | Quit[] / Quit[n] terminates the kernel with exit code n (0-255, default 0) after evaluating $Epilog, by raising SystemExit(n); identical to Exit. Check: exact (SystemExit code) in tests. |
| `RandomGeneratorState` | added | 3 | RandomGeneratorState: the state of the library's Mersenne Twister (the generator behind SeedRandom, RandomReal, RandomInteger, RandomChoice, RandomVariate, ...), as RandomGeneratorState[{"MersenneTwister", {}}, <\|"Version", "State", "Gauss"\|>]; it is a value of $RandomGeneratorState, a RandomSeeding setting of BlockRandom (restoring the state), and has the properties "Method", "StateHash" and "CrossSessionPersistent" (True: the state reproduces the same numbers in any session). Check: exact (restoring a state reproduces the same random numbers) in tests. |
| `RandomSeeding` | added | 16 | RandomSeeding: option of BlockRandom (and of the W29 random-localizing functions) giving the seed used inside: Inherited (the current state), Automatic (a new random seed), an integer or string seed, or a RandomGeneratorState. Check: exact (equal seeds give equal numbers) in tests. |
| `Run` | added | 5 | Run["command"] runs command through the system shell ($SystemShell; cmd.exe on Windows) and gives its exit code (128+s if killed by signal s); Run[e1, e2, ...] runs the strings as they are and other expressions in InputForm, separated by spaces. The command's output goes to the kernel's standard output and error. Note: this runs arbitrary shell commands. Check: reference (exit codes of sys.executable -c programs) in tests. |
| `RunProcess` | added | 24 | RunProcess["program"] / RunProcess[{"program", arg1, ...}] runs an external program to completion (no shell; the program name is not split) and gives <\|"ExitCode" -> n, "StandardOutput" -> s, "StandardError" -> s\|>; RunProcess[cmd, "prop"] one of these, RunProcess[cmd, All] the association, RunProcess[cmd, prop, input] feeds input (a string, ByteArray, or the OutputForm text of an expression) to the standard input. Arguments "name" -> value become --name=value (-n=value for one-letter names); numbers are converted to text. Options ProcessDirectory and ProcessEnvironment (an association merged into the inherited environment; None unsets a variable). A program that cannot be started raises ValueError (Wolfram returns $Failed). Note: this runs arbitrary programs with the user's rights. Check: reference (Python subprocess results for sys.executable -c programs) in tests. |
| `RunThrough` | added | 5 | RunThrough["command", expr] runs command through the system shell with the InputForm text of expr (evaluated first; use Unevaluated to send it as is) on its standard input, then parses the command's standard output as MikoshiLang input and evaluates it (Null if there is no output). A non-zero exit code with no output raises ValueError. Check: exact (a sys.executable -c program transforming its input) in tests. |
| `ScheduledTask` | added | 17 | ScheduledTask[expr, spec] (HoldFirst, inert) describes a task to run on a schedule for SessionSubmit and LocalSubmit: spec None, Now, t seconds or a time Quantity (repeated), {t} (once), {t, n} (n times) or "Hourly"/"Daily"/"Weekly"/"Monthly"/"Yearly"; option AutoRemove. Dates and cron specifications raise NotImplementedError when submitted. Check: exact (run counts) in tests. |
| `SessionSubmit` | added | 42 | SessionSubmit[expr] starts evaluating expr in the background of the current session (a thread sharing the session's definitions, running preemptively like Wolfram session tasks) and gives a TaskObject at once; SessionSubmit[ScheduledTask[expr, spec]] runs it on a schedule (None: on demand only; t seconds or a time Quantity: every t; {t}: once after t; {t, n}: n times; Now; "Hourly", "Daily", ...). Options HandlerFunctions (events TaskStarted, ScheduleTriggered, ResultReceived, ScheduleExecuted, TaskStatusChanged, TaskFinished, TaskRemoved; PrintOutputGenerated/MessageGenerated raise NotImplementedError), HandlerFunctionsKeys, Method (Automatic), AutoRemove. Dates/cron schedules raise NotImplementedError. HoldAll. Check: exact (TaskWait then EvaluationResult) in tests. |
| `SetEnvironment` | added | 13 | SetEnvironment["var" -> "value"] sets an environment variable of this process (inherited by Run, RunProcess and StartProcess); "var" -> None unsets it; a list or association sets several. Integer values are converted to strings. Returns Null. Check: reference (os.environ) in tests. |
| `SetSharedFunction` | added | 7 | SetSharedFunction[f1, ...] makes the symbols shared functions: f[args] evaluated on a parallel kernel is evaluated on the master kernel (Null if the master has no applicable definition), and definitions f[...] = ... made on a kernel are stored on the master. HoldAll; returns Null. Check: exact (calls are evaluated on the master: $ProcessID of the master) in tests. |
| `SetSharedVariable` | added | 12 | SetSharedVariable[s1, ...] makes the symbols shared variables: every read and assignment of si on a parallel kernel goes to the master kernel (a variable without a value reads as Null there); updates are not atomic unless done inside CriticalSection. HoldAll; returns Null. Check: exact (values assigned on the kernels are seen on the master) in tests. |
| `SetSystemOptions` | added | 8 | SetSystemOptions["group" -> {"name" -> value, ...}, ...] resets internal system options (see SystemOptions) and returns the new settings of the groups changed; every value is validated first (nothing changes if one is invalid). RecursionOptions set $RecursionLimit/$IterationLimit. Check: exact (SystemOptions reads back the value) in tests. |
| `Share` | added | 4 | Share[] / Share[expr] gives the number of bytes saved by sharing common subexpressions. MikoshiLang expressions are immutable Python objects that are already shared by reference wherever they are reused, so no further memory can be saved and the result is always 0 (Wolfram's documented result when nothing can be shared). Check: exact in tests. |
| `StartProcess` | added | 27 | StartProcess["program"] / StartProcess[{"program", arg1, ...}] starts an external program in the background (no shell) and gives ProcessObject[<\|"ManagedProcess" -> True, "UID" -> k, "PID" -> pid, "PPID" -> ...\|>]; WriteLine/WriteString/BinaryWrite on it write to its standard input, ReadLine/ReadString/Read on it read its standard output (ReadString[proc, EndOfBuffer] what is available now), ProcessConnection gives the individual streams. Arguments "name" -> value become --name=value. Options ProcessDirectory and ProcessEnvironment as in RunProcess. Extra positional arguments leave it unevaluated (as documented); a program that cannot be started raises ValueError. Started processes are terminated when MikoshiLang exits. Check: reference (Python subprocess) in tests. |
| `SystemInformation` | added | 13 | SystemInformation[] gives {comp -> {prop -> value, ...}, ...} for the components "Kernel" (version, creation date, system id, process ids, user, machine, directories, Python/SymPy versions), "Machine" (physical and virtual memory as Quantity[..., "Gibibytes"], page size, processors, load average), "Links" (open streams, child processes, parallel kernels) and "Network"; "FrontEnd" and "Devices" are Missing["NotActive"] (no front end). SystemInformation[comp], [comp, prop], [comp, "Properties"], ["Components"] and ["Small"] (the main Kernel properties). Unknown names raise ValueError. Check: reference (Python platform/os values) in tests. |
| `SystemOpen` | added | 6 | SystemOpen["file"], SystemOpen[File[...]] or SystemOpen[URL[...]] / SystemOpen["http..."] opens the target with the associated program of the desktop (xdg-open on Linux, open on macOS, os.startfile on Windows) without waiting, and returns Null; a file that does not exist raises ValueError, a URL without a scheme://... raises ValueError and a missing opener raises NotImplementedError. Check: exact (the opener command, with the launcher replaced) in tests. |
| `SystemOptions` | added | 8 | SystemOptions[] gives the internal system options as nested rules; SystemOptions["group"] gives {"group" -> {...}} and SystemOptions["group" -> "name"] (or ["group", "name"]) one setting. Groups: "ParallelOptions" (MathLinkTimeout: seconds to wait for a launched subkernel, default 60; RelaunchFailedKernels; RecoveryMode "ReQueue"/"Abandon" for evaluations of a failed kernel; MaxKernelLaunchCount), "ProcessOptions" (KillTimeout: seconds KillProcess waits before SIGKILL) and "RecursionOptions" ($RecursionLimit and $IterationLimit). Unknown names raise ValueError. Check: exact (round trip with SetSystemOptions) in tests. |
| `SystemProcesses` | added | 8 | SystemProcesses[] gives ProcessObject[<\|"ManagedProcess" -> False, "PID", "PPID", "Program", "Path", "User", "Memory" (Quantity in megabytes), "Threads", "StartTime"\|>] for the processes of the current user, SystemProcesses[All] for all users; SystemProcesses[patt] those whose program name contains the string (pattern), ignoring case; SystemProcesses[prop -> val] / [{prop -> val, ...}] those whose properties match (a string is a case-insensitive substring of string properties, otherwise a pattern matched with MatchQ). proc["prop"] reads a property. Linux reads /proc, other Unix systems use ps; Windows raises NotImplementedError. Check: reference (os.getpid() and the test's own child processes) in tests. |
| `TaskAbort` | added | 4 | TaskAbort[task] aborts the evaluation the task is currently running (its result becomes $Aborted; a scheduled task continues with its next run; for LocalSubmit tasks the kernel process is killed) and gives the TaskObject at once; it does nothing if the task is not evaluating. Listable. Check: exact (EvaluationResult $Aborted) in tests. |
| `TaskExecute` | added | 4 | TaskExecute[task] evaluates the task's expression once now, synchronously in the current session (in a new local kernel for LocalSubmit tasks), without changing its schedule; the result becomes its EvaluationResult and the TaskObject is returned. Listable. Check: exact (EvaluationResult) in tests. |
| `TaskObject` | added | 3 | TaskObject[<\|"TaskUUID", "TaskEnvironment", "TaskType", "EvaluationExpression" :> expr, ...\|>] represents a task from SessionSubmit or LocalSubmit; task["prop"] gives "TaskStatus" ("Running", "Waiting", "Suspended", "Finished", "Removed"), "EvaluationResult" (Missing until available), "EvaluationExpression" (HoldForm), "TaskUUID", "TaskType", "TaskEnvironment", "EventData", "HandlerFunctions", "HandlerFunctionsKeys", "Properties" and for scheduled tasks "Schedule", "RunInterval", "PreviousRunCount", "RemainingRunCount", "TotalRunCount", "NextScheduledTime". Check: exact in tests. |
| `TaskRemove` | added | 5 | TaskRemove[task] stops a task (aborting a running evaluation and cancelling future scheduled runs), removes it from Tasks[] and gives its TaskObject (its status becomes "Removed"). Listable. Check: exact (Tasks[] afterwards) in tests. |
| `TaskResume` | added | 4 | TaskResume[task] resumes a suspended task (status "Running"; a pending scheduled run waits its full interval again) and gives the TaskObject. Listable. Check: exact (TaskStatus after resuming) in tests. |
| `TaskSuspend` | added | 6 | TaskSuspend[task] suspends a task: no further scheduled runs start until TaskResume (an evaluation already running continues); its status is "Suspended". Gives the TaskObject; finished or removed tasks are left alone. Listable. Check: exact (TaskStatus; no runs while suspended) in tests. |
| `TaskWait` | added | 25 | TaskWait[task] waits until the task (TaskObject or id string) has completely finished (all scheduled runs) and gives its TaskObject; an on-demand (None) task returns at once. Option TimeConstraint -> t returns after at most t seconds. Listable. Check: exact (EvaluationResult after waiting) in tests. |
| `Tasks` | added | 7 | Tasks[] gives the TaskObjects of this session's tasks that have not been removed (running, waiting, suspended or finished), in creation order; Tasks["Session"] / Tasks["Local"] only those of that environment. Check: exact (after SessionSubmit/TaskRemove) in tests. |
| `UnsetShared` | added | 13 | UnsetShared[s1, ...] stops sharing the variables or functions si and gives the list of HoldForm[si] that were shared; UnsetShared[All] stops all sharing. HoldAll. Check: exact ($SharedVariables afterwards) in tests. |
| `WaitAll` | added | 11 | WaitAll[expr] sends all queued ParallelSubmit evaluations to the kernels, waits for the EvaluationObjects in expr (anywhere in it: a list, a sum, ...) to finish, replaces them by their results and evaluates the result; aborted evaluations give $Aborted. Without kernels the queued evaluations run on the master. Check: exact in tests. |
| `WaitNext` | added | 6 | WaitNext[{eo1, eo2, ...}] sends the queued evaluations to the kernels, waits until one of the given EvaluationObjects has finished and gives {result, eo, rest} with the remaining objects (the one that finished first; an already finished one is taken first). Check: exact (all results are collected by repeated WaitNext) in tests. |
| `WithLock` | added | 5 | WithLock[File["path"], expr] (or a path string) evaluates expr while holding an exclusive operating-system lock on the file (created if missing and left in place), so concurrent kernels and processes using the same lock file run expr one at a time; WithLock[{l1, ...}, expr] with symbols uses the master's variable locks like CriticalSection. HoldRest. Check: exact (evaluations serialized) in tests. |

The canonical form TimeSeries[{{t1, v1}, ...}] (sorted) is inert; ts[t] interpolates (first order for numeric values, zero order otherwise, the nearest end value outside the range) and ts["prop"] gives "Path", "NormalPath", "Times", "Values" (a list), "NormalValues", "FirstTime", "LastTime", "FirstValue", "LastValue", "PathLength", "ValueList", "TimeList", "ResamplingMethod", "MinimumTimeIncrement", "Properties"; Normal[ts] is the path. Check: exact; reference in tests. |

Check: exact; reference in tests. |

| `InverseMellinTransform` | added | 3 | InverseMellinTransform[F, s, x] via SymPy (fundamental strip inferred); result checked by transforming back with MellinTransform; unevaluated otherwise |
| `InverseZTransform` | fixed | 17 | InverseZTransform[F, z, n] for rational F (causal, n >= 0, Wolfram convention F(z) = Σ f(n) z^-n): partial fractions in w = 1/z give c/(1 - p w)^k -> c Binomial[n + k - 1, k - 1] p^n and c w^m -> c DiscreteDelta[n - m]; F must stay finite as z -> Infinity (causal sequence). | `ZTransform` | fixed | 5 | Wolfram ZTransform[f, n, z] = Σ_{n=0}^∞ f(n) z^(-n) via symbolic summation (convergence conditions dropped); unevaluated when the sum has no closed form; legacy always returned itself |

| `TreeGame` | added | 29 | TreeGame[{player, action1, ...}] (end nodes {payoff1, ...}; actions annotated action -> label \| prob \| {label, prob}; information sets player -> ilabel) or TreeGame[Tree[<\|"Player" -> p\|>, {...}]] with "Payoffs", "Label", "Probability", "InformationSet" keys: validated (consistent payoff counts, complete probability distributions) and kept as the inert game object TreeGame[spec] |
| `TreeGamePayoff` | added | 14 | TreeGamePayoff[tgame, strat] expected payoff list for a strategy profile <\|player -> <\|node -> {pr, ...}\|>, ...\|> or <\|node -> {pr, ...}, ...\|> (nodes are child-index paths, {} the root); actions with probabilities in the game use them unless the strategy overrides them; TreeGamePayoff[tgame, strat, "RandomExpectation"] averages unspecified nodes uniformly; "Perfect", "PerfectExpectation" and "Random" raise; an incomplete strategy without an adversary type raises |
| `TreeGraph` | added | 4 | TreeGraph[{edges or rules}] / TreeGraph[{vertices}, {edges}] gives the Graph after checking it is a tree (DirectedEdges -> False makes rules undirected); the predecessor-list form and Tree objects raise |
| `TreeInsert` | added | 3 | TreeInsert[tree, child, pos \| {pos1, ...}] inserts child (non-trees become leaves) so that it is at position pos (negative indices count from the end, like Insert); list children only |
| `TreeLayout` | added | 3 | presentation option of Tree (and the tree constructors); kept on the Tree expression and ignored by computations |
| `TreeLeafCount` | added | 3 | number of leaves; Tree[d, {}] has 0 |
| `TreeLeafQ` | added | 5 | True for a leaf Tree[data, None]; False for anything else |
| `TreeLeaves` | added | 3 | the leaves (level -1) in depth-first order |
| `TreeLevel` | added | 11 | TreeLevel[tree, levelspec] subtrees on the levels (children before parents); levelspec -> "Data" \| "Subtree" \| "Position" \| "Level" ...; "Leaves", "NonLeaves"; TreeTraversalOrder option |
| `TreeMap` | added | 23 | TreeMap[f, tree, levelspec -> elem] applies f to the data (or "Subtree", "Position", "Level", "NegativeLevel", "LevelPair", "Children", "ChildrenData", or a list of these as arguments) of the subtrees on the levels (default All); the result becomes the new data |
| `TreeMapAt` | added | 3 | TreeMapAt[f, tree, pos \| {pos1, ...}] applies f to the data at the positions (repeatedly for repeated positions) |
| `TreePosition` | added | 3 | TreePosition[tree, pattern, levelspec, n] positions (children before parents; {} is the root; association children are addressed by Key[k]) |
| `TreeQ` | added | 3 | True for a valid Tree object |
| `TreeReplacePart` | added | 3 | TreeReplacePart[tree, pos -> new \| {pos1 -> new1, ...} \| {pos1, pos2} -> new] replaces subtrees (non-trees become leaves); explicit positions only (no patterns) |
| `TreeRules` | added | 5 | TreeRules[tree]: data -> {rules of children} (or an association); leaves give their data (data -> None when the data itself looks like such a rule) |
| `TreeScan` | added | 3 | TreeScan[f, tree, levelspec -> elem] evaluates f on the data (or elements) of each subtree in traversal order; returns Null |
| `TreeSelect` | added | 3 | TreeSelect[tree, crit], [tree, crit, n], [tree, crit, levelspec, n] subtrees with crit[subtree] True |
| `TreeSize` | added | 24 | number of subtrees (nodes) |
| `TreeTraversalOrder` | added | 6 | option of TreeMap, TreeScan, TreeLevel, TreeCases, TreePosition, TreeSelect: Automatic/"DepthFirst"/"PostOrder"/"BottomUp" (children before parents, default), "PreOrder"/"TopDown", "BreadthFirst"/"LevelOrder" (top-down); other orders raise |
| `UnlabeledTree` | added | 3 | a tree of the same shape with Null as every node's data |

### verification (V1)

| Function | Status | Cases | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Verify` | added | 38 | Verify[expr] evaluates expr and checks the result independently: Integrate by differentiation (or mpmath quadrature for definite integrals), Solve/NSolve by substituting every solution (completeness is not checked), DSolve by substitution, D by numerical differentiation, Limit and Series numerically, FactorInteger and PrimeQ with primality proofs (deterministic Miller-Rabin below 3.3*10^24, Pratt certificates above) or compositeness witnesses, GCD by a Bezout identity, Factor by expansion, Simplify/FullSimplify/Expand/Together/Apart/TrigExpand by equivalence with the input, Inverse and LinearSolve by multiplying back, Det by a second algorithm and Eigenvalues through the characteristic polynomial. It gives Certified[value, info] when an exact certificate was checked, Checked[value, info] when the evidence is symbolic simplification or numerical sampling, and Unchecked[value, reason] when no checker applies; a failed check raises ArithmeticError. MikoshiLang extension. Check: self-check; seeded wrong results are caught in tests. |

## Quarantine decision for the remaining names

The legacy `extended*.py` modules defined about 5,508 further names. 148 of them were reviewed during the audit:

* those with a real Wolfram meaning and a correct implementation were promoted or recorded under their area;
* 6 that the kernel already evaluates correctly (`AtomQ`, `ListQ`, `StringQ`, `ToString`, `ReplaceAll`,
  `Distance2D`) were recorded as kernel heads;
* `YoungTableaux` was briefly quarantined because the legacy version returned the size of a single tableau. It is now properly implemented and promoted (see above).

**Decision for the remaining names: keep them quarantined.** These are the other names on the list in
`mikoshilang/quarantined.json`. They raise
`NotImplementedError: <name> belongs to the quarantined, unreviewed library`.

Sampling during the audit showed why. The great majority are one-line rules that:

* hard-code a placeholder under a broad name. For example, `ANOVAOneWay[...]` always returns `1.0`,
  `AFTModel[...]` returns `{0}`, `ARCH[q]` returns the string `"ARCH(q)"`, and `AGCSignal[x]` is the identity;
* duplicate a reviewed head under a near-synonym.

Promoting any of them requires an actual implementation plus at least 3 differential cases, as with the 26
promoted heads. `tests/library/test_coverage.py::test_every_quarantined_name_raises` calls every remaining
quarantined name and fails if any returns a value.
